markscheme: \(4x-8x=17+13\), or equivalent correct collection of terms.

title: Prime factors and a square number
parts:
Write 720 as a product of its prime factors.
Show your working clearly.
Find the smallest whole number that 720 can be multiplied by to give a square number.
markscheme: For example, \(720=2\times360=2\times2\times180\), continuing a correct factor tree or division ladder.
Note: At least two correct stages in the prime factorisation.
Note: dep on both method marks; inclusion of 1 is condoned.
Note: If not B3 then award B2 for a correct product with one prime exponent wrong, or B1 for at least two correct prime factors.

title: Percentage increase and reverse percentage
parts: Work out the price of the dessert after the increase.

After the increase, the price of lasagne is $9.45.

Work out the price of lasagne before the increase.
markscheme: \(4.25+0.34\), or use \(4.25\times1.08\) for both method marks.
\(9.45\div108\times100\), or use \(9.45\div1.08\) for both method marks.
body:
Lorenzo increases all the prices on his restaurant menu by 8%.

Before the increase, the price of a dessert was $4.25.

title: Area of an isosceles triangle
body:
The diagram shows isosceles triangle \(ABC\). \(AB=AC=7.5\text{ cm}\).
The height of the triangle is 6 cm. Calculate the area of the triangle.
markscheme: Half the base \(=4.5\text{ cm}\), so the base is \(9\text{ cm}\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An isosceles triangle ABC has A at the apex and B and C at the ends of the horizontal base. Both sloping sides AB and AC are labelled 7.5 cm. A perpendicular from A to the base is labelled 6 cm and has a right-angle marker at the base. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Mean after a group leaves
body:
There are 10 people in a lift.
These 10 people have a mean weight of 79.2 kg. 3 of these people get out of the lift.
These 3 people have a mean weight of 68 kg. Work out the mean weight of the 7 people left in the lift.
markscheme: Total weight of all 10 people \(=10\times79.2=792\text{ kg}\), and total weight of the three leaving \(=3\times68=204\text{ kg}\).

title: Index laws
markscheme: Note: B1 for two correct terms as part of a product.
Note: If not B2 then award B1 for any two correct factors in the product.

title: Converting speed units
body:
Change 22 metres per second to a speed in kilometres per hour.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: M2 may be awarded directly for the complete multiplication by 3.6.

title: Ages in a ratio
body:
3 years ago, the ratio of Tom’s age to Clemmie’s age was \(2:7\).
Tom is now 15 years old and Clemmie is now \(x\) years old. Find the value of \(x\).

title: Pressure on cuboid faces
body:
\[\text{pressure}=\dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}\]A box, in the shape of a cuboid, is going to be put on a table. The whole of one face of the box will be in contact with the table.
The force exerted by the box on the table is always 105 newtons. The box is 5 m by 4 m by 3 m. The greatest pressure exerted by the box on the table is \(P\) newtons/m².
The least pressure exerted by the box on the table is \(Q\) newtons/m². Work out the value of \(P-Q\).
markscheme: Calculate a relevant pressure, for example \(105\div(5\times4)=5.25\) or \(105\div(4\times3)=8.75\text{ N/m}^2\).
Note: dep on the previous method mark; if all three pressures are found, use their highest minus their lowest.
Note: oe; dep on both pressure calculations.

title: Venn-diagram regions
parts: On the Venn diagram, shade the set \((A\cup B)'\cap C\).
Use set notation to describe the shaded region in the Venn diagram below.
markscheme: Shade the part of C that is outside both A and B.
Note: Professional judgement is required; allow double shading if the meaning is clear.
Note: Accept equivalent expressions, including \((D\cap F)\cup(E\cap F)\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A universal-set rectangle labelled E contains three overlapping circles: A upper-left, B upper-right and C below. No region is shaded.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. A second universal-set rectangle labelled E contains three overlapping circles: D upper-left, E upper-right and F below. Every part of F that overlaps D or E is shaded, including the central triple overlap.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. In the first diagram, shade only the portion of circle C that lies outside both A and B.

title: Travel and lateness probability
body:
Each day that Barney goes to college, he either goes by bus or he walks.
The probability that Barney will go to college by bus on any day is 0.3. When Barney goes to college by bus, the probability that he will be late is 0.2.
When Barney walks to college, the probability that he will be late is 0.1.
parts:
Barney will go to college on 200 days next year.

Work out an estimate for the number of days Barney will be late for college next year.
markscheme: Complete the probabilities: bus \(0.3\), walk \(0.7\), late and not late after bus \(0.2,0.8\), and late and not late after walking \(0.1,0.9\).
Note: B1 for two, three or four correct probabilities.
Note: ft part (a), where all probabilities are between 0 and 1 inclusive. Accept use of the complementary not-late route.
Note: ft from (a), where probabilities lie between 0 and 1 inclusive.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-stage probability tree first branches to bus and walk, then each branch splits into late and not late. Only the bus probability 0.3 is printed; the remaining five probability labels are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Label the first split bus 0.3 and walk 0.7. After bus, label late 0.2 and not late 0.8. After walk, label late 0.1 and not late 0.9.

title: Equation of a perpendicular line
body:
The straight line \(L_1\) has equation \(2y=6x-5\).
The straight line \(L_2\) is perpendicular to \(L_1\) and passes through the point \((9,-1)\).
Find an equation for \(L_2\).
Give your answer in the form \(ay+bx=c\).

title: Velocity and acceleration
body:
A particle \(P\) is moving along a straight line.
The fixed point \(O\) lies on this line. At time \(t\) seconds, the displacement, \(s\) metres, of \(P\) from \(O\) is given by\[s=4t^3-6t^2+5t\] At time \(t\) seconds, the velocity of \(P\) is \(v\) m/s.
markscheme: Note: At least two terms differentiated correctly.
Note: ft their velocity; dep on differentiation.
parts: Find an expression for \(v\) in terms of \(t\).
Find the time at which the acceleration of the particle is \(6\text{ m/s}^2\).

title: Probability from a histogram
body:
The histogram shows information about the ages of all the passengers travelling on a plane.
No one on the plane is older than 80 years. 24 passengers on the plane are aged between 40 years and 60 years.
markscheme: Use frequency = class width \(\times\) frequency density to obtain frequencies 4, 18, 32, 30, 24 and 16 for the six classes.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A histogram has Age (years) on the horizontal axis with class boundaries 0, 10, 20, 25, 40, 60 and 80. Its six adjoining bars have relative heights 0.4, 1.8, 6.4, 2, 1.2 and 0.8 respectively. The vertical axis is labelled Frequency density but its numerical scale is not printed.
parts: Work out the total number of passengers on the plane.

A passenger on the plane is picked at random.

Work out an estimate for the probability that this person is older than 55 years.

title: Expanding and changing the subject
parts:
Expand and simplify \((x+2)(2x+3)(x-7)\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: First expand two factors, for example \((x+2)(2x+3)=2x^2+7x+6\).
Expand all three brackets in one stage, obtaining at least six of the eight terms correctly.
Note: oe; dep on correct collection of m terms.

title: Arithmetic sequence from term and sum
body:
The 25th term of an arithmetic series is 44.5.
The sum of the first 30 terms of this arithmetic series is 765. Find the 16th term of the arithmetic series.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Solve the simultaneous equations to obtain \(d=2\).
Note: dep on two correct arithmetic-series equations.

title: Fractional powers in standard form
body:
\(a=25\times10^{14n}\) where \(n\) is an integer.
Find an expression, in terms of \(n\), for \(a^{\frac32}\).
Give your answer in standard form.

title: Function transformations and sine parameters
parts:
Write down the coordinates of the maximum point on the curve with equation

(i) \(y=f(x-5)\)

(ii) \(y=3f(x)\).

Here is the graph of \(y=a\sin(bx)^\circ\) for \(0\le x\le360\).

Find the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).
markscheme: Note: Accept the equivalent pair \(a=2,\ b=-3\). B1 for one correct parameter value, including the corresponding sign alternative.
Note: If B2 not awarded, award B1 for one correct parameter including the corresponding sign alternative.
body:
A curve has equation \(y=f(x)\). There is only one maximum point on the curve.
The coordinates of this maximum point are \((4,3)\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Axes run from x = 0 to 360, labelled at 90, 180, 270 and 360, and y = −2 to 2. A sine curve y = a \sin(bx)° starts at the origin and descends, with troughs at (30,−2), (150,−2), (270,−2), peaks at (90,2), (210,2), (330,2), and zeros every 60°.

body:

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: SC for one complete valid solution pair; cao.

title: Angles in a cyclic diagram
body:

\(ABC, AFD, BFE\) and \(CDE\) are straight lines. Work out the size of angle \(x\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Use cyclic and triangle angle facts to obtain \(\angle FDE=x\) and \(\angle AFB=x-54^\circ\), or an equivalent valid pair.
Note: dep on correct cyclic-angle relation; oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Four points B, C, D and F form a cyclic quadrilateral. Straight lines A–B–C and A–F–D meet at A to the left; straight lines B–F–E and C–D–E meet at E below-right. The angle between AB and AF at A is labelled 54°, the angle between EF and ED at E is labelled 32°, and x labels angle CBF at B. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Vectors and ratios on lines
body:
\(\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a\)    \(\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c\)    \(\overrightarrow{AB}=2\mathbf c\) \(P\) is the point on \(AB\) such that \(AP:PB=3:1\).
\(Q\) is the point on \(AC\) such that \(OQP\) is a straight line. Use a vector method to find \(AQ:QC\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: \(\overrightarrow{AC}=\mathbf c-\mathbf a\), and write \(\overrightarrow{OQ}=\mathbf a+n(\mathbf c-\mathbf a)\).
Because O, Q and P are collinear, equate \((1-n)\mathbf a+n\mathbf c\) with a scalar multiple of \(\mathbf a+\dfrac32\mathbf c\).
Note: ft correct vector expressions; dep on matching coefficients.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. O, A and B form a triangle with A and P on the horizontal top side AB and O below-left. C lies to the right of O on a horizontal ray OC. P lies on AB with AP:PB = 3:1. The straight line OP crosses AC at Q. OA is labelled a, OC is labelled c, and AB is labelled 2c. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Bearing using trigonometry
body:
A boat sails from point \(X\) to point \(Y\) and then to point \(Z\). \(Y\) is on a bearing of \(280^\circ\) from \(X\).
\(Z\) is on a bearing of \(220^\circ\) from \(Y\). The distance from \(X\) to \(Y\) is 3.5 km.
The distance from \(Y\) to \(Z\) is 6 km. Work out the bearing of \(Z\) from \(X\).
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

body:

Height of sunflower (\(h\) cm)Frequency
\(90<h\le100\)8
\(100<h\le110\)12
\(110<h\le120\)15
\(120<h\le130\)10
\(130<h\le140\)3
Work out an estimate for the mean height of the sunflowers.
markscheme: Note: M2 for at least four correct midpoint–frequency products added; if not, M1 for consistent representative values in at least four intervals.

Note: If not M2 then award M1 for consistent use of a value within at least four intervals.

body:

Draw the correct perpendicular bisector through the two arc intersections, retaining the arcs.

\(x\in E\) and \(x\notin A\cup B\).

List all the members of set \(C\).

title: Volume of a cylinder
body:
A cylinder has diameter 14 cm and height 20 cm. Work out the volume of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: Accept answers in the range 3077.2 to 3080.

title: Percentage profit and reverse percentage
body:
Josh buys and sells books for a living. He buys 120 books for £4 each.
He sells \(\dfrac12\) of the books for £5 each.
He sells 40% of the books for £7 each.
He sells the rest of the books for £8 each.
parts:
One book that Josh owns had a value of £15 on the 1st May 2019.
The value of this book had increased by 20% in the last year. Find the value of the book on the 1st May 2018.
markscheme: Income from one group, for example \(120\div2\times5=300\), \(120\times0.4\times7=336\), or \((120-60-48)\times8=96\).
Profit on the three groups is \(60+144+48=252\), after first finding the £480 cost.

title: Lengths in similar triangles
body: \(ABC\) and \(DEF\) are similar triangles.
markscheme: Note: ft their DF from part (a) if used consistently.

figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Similarly oriented triangle DEF has DE = 15 cm and EF = 19.5 cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Combined mean for two groups
body:
30 students in a class sat a Mathematics test.
The mean mark in the test for the 30 students was 26.8. 13 of the 30 students in the class are boys.
The mean mark in the test for the boys was 25. Find the mean mark in the test for the girls.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Total class marks \(=30\times26.8=804\), or boys’ total \(=13\times25=325\).
Note: A complete method using the totals or the difference of means is required.
Note: Accept 28.15 to 28.2; accept 28 only from complete working.

title: Algebraic speed conversion
body:
Change a speed of \(x\) kilometres per hour into a speed in metres per second.
Simplify your answer.
markscheme: Multiply by 1000 or divide by 60 as a correct first conversion step.
Note: dep; a complete correct conversion method.

title: Solving simultaneous linear equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[x+2y=-0.5\]\[3x-y=16\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Multiply one equation so matching coefficients can be eliminated, for example \(x+2y=-0.5\) and \(6x-2y=32\), giving \(7x=31.5\).
Substitute \(x=4.5\) into either original equation, or repeat elimination to find y.
Note: dep on the first method mark; ft their first value.
Note: dep on the first method mark; both solutions required.
Substitute an expression for one variable into the other equation, for example \(3(-0.5-2y)-y=16\).
Substitute the resulting value back into an original equation.

title: Straight line and region inequalities
parts:
The region \(R\), shown shaded in the diagram, is bounded by four straight lines.

Write down the inequalities that define \(R\).
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for \(y=5x\), \(y=5x+a\), \(y=bx-3\), or \(5x-3\).
Note: oe double-ended inequalities accept. B1 for two or three correct inequalities. Strict or inclusive signs are accept throughout; SC: award B2 for all four reversed inequalities.

title: Standard form and percentage multipliers
body:
The table gives the average crowd attendance per match for each of five football clubs for one season.
Football clubAverage crowd attendance
Monaco\(9.5\times10^3\)
Chelsea\(4.2\times10^4\)
Juventus\(3.9\times10^4\)
Oxford United\(8.3\times10^3\)
Barcelona\(7.7\times10^4\)
parts:
Find the difference between the average crowd attendance for Barcelona and the average crowd attendance for Monaco.
Give your answer in standard form.

Antonio says, “The average crowd attendance for Chelsea is approximately 50 times that for Oxford United.” Is Antonio correct?
You must give a reason for your answer.

During last season the cost of a ticket to watch Seapron United increased by 15% and then decreased by 8%.

Work out the overall percentage change in the cost of a ticket to watch Seapron United during last season.
markscheme: No; Chelsea is about 5 times Oxford United, not 50 times.
Note: The decision must be supported by correct comparable figures in the same form.
Note: A decrease of 5.8% or −5.8 scores the method mark only.

title: Trapezium perimeter using trigonometry
body:
\(ABCD\) is a trapezium. Calculate the perimeter of the trapezium.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: With E vertically below C on AD, \(ED=\dfrac{16.7}{\tan43^\circ}=17.9085\ldots\), or \(CD=\dfrac{16.7}{\sin43^\circ}=24.4868\ldots\).
Find both \(ED=17.9085\ldots\) and \(CD=24.4868\ldots\), using trigonometry or Pythagoras for the second length.
Note: dep on both previous method marks; use no extra sides.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Trapezium ABCD has horizontal parallel sides BC and AD. AB = 16.7 cm, BC = 21.2 cm, and angle CDA = 43°. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Magnitude of a vector difference
body:
Here are two vectors.\[\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-9\end{pmatrix}\qquad\overrightarrow{CB}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\end{pmatrix}\]

Find the magnitude of \(\overrightarrow{AC}\).
markscheme: \(\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{AB}-\overrightarrow{CB}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-12\end{pmatrix}\), or its negative if using the reverse route.

title: Changing the subject of a radical formula
body: Make \(x\) the subject of the formula \(y=\sqrt{\dfrac{3x-2}{x+1}}\).

title: Rationalising a surd denominator
body:
Show that \(\dfrac{4+\sqrt8}{\sqrt2-1}\) can be written in the form \(a+b\sqrt2\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
Show each stage of your working clearly and give the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).
markscheme: Note: Also accept multiplication by \(-\sqrt2-1\) over itself.
Note: dep on rationalising; at least three numerator terms must be expanded correctly.

title: Direct proportion to a cube
body:
\(y\) is directly proportional to the cube of \(x\).
\(y=20h\) when \(x=h\), where \(h\ne0\).
parts: Find a formula for \(y\) in terms of \(x\) and \(h\).

Find \(x\) in terms of \(h\) when \(y=67.5h\).
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: Note: Full marks also follow from \(y=kx^3\) and \(k=20/h^2\).
Note: ft part (a), dep on at least one method mark there.

title: Maximum surface area of a cuboid
body:
The diagram shows a solid cuboid.

The total surface area of the cuboid is \(A\text{ cm}^2\).

Find the maximum value of \(A\).
markscheme: Area of one face is \(x^2\) or \(x(12-3x)\).
Note: Alternatively, complete the square in a correct quadratic expression for A.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A cuboid has square end dimensions x cm by x cm and length (12 − 3x) cm. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Area of a quadrilateral using trigonometry
body:
\(ABCD\) is a quadrilateral. The area of triangle \(ACD\) is \(250\text{ cm}^2\). Calculate the area of the quadrilateral \(ABCD\).
Show your working clearly.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: By the sine rule in triangle ABC, \(\dfrac{AB}{\sin47^\circ}=\dfrac{30.5579\ldots}{\sin95^\circ}\), or an oe equation for BC.
Note: dep on the area-formula method; ft their AC.
Note: dep on the previous method marks.
Total area \(=250+\dfrac12(30.5579\ldots)(22.4340\ldots)\sin38^\circ=461.03\ldots\text{ cm}^2\), or the oe calculation using BC and angle 47°.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Quadrilateral ABCD is split by diagonal AC. AD = 26 cm, angle DAC = 39°, angle ABC = 95°, and angle BCA = 47°. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Line and quadratic-curve intersections
body:
The equation of the line \(L\) is \(y=9-x\).
The equation of the curve \(C\) is \(x^2-3xy+2y^2=0\). \(L\) and \(C\) intersect at two points. Find the coordinates of these two points.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Factorise or otherwise solve the quadratic, for example \((2x-9)(x-6)=0\).
Note: dep on the substitution method; a complete method for their three-term quadratic is required.
Note: dep on the substitution method; pairs must be matched correctly.

title: Angle between a line and a plane
body:
The diagram shows cuboid \(ABCDEFGH\). For this cuboid the length of \(AB\) : the length of \(BC\) : the length of \(CF=4:2:3\). Calculate the size of the angle between \(AF\) and the plane \(ABCD\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Let the proportional lengths be \(4x,2x,3x\). Then \(AC=\sqrt{(4x)^2+(2x)^2}=\sqrt{20}x\), or \(AF=\sqrt{29}x\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A cuboid ABCDEFGH is drawn obliquely. ABCD is one rectangular face and F is vertically above C. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Simplifying an algebraic fraction
body: Simplify fully \(\dfrac{6x^3+13x^2-5x}{4x^2-25}\).
markscheme: Factorise either polynomial with the common factor visible: numerator \(=x(2x+5)(3x-1)\), or denominator \(=(2x+5)(2x-5)\).
Note: Both numerator and denominator must be correctly factorised.
Note: Accept \(\dfrac{3x^2-x}{2x-5}\). Do not ignore subsequent working.

title: Reverse probability without replacement
body:
Boris has a bag that only contains red sweets and green sweets. Boris takes at random 2 sweets from the bag.
The probability that Boris takes exactly 1 red sweet from the bag is \(\dfrac{12}{35}\).
Originally there were 3 red sweets in the bag. Work out how many green sweets there were originally in the bag.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Let t be the total number of sweets. One ordered mixed-colour probability is \(\dfrac3t\times\dfrac{t-3}{t-1}\).
Note: dep on the first method mark; the oe sum of RG and GR is accept.
Note: dep on the quadratic accuracy mark.
Valid total \(t=15\), so the number of green sweets is \(15-3=12\).
Note: dep on the quadratic accuracy mark; cao.
Let x be the number of green sweets. One ordered mixed-colour probability is \(\dfrac3{x+3}\times\dfrac{x}{x+2}\).

title: Finding an inverse quadratic function
body: The function \(f\) is such that \(f(x)=3x-2\).
parts:
The function \(g\) is such that \(g(x)=2x^2-20x+9\), where \(x>5\).

Express the inverse function \(g^{-1}\) in the form \(g^{-1}(x)=\ldots\)
markscheme: Note: dep on the first method mark.
Note: The positive branch is required because the original domain is x ≥ 5. Allow candidates to swap x and y during inversion.
After swapping x and y, form \(2y^2-20y+(9-x)=0\).
Apply the quadratic formula to y.

title: Reading and solving inequalities
parts: Write down the inequality shown on the number line.
markscheme: \(4y-y\le8+13\), or oe collection of the y-terms and numbers on opposite sides.
Note: Allow any inequality sign, or equality, at this method stage.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A number line has an open circle at −3 and a ray extending to the right with an arrow.

title: Subtracting mixed numbers
body:
Show that \(5\dfrac23-2\dfrac34=2\dfrac{11}{12}\).
Show each stage of your working clearly.

title: Plotting a quadratic graph
body:
The table gives some values of \(x\) and \(y\), where \(y=1+5x-x^2\).
\(x\)−10123456
\(y\)1771
parts: On the grid, draw the graph of \(y=1+5x-x^2\) for values of \(x\) from −1 to 6.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for two or three correct values.
Note: If B2 not awarded, award B1 for six or seven correct table values.
Plot at least six points correctly, following through a table earning at least B1.
Draw the fully correct smooth downward-opening curve.
Note: Do not accept a horizontal line at the top of the curve or straight line segments.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank coordinate grid spanning x = −2 to 7 and y = −6 to 8 at unit intervals, with labelled axes and origin. The table of values is printed in the question text, not in the figure.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot and join smoothly (−1,−5), (0,1), (1,5), (2,7), (3,7), (4,5), (5,1), and (6,−5), forming a downward parabola with a rounded maximum midway between x = 2 and x = 3.

title: Similar triangles and area units
body: \(ABC\) and \(DEF\) are similar triangles.
parts:
The area of triangle \(DEF\) is \(525\text{ cm}^2\).

Find the area of triangle \(DEF\) in \(\text{m}^2\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Triangle ABC has AB = 12 cm and BC = 16 cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Similarly oriented triangle DEF has EF = 40 cm. Matching angle marks correspond with triangle ABC. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Factorising a quadratic
body: Factorise \(x^2-5x-36\).
markscheme: Find integer factors with product −36 and sum −5, giving the form \((x+a)(x+b)\).
Note: Ignore any extension to the roots.

title: Probability from a table
body:
There are some ice lollies in a freezer.
Each ice lolly is one of four flavours: banana, strawberry, mint or chocolate.
The table gives the probability that an ice lolly taken at random is banana, strawberry or chocolate.
FlavourBananaStrawberryChocolate
Probability0.350.320.12
Julius takes at random an ice lolly from the freezer. Work out the probability that the flavour of the ice lolly that Julius takes is either strawberry or mint.
markscheme: Note: dep on the first method mark.

title: Scaling a three-part ratio
body:
A football team played 55 games.
The ratio of the number of games the team won to the number of games the team drew to the number of games the team lost was \(6:3:2\).
Work out how many more games the team won than the team lost.
markscheme: Note: Alternatively, M2 for explicitly finding 30 wins and 10 losses.

title: HCF and LCM from prime powers
body: \(A=3^2\times5^4\times7\)    \(B=3^4\times5^3\times7\times11\)
parts: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of \(A\) and \(B\).
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of \(A\) and \(B\).

title: Standard form calculations
parts:
Work out \((6\times10^7)\div(8\times10^{-2})\).
Give your answer in standard form.
markscheme: \(60000000\div0.08=750000000\), or oe separate coefficient and exponent calculation.

title: Compound depreciation
body:
Henri buys a yacht for 150 000 euros.
The value of the yacht depreciates by 18% each year.
Work out the value of the yacht at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest euro.
markscheme: Note: If not M2, M1 for a correct first-year step such as \(150000\times0.82=123000\) or depreciation \(150000\times0.18=27000\).
Note: Accept 82705.2 before rounding. Printed special cases award B1 for specified incorrect multiplier methods.

title: Equation from a straight-line graph
body:
Line \(L\) is drawn on the grid.

Find an equation for \(L\).
markscheme: Gradient \(=\dfrac{-4}{2}=-2\), using two points on the line.
Note: Award B1 for a correct gradient or a correct intercept.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A straight descending line on a grid from x = −4 to 3 and y = −4 to 4 passes through (−2,3), (−1,1), (0,−1), and (1,−3).

title: Length through two right triangles
body:
The diagram shows points \(A\) and \(B\).
Calculate the length of \(AB\).
Show your working clearly.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: In right triangle ABD, \(\cos42^\circ=\dfrac{BD}{AB}\), or use the sine rule with angles 90° and 48°.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A and C lie on a horizontal line with D between them. B is above D and BD is perpendicular to AC. BC is labelled 3.1 m, angle BCD is 32 degrees, and angle ABD is 42 degrees. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Cumulative frequency and probability
body:
Sandeep recorded the length of time, in minutes, that each of 100 adults went for a walk one day. The table gives information about these times.
Time (\(t\) minutes)Cumulative frequency
\(30<t\le40\)6
\(30<t\le50\)20
\(30<t\le60\)56
\(30<t\le70\)84
\(30<t\le80\)95
\(30<t\le90\)100
parts: On the grid, draw a cumulative frequency graph for the information in the table.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the median length of time.

One of the adults is chosen at random.

Use your graph to find an estimate for the probability that this adult went for a walk for more than 72 minutes.
markscheme: Plot at least five of \((40,6),(50,20),(60,56),(70,84),(80,95),(90,100)\) correctly at the interval ends.
Join the plotted points with a cumulative-frequency curve or line segments.
Note: The graph need not be joined to (30,0); consistently placed points within intervals at the correct heights are accept.
Use cumulative frequency 50 and read the corresponding time from the graph.
Read cumulative frequency 86, 87 or 88 at 72 minutes.
Number walking more than 72 minutes \(=100-86\), \(100-87\), or \(100-88\).
Note: dep on the graph reading; ft their graph.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank cumulative-frequency grid has time from 30 to 90 minutes horizontally and cumulative frequency from 0 to 100 vertically.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (40,6), (50,20), (60,56), (70,84), (80,95), and (90,100), then join with a smooth increasing curve or line segments.

title: Fractional and algebraic indices
parts: Given that \(3^n=\dfrac{3^x}{9^y}\), find \(n\) in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
markscheme: Note: B1 for each correct factor; also allow B1 if \((x^3y^2)^3\) or \((x^{36}y^{24})^{1/4}\) is seen.

title: Circle theorem reasoning
body:
\(A, B, C\) and \(D\) are points on a circle, centre \(O\). \(AOC\) is a diameter of the circle. Angle \(AOD=98^\circ\). Work out the size of angle \(DBC\).
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
markscheme: \(\angle ABD=98^\circ\div2=49^\circ\), because the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
\(\angle ABC=90^\circ\), because an angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
Note: dep on the first method mark.
Note: dep on the first method mark; a correct associated reason is required.
Note: A correct answer with no reasons scores M1A1.
\(\angle AOD\) leaves \(180^\circ-98^\circ=82^\circ\) on the straight diameter.
In isosceles triangle AOD, the base angle is \(82^\circ\div2=41^\circ\).
Angles subtended by chord DC in the same segment are equal.
\(\angle DOC=180^\circ-98^\circ=82^\circ\), since angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle has horizontal diameter AC through centre O, with A at left and C at right. B lies on the upper arc and D on the lower-right arc. Chords BD and BC are drawn, and radii OA and OD form a central angle of 98 degrees. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Inverse square proportion
body:
The following table gives values of \(x\) and \(y\), where \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x\).
\(x\)1.5234
\(y\)16942.25
parts: Find a formula for \(y\) in terms of \(x\).
Given that \(x>0\), find the value of \(x\) when \(y=144\).
markscheme: Note: cao; the positive root is required.

title: Algebraic proof for a sequence
body:
The table gives information about the first six terms of a sequence of numbers.
Position123456
Term\(\dfrac{1\times2}{2}\)\(\dfrac{2\times3}{2}\)\(\dfrac{3\times4}{2}\)\(\dfrac{4\times5}{2}\)\(\dfrac{5\times6}{2}\)\(\dfrac{6\times7}{2}\)
Prove algebraically that the sum of any two consecutive terms of this sequence is always a square number.
markscheme: Term n is \(\dfrac12n(n+1)\), or term \(n+1\) is \(\dfrac12(n+1)(n+2)\).
Note: dep on all three method marks.
Note: SC: award B1 for a valid algebraic expression for two consecutive terms.

title: Functions and gradient estimation
body: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined as\[f(x)=\dfrac{x}{4x-3}\qquad g(x)=x-5\]
parts: State the value that must be excluded from any domain of \(f\).
Express the inverse function \(f^{-1}\) in the form \(f^{-1}(x)=\ldots\)

Part of the curve with equation \(y=h(x)\) is shown on the grid. Find an estimate for the gradient of the curve at the point where \(x=-0.5\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Let \(y=\dfrac{x}{4x-3}\), or swap x and y. Then \(y(4x-3)=x\).
Draw a tangent to the curve at \(x=-0.5\).
Use two points on the tangent to calculate rise ÷ run, for example \(18\div3\).
Note: dep on the tangent mark. SC: B1B1 for a tangent at x = +0.5 and gradient from −3 to −4.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A smooth curve y = h(x) is shown for approximately −2 ≤ x ≤ 3 on a grid. It rises steeply from near (−2,−10), crosses the x-axis near −1.7, reaches a broad maximum near (0.1,16), then falls through about (1,12) and (2,6) to a shallow minimum near (2.8,4.5). No tangent is printed.

title: Perimeter of a circular segment
body:
The diagram shows a sector \(OAPB\) of a circle, centre \(O\). Angle \(AOB=80^\circ\).
The area of the sector is \(\dfrac{25}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
\(AB\) is a chord of the circle. Work out the perimeter of the shaded segment.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: dep on both length-method marks; awrt 20.1.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two radii OA and OB form an 80-degree sector with minor arc APB above chord AB. The circular segment between chord AB and arc APB is shaded. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Upper bound of a rational expression
body:
\[x=\dfrac{6a}{b-a}\]\(a=3.46\), correct to 3 significant figures.
\(b=6.3\), correct to 1 decimal place. Work out the upper bound for the value of \(x\).
Give your answer as a decimal correct to 3 significant figures.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: dep on both correct bounds. The admissible ranges are \(3.46<a_{UB}\le3.465\) and \(6.25\le b_{LB}<6.3\).

title: Volume of similar bottles
body:
The diagram shows two similar bottles, \(A\) and \(B\).
The surface area of bottle \(A\) is \(240\text{ cm}^2\).
The surface area of bottle \(B\) is \(540\text{ cm}^2\).
The volume of bottle \(B\) is \(2025\text{ cm}^3\).
Work out the volume of bottle \(A\).
markscheme: Linear scale factor B to A \(=\sqrt{240/540}=\dfrac23\), or its reciprocal used consistently.
Note: Accept 0.66 or better for the linear factor in a complete method.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two outline bottles of the same shape are shown, with bottle A smaller and bottle B larger. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Completing the square
body: Write \(5+12x-2x^2\) in the form \(a+b(x+c)^2\), where \(a, b\) and \(c\) are integers.
markscheme: Note: Full marks if a = 23, b = −2 and c = −3 are correctly stated. Printed special cases: B3 for \(23-2(3-x)^2\); B2 for a correct square term plus an unspecified constant; B1 for \(-2(x+3)^2+\text{constant}\).

title: Angle between a pyramid edge and its base
body:
The diagram shows a solid pyramid \(ABCDE\) with a horizontal base. The base \(BCDE\) is a square of side 10 cm. The vertex \(A\) is vertically above the centre \(O\) of the base.
The sloping edges \(AB, AC, AD\) and \(AE\) are equal in length.
The total surface area of the pyramid is \(360\text{ cm}^2\). Work out the size of the angle between \(AC\) and the base \(BCDE\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: \(360=10(10)+4\left(\dfrac12\times10\times h\right)\), where h is a triangular face’s perpendicular height.
Find relevant lengths, for example \(AC=\sqrt{13^2+5^2}=\sqrt{194}=13.93\ldots\) and \(AO=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12\text{ cm}\).
Note: Alternatively use \(OC=5\sqrt2=7.07\ldots\). M2 for two accurate relevant sides, or M1 for one.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Pyramid ABCDE has square horizontal base BCDE, with front edge BC labelled 10 cm. Apex A is vertically above centre O; dotted AO is vertical. Hidden base edges BE and ED and hidden sloping edge AE are dashed. Solid edges AB, AC, AD, BC and CD are shown. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Reverse probability with marbles
body:
A box contains marbles. 4 of the marbles are red.
The rest of the marbles are yellow. Judy takes at random a marble from the box and does not replace it.
Sam then takes at random a marble from the box.
The probability that Judy and Sam both take a yellow marble is 0.7.
Work out how many marbles were originally in the box.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Let x be the total. Then \(\dfrac{x-4}{x}\times\dfrac{x-5}{x-1}=0.7\).
Note: If not M2, M1 for either correct factor \((x-4)/x\) or \((x-5)/(x-1)\).
Note: Rearrange their equation to a three-term quadratic.
\((3x-8)(x-25)=0\), or use the quadratic formula or completing the square.
Note: A correct first step in solving the quadratic.
Note: dep on the algebraic method marks; accept 25 only.
Let y be the yellow count. Then \(\dfrac{y}{y+4}\times\dfrac{y-1}{y+3}=0.7\).
\((3y+4)(y-21)=0\), or an oe complete solving method.
Note: Full marks also follow from verifying \(\dfrac{21}{25}\times20/24=0.7\) after earning the first M2. SC B1 for beginning to solve an incorrect three-term quadratic.

title: Coordinates and a straight line
body:
The point \(A\) has coordinates \((5,-4)\).
The point \(B\) has coordinates \((13,1)\).
parts: Work out the coordinates of the midpoint of \(AB\).

Line \(L\) has equation \(y=2-3x\).

Write down the gradient of line \(L\).

Line \(L\) has equation \(y=2-3x\). Does the point with coordinates \((100,-302)\) lie on line \(L\)?
You must give a reason for your answer.
markscheme: No, because when x = 100 the line has y = 2 − 300 = −298, not −302.
Note: oe valid numerical reasons are accept.

title: Lowest common multiple
body: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 28 and 105.
markscheme: Note: Accept four listed multiples of each number, a fully correct Venn diagram, or \(28\times105\div7\).
Note: If not M2 then award M1 for at least two correct multiples or prime factors.

title: Area of a compound shape
body:
The diagram shows a shape.

The shape has area \(129\text{ cm}^2\).

Work out the value of \(x\).
markscheme: Area of the left rectangle \(=12\times9=108\text{ cm}^2\), or area of the right extension \(=(9-6)x=3x\).
Note: dep on the first area method; ft their relevant area.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An L-shaped rectilinear polygon has left vertical side 9 cm, top horizontal side 12 cm, then a vertical drop of 6 cm, followed by a rightward horizontal step labelled x cm. The outer bottom edge returns to the left side. Right-angle markers appear at each corner. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Grouped baby weights
body:
The table shows information about the weights, in kilograms, of 40 babies.
Weight (\(w\) kg)Frequency
\(2<w\le3\)12
\(3<w\le4\)16
\(4<w\le5\)9
\(5<w\le6\)2
\(6<w\le7\)1
parts: Work out an estimate for the mean weight of the 40 babies.

One of the 40 babies is going to be chosen at random.

Find the probability that this baby has a weight of more than 5 kg.
markscheme: Note: M2 for at least four correct products added; if not, M1 for consistent representatives in at least four intervals.
Note: dep on at least one preceding method mark; division by their total frequency is allowed.
Note: Accept a probability \(a/40\), where \(0<a<40\), or \(3/b\), where integer \(b>3\), for the method mark.

title: Ratio and fractional groups
body:
120 children go on an activity holiday.
The ratio of the number of girls to the number of boys is \(3:5\). On Sunday, all the children either go sailing or go climbing. \(\dfrac{16}{25}\) of the boys go climbing.
Twice as many girls go sailing as go climbing. Work out how many children go sailing on Sunday.
markscheme: Note: M2 may be awarded directly for 45 girls or 75 boys.

title: Standard form calculations
parts:
Work out \(\dfrac{5.6\times10^4+7\times10^3}{2.8\times10^{-3}}\).

Give your answer in standard form.

title: Algebraic manipulation and equation solving
markscheme: Note: Any three correct terms, or all four ignoring signs; an accept partially collected form also scores.
Note: If not B2, B1 for any valid partial factorisation.
Note: ft, dep on a four-term equation. Accept a correct separated-fraction route.
Note: dep on at least two method marks.

title: Fractional enlargement
body: On the grid, enlarge the shaded shape with scale factor \(\dfrac12\) and centre \((1,2)\).
markscheme: Image vertices are \((6,3),(8,3),(8,6),(4,6)\), joined as the corresponding trapezium.
Note: If not B2, B1 for the correct size and orientation or for three or four correctly plotted image points.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. On a coordinate grid from x = 0 to 16 and y = 0 to 11, a shaded trapezium has vertices (7,10), (15,10), (15,4), and (11,4). Its sloping side joins (11,4) to (7,10). The centre (1,2) is not specially marked.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw the image trapezium with vertices (4,6), (8,6), (8,3), and (6,3), joining them in corresponding order.

title: Right-triangle length
body:
Here is a right-angled triangle. Calculate the length of \(PQ\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: Alternative M2 route: find \(RQ=24.3\tan63^\circ\), then use Pythagoras with 24.3.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Right-angled triangle PQR has P at upper-left, R at lower-left and Q at lower-right. PR is vertical and labelled 24.3 cm. Angle RPQ at P is labelled 63°, and R has a right-angle marker. The text “Diagram NOT accurately drawn” is printed.

title: Region defined by inequalities
body:
The shaded region in the diagram is bounded by three lines.
The equation of one of the lines is given. Write down the three inequalities that define the shaded region.
markscheme: Note: B3 for all three, B2 for two, B1 for one. Strict signs are accept. SC: B3 for all three reversed inequalities; if otherwise no marks, B1 for recognising x + y = 4.
Note: Award B1 for two correct inequalities.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A shaded triangular region is bounded by solid lines x = −1, x + y = 4, and y = x/3 − 2. Its vertices are approximately (−1,5), (−1,−2.33), and (4.5,−0.5). The equation y = x/3 − 2 is printed beside the lower sloping boundary.

title: Changing compound interest rate
body:
Max invests $6000 in a savings account for 3 years.
The account pays compound interest at a rate of 1.5% per year for the first 2 years. The compound interest rate changes for the third year.
At the end of 3 years, there is a total of $6311.16 in the account. Work out the compound interest rate for the third year.
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
markscheme: Amount after two years \(=6000\times1.015^2=6181.35\), or find the corresponding two-year multiplier.
Note: dep on the first method mark; oe calculations using total multipliers or interest differences are accept.

title: Cumulative frequency and group size
body:
A total of 80 men and women took part in a race.
The cumulative frequency graph gives information about the times, in minutes, they took for the race.
parts: Use the graph to find an estimate for the interquartile range.

60% of the men took 50 minutes or less for the race.
No women took 50 minutes or less for the race. Work out an estimate for the number of men who took part in the race.
markscheme: Read approximately 38 minutes at cumulative frequency 20 and 56 minutes at cumulative frequency 60, then subtract.
Read cumulative frequency from 40.5 to 43 at 50 minutes; this is the number of men finishing within 50 minutes.
Estimated total men \(=42\div0.6\), following through their graph reading.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A cumulative-frequency graph runs from (20,0), rises through approximately (30,8), (40,23), (50,42), (55,58), (60,69), and ends at (70,80). Horizontal axis is time 20–70 minutes; vertical axis is cumulative frequency 0–80.

title: Cube volume from pressure
body:
The diagram shows a solid cube.
The cube is placed on a table so that the whole of one face of the cube is in contact with the table. The cube exerts a force of 56 newtons on the table.
The pressure on the table due to the cube is \(0.14\text{ newtons/cm}^2\).\[\text{pressure}=\dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}\] Work out the volume of the cube.
markscheme: Note: dep on both previous method marks.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique cube is labelled w cm along three mutually perpendicular edges. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Parallelogram area and diagonal
body:
The diagram shows parallelogram \(EFGH\). \(EF=9.3\text{ cm}\).
\(FG=14.7\text{ cm}\).
Angle \(EFG=106^\circ\).
parts:
Work out the area of the parallelogram.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Work out the length of the diagonal \(EG\) of the parallelogram.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: oe methods via a perpendicular height or twice a triangle area are accept.
Note: dep on the cosine-rule method; correct order of operations.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Parallelogram EFGH has E lower-left, F upper-left, G upper-right and H lower-right. EF is labelled 9.3 cm, FG is labelled 14.7 cm, and the interior angle at F is 106 degrees. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Maximum cuboid volume
body: The diagram shows a cuboid of volume \(V\text{ cm}^3\).
parts:
There is a value of \(x\) for which the volume of the cuboid is a maximum. Find this value of \(x\).
Show your working clearly.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Expand a pair of factors correctly, for example \((2x+5)(x+1)=2x^2+7x+5\).
Multiply by the third factor, obtaining at least three of the six terms correctly, for example \((2x^2+7x+5)(3-x)\).
\(\dfrac{dV}{dx}=16-2x-6x^2\), with at least two terms differentiated correctly.
Note: dep on the differentiation method mark.
Note: dep on the differentiation method; reject the negative root as physically invalid.
Note: dep on the differentiation method; accept 1.47 to 1.5 from correct working.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique cuboid has front bottom length (2x + 5) cm, vertical height (x + 1) cm, and depth (3 − x) cm. Hidden rear and left-bottom edges are dashed. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Upper bound of a formula
body:
\[P=\dfrac{2a-c}{d}\]\(a=58.4\), correct to 3 significant figures.
\(c=20\), correct to 2 significant figures.
\(d=3.6\), correct to 2 significant figures. Work out the upper bound for the value of \(P\).
Show your working clearly.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
markscheme: Use a correct bound, ultimately \(a_{UB}=58.45\), \(c_{LB}=19.5\), and \(d_{LB}=3.55\).
Note: Use \((2a_{UB}-c_{LB})/d_{LB}\) with the stated admissible bound ranges.

title: Surds and fractional indices
parts:
Show that \((6+2\sqrt{12})^2=12(7+4\sqrt3)\).

Show each stage of your working.
markscheme: Note: oe use of \((a+b)^2\), or showing \(\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt3\), is accept.
Note: dep on the first method mark.
Apply one of cube-rooting, inverting or squaring, for example \(\left(\dfrac{3a^4}{t^5}\right)^{-2}\).
After two operations, obtain for example \(\left(\dfrac{t^5}{3a^4}\right)^2\).

title: Probability that a category remains
body:
There are 16 sweets in a bowl. 4 of the sweets are blackcurrant.
5 of the sweets are lemon.
7 of the sweets are orange. Anna, Ravi and Sam each take at random one sweet from the bowl. Work out the probability that the 5 lemon sweets are still in the bowl.
markscheme: Note: If not M3: M1 for one correct three-sweet category product; M2 for that plus a second relevant ordered category, or another valid partial-event method.
Note: oe exact or decimal answers accept.

Including all three orders of each mixed selection, \(P(BBO)=3\times\dfrac4{16}\times\dfrac3{15}\times\dfrac7{14}=\dfrac{252}{3360}\) and \(P(BOO)=3\times\dfrac4{16}\times\dfrac7{15}\times\dfrac6{14}=\dfrac{504}{3360}\).
Note: An oe complement calculation subtracting all cases containing at least one lemon from 1 is also accept.

title: Angle between a cuboid diagonal and a plane
body:
The diagram shows a cuboid \(ABCDEFGH\). \(EH=9\text{ cm}\), \(HG=5\text{ cm}\) and \(GB=6\text{ cm}\). Work out the size of the angle between \(AH\) and the plane \(EFGH\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Use a correct ratio, for example \(\sin\angle AHF=\dfrac6{\sqrt{142}}\) or \(\tan\angle AHF=\dfrac6{\sqrt{106}}\).
Note: A complete oe cosine-rule or complementary-angle method is accept.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique cuboid has bottom face EFGH and corresponding top vertices D, A, B, C. Bottom front edge EH is 9 cm, bottom right depth HG is 5 cm, and vertical edge GB is 6 cm. Hidden edges AF, FG and EF are dashed. Segment AH is not drawn. Label the diagram not accurately drawn.

title: Sketching a parameterised quadratic
body:
The curve \(C\) has equation \(y=4(x-1)^2-a\), where \(a>4\). Using the axes below, sketch the curve \(C\).
On your sketch show clearly, in terms of \(a\), (i) the coordinates of any points of intersection of \(C\) with the coordinate axes, (ii) the coordinates of the turning point.
markscheme: Draw an upward-opening quadratic curve with a minimum.
Draw the fully correct curve: minimum in the fourth quadrant, negative y-intercept, and one x-intercept on each side of the y-axis, all correctly labelled.
Note: SC: award B1 for a correctly shaped upward-opening parabola.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Blank unscaled coordinate axes are provided.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw an upward-opening parabola with vertical axis of symmetry x = 1 and minimum (1,−a) below the x-axis. Label the y-intercept (0,4−a), the negative x-axis intercept (1−√a/2,0), and the positive x-axis intercept (1+√a/2,0).

title: Inverse of a composite quadratic
body:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are such that\[f(x)=x^2-2x\qquad g(x)=x+3\]

The function \(h\) is such that \(h(x)=fg(x)\) for \(x\ge-2\).

Express the inverse function \(h^{-1}(x)\) in the form \(h^{-1}(x)=\ldots\)
markscheme: Note: ft, dep on the composition method. Accept a correct quadratic-equation route.
Note: dep on the first two method stages; the positive square-root branch is required.

title: Isosceles triangle with coordinate constraints
body:
Triangle \(HJK\) is isosceles with \(HJ=HK\) and \(JK=\sqrt{80}\).
\(H\) is the point with coordinates \((-4,1)\).
\(J\) is the point with coordinates \((j,15)\), where \(j<0\).
\(K\) is the point with coordinates \((6,k)\). \(M\) is the midpoint of \(JK\).
The gradient of \(HM\) is 2. Find the value of \(j\) and the value of \(k\).
markscheme: Because HM is the perpendicular bisector of JK, gradient JK \(=-\dfrac12\).
Note: dep on the first three method marks. Alternative methods use JK² = 80 or equal distances HJ = HK, producing a quadratic.

title: Sharing money in a ratio
body: Brendon, Asha and Julie share some money in the ratios 3 : 2 : 6. The total amount of money that Asha and Julie receive is $36. Work out the amount of money that Brendon receives.
markscheme: Note: An answer of \(\dfrac{27}{2}\) earns this method mark. SC: B1 for \(36\div5\times7\ (=43.2)\) or \(36\div9\times2\ (=8)\). [Printed as it appears in the Edexcel mark scheme: \(36\div5\times7\) is 50.4, not 43.2.]

title: Multiplying mixed numbers
body:
Show that \(3\dfrac15\times2\dfrac58=8\dfrac25\).
Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: Both fractions must be expressed as improper fractions.
\(\dfrac{16}{5}\times\dfrac{21}{8}=\dfrac{336}{40}\), with correct cancelling or multiplication of numerators and denominators.
Note: dep on both method marks. The result of the multiplication or correct cancelling before multiplication must be seen. Use of decimals scores no marks.

title: Algebraic manipulation
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for \(3(3ef-4f)\), \(f(9e-12)\), \(3f(ke-4)\), or \(3f(3e-m)\), where the bracket contains two terms and the outside factor is valid.
Note: If not B2 then award B1 for a valid partial factorisation.
Note: Accept any three correct terms, all four correct terms ignoring signs, \(x^2-3x+\cdots\), or \(\cdots-3x-10\).
\(n^{11}\div n^5\), \(n^{-1}\times n^7\), \(n^4\times n^2\), or another correct simplification of two terms.

title: Sets and intersections
parts: List all the members of (i) \(B\cup G\), (ii) \(W\cap G^\prime\).
Serena writes \(B\cap G\cap W=\varnothing\). Is Serena’s statement correct? Give a reason.
markscheme: No, because \(e\) is in all three sets; equivalently \(B\cap G\cap W=\{e\}\).

title: Semicircular garden area
body:
The diagram shows Yuen’s garden. The garden is in the shape of a semicircle with radius 7.2 m.
Yuen has 12 boxes of grass seed. Each box covers an area of 6 m².
Has Yuen got enough grass seed for his garden? Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Boxes needed \(=81.4\ldots\div6=13.5\ldots\), or available coverage \(=12\times6=72\text{ m}^2\), or area per box required \(=81.4\ldots\div12=6.7\ldots\text{ m}^2\).
Note: dep on the area mark. The calculation 12 × 6 alone earns no marks.
No, with the correct comparative figures.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A semicircle is drawn with a horizontal diameter along the bottom and the curved edge above it. A radius from the midpoint of the diameter to the right endpoint is labelled 7.2 m. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Solving a quadratic equation
body: Solve \(x^2-5x-36=0\). Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Begin with \((x\pm9)(x\pm4)\), or \((x+a)(x+b)\) where \(ab=-36\) or \(a+b=-5\); alternatively substitute correctly into the quadratic formula.
Note: The accuracy mark is dep on at least one method mark.

title: Reverse percentage
body: In a sale, the normal price of a hat is reduced by 15%. The sale price is 20.40 euros. Work out the normal price.
markscheme: Note: If not M2, M1 for \(20.40\div(100-15)=0.24\), or another valid partial method.

title: Combined means
body: Five children on a trampoline have mean weight 28 kg. Two get off and their mean weight is 26.5 kg. Work out the mean weight of the three children who remain.

title: Gold blocks and density
body:
Pablo made a solid gold statue. The statue has a mass of 5.73 kg.
He melted down some identical gold blocks to make the statue.
The gold blocks are cuboids of length 8 cm, width 2 cm and height 1.5 cm.
The density of gold is \(19.32\text{ g/cm}^3\). Work out the least number of gold blocks Pablo melted down in order to make the statue.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Volume of statue \(=\dfrac{5.73\times1000}{19.32}=296.58\ldots\text{ cm}^3\), or mass of one block \(=19.32\times24=463.68\text{ g}\).
Note: If not M2, M1 for correct use of density, such as \(V=\dfrac{5.73\times1000}{19.32}\) or \(M=19.32\times24\). Work may be in grams or kilograms.
Note: cao; the least whole number is required.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A long thin cuboid drawn in oblique projection, receding to the upper right. The long receding edge is labelled 8 cm on a dimension arrow; the front face is 2 cm across, on a dimension arrow below it, and 1.5 cm high, on a dimension arrow to its left. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Equal perimeters
body:
The diagram shows a regular hexagon, \(ABCDEF\), and an isosceles triangle, \(GHJ\). The perimeter of the hexagon is equal to the perimeter of the triangle. Find the length of each side of the hexagon.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: dep on at least one perimeter method mark.
Note: dep on the preceding equation and correct expansions.
Note: oe; dep on both perimeter method marks.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A regular hexagon ABCDEF is drawn with a horizontal top and bottom; the bottom side AB is labelled (x − 1) cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Separately, an isosceles triangle GHJ is drawn with horizontal base GH and vertex J below. Equal sloping sides GJ and HJ are each labelled (x + 5) cm by a single label on the right side; base GH is labelled (2x − 3) cm.

title: Bounds of measurements
body: The weight of a cat is \(4.3\text{ kg}\), correct to 2 significant figures. Also, \(G=e-f\), where \(e=17\) correct to the nearest integer and \(f=9.4\) correct to one decimal place.
parts: Write down the upper bound of the weight of the cat.
Write down the lower bound of the weight of the cat.
Work out the upper bound for the value of \(G\).

title: Comparing waiting times
body: The cumulative frequency graph gives information about the waiting times, in minutes, of people with appointments at Hospital A.
parts: Use the graph to find an estimate of the median waiting time at Hospital A.
Use the graph to find an estimate of the interquartile range of the waiting times at Hospital A.
At Hospital B the median is 28 minutes and the interquartile range is 19 minutes. Compare the waiting times at Hospitals A and B.
markscheme: Upper quartile \(\approx29\), lower quartile \(\approx17\), so calculate \(29-17\).
Hospital A has the lower median, so people generally wait less time at Hospital A.
Note: ft the median read in part (a).
Hospital A has the lower interquartile range, so its waiting times are more consistent or less spread out.
Note: ft part (b). To award both marks, at least one comparison must be in context.
Note: Award B1 for a correct median read from the graph.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A cumulative-frequency graph has waiting time from 0 to 50 minutes on the horizontal axis and cumulative frequency from 0 to 60 on the vertical axis. A smooth increasing curve starts near (4,0), passes approximately through (12,5), (17,15), (23,30), (29,45), (35,55), and levels near (43,60). Major grid intervals are 10 units and minor intervals are 1 unit.

title: Recurring decimals and rationalising surds
parts: Given that \(y\) is a prime number, express \(\dfrac3{2-\sqrt y}\) in the form \(\dfrac{a+b\sqrt y}{c-y}\), where \(a,b,c\) are integers.
markscheme: Let \(x=0.57272\ldots\) and write \(100x=57.27272\ldots\), or write \(10x=5.7272\ldots\) and \(1000x=572.72\ldots\), with the intention to subtract.
Note: Award for multiplying by the conjugate, or a correct numerator or denominator.

title: Angles in a circle
body:
\(A, B\) and \(C\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\).
Angle \(ABC=38^\circ\). Work out the size of angle \(OAC\).
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
markscheme: \(\angle AOC=38^\circ\times2=76^\circ\), because the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
Reasons: angles in a triangle add to \(180^\circ\), and base angles in isosceles triangle AOC are equal because \(OA=OC\).
Note: The reason marks are dep on the method mark. If not B2, award B1 for one correct relevant circle theorem.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle has centre O. Points A at lower-left, B at upper-left and C at upper-right lie on the circumference. Chords AB and BC are drawn. Radii OA and OC form central angle AOC. Angle ABC is marked 38 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Linked right triangles
body:
The diagram shows two right-angled triangles, \(DEF\) and \(EFG\). Work out the length of \(EG\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: \(EF=12\cos40^\circ=9.19\ldots\), or \(FD=12\sin40^\circ\) followed by Pythagoras to find EF.
Note: If not M2, M1 for a correct relation involving EF, such as \(\cos40^\circ=\dfrac{EF}{12}\).
Note: dep on M2. Alternatively find \(FG\) using sine, then use Pythagoras.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two right-angled triangles share the vertical side EF. In triangle DEF, D is lower-left, F lower-right and E directly above F. DE is the hypotenuse and is labelled 12 cm; angle DEF at E is 40 degrees; angle DFE at F has a right-angle marker. In triangle EFG, E is upper-left, F lower-left and G upper-right. EG is horizontal, FG is the hypotenuse, angle FEG at E has a right-angle marker, and angle EGF at G is 28 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Independent game outcomes
body: Steffi plays one game of tennis and one game of chess. The probability she wins tennis is 0.6 and the probability she wins both games is 0.42. Work out the probability that she will not win either game.
markscheme: Note: A complete oe complement calculation is accept.

title: Functions and composition
body: The function f is \(f(x)=(x-4)^2\) for all values of \(x\). The function g is \(g(x)=\dfrac4{x+3}\), \(x\ne-3\).
parts: State the range of the function f.

title: Gradient, tangent and graph intersections
body: The diagram shows \(y=f(x)\) for \(-4\le x\le12\). Point P on the curve has \(x\)-coordinate 2.
parts: (i) Use the graph to estimate the gradient at P. (ii) Hence find the tangent equation in the form y = mx + c.
The equation \(f(x)=k\) has exactly two different solutions for \(-4\le x\le12\). Use the graph to find the two possible values of \(k\).
markscheme: Draw a tangent at P, where \(x=2\).
Use \(\dfrac{\text{difference in y-values}}{\text{difference in x-values}}\) on the tangent.
Note: dep on the tangent mark; accept −0.4 to −0.7 from correct figures for the candidate’s line.
Note: ft their gradient and tangent intercept, provided the intercept is greater than 3.
Note: SC: award B1 for a correct tangent drawn at P.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A smooth cubic-like curve is drawn on a square grid for x from −4 to 12 and y from −2 to 4. It begins near (−4,−1), crosses the x-axis near −3.5, reaches a local maximum at about (0,3), passes through P at about (2,2.4), crosses again near x = 5.4, reaches a local minimum at about (8,−1), crosses near x = 10, and ends near (12,3). P is plotted and labelled. No tangent is drawn.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Add a straight tangent through P at x = 2 with gradient about −0.6; a representative accepted tangent has equation y = −0.6x + 3.6.

title: Histogram with an unknown scale
body:
The histogram shows information about the heights of all the students in Year 11 at a school.
There are 160 students with a height between 155 cm and 170 cm. Work out the total number of students in Year 11 at the school.
markscheme: Calibrate the scale, for example \(5(2x)+10x=160\), or use an oe bar-area or grid-square method.
Note: Accept finding 400 small squares in total, 10 students per 1 cm², or an oe scale.
\(x=8\), giving the appropriate frequency-density scale; equivalently obtain 0.4 students per small square.
Note: A method to find the frequency of another bar also earns this mark: first 108, fourth 90, fifth 12.
Note: dep on at least one earlier method mark; allow one error or repeat but no omission.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A histogram has height (cm) on the horizontal axis from 140 to 190, labelled every 10 cm, and frequency density on the vertical axis. The vertical scale is deliberately unnumbered apart from 0. Five adjoining bars cover 140–155, 155–160, 160–170, 170–185 and 185–190. In equal small-grid units their heights are respectively 18, 40, 20, 15 and 6.

title: Frustum and sphere volumes
body:
The diagram shows a frustum of a cone and a sphere.
The frustum is formed by removing a small cone from a similar large cone. The small cone has height \(h\) cm and the large cone has height \(2h\) cm. The large cone and the sphere each have radius \(r\) cm.
The volume of the frustum is equal to the volume of the sphere. Find \(r\) in terms of \(h\).
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: Similarity gives the small-cone radius \(\dfrac r2\). Find either cone volume: \(V_L=\dfrac13\pi r^2(2h)=\dfrac23\pi r^2h\), or \(V_S=\dfrac13\pi\left(\dfrac r2\right)^2h=\dfrac1{12}\pi r^2h\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A frustum is drawn with the removed small cone shown above it by dotted sloping sides. A vertical double arrow from the apex to the cut plane is labelled h cm. A second vertical double arrow beside the entire original large cone, from apex level to base level, is labelled 2h cm. A horizontal double arrow marking the large base radius is labelled r cm. Dashed rear arcs show the circular rims. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Separately, a sphere is drawn with a horizontal great circle shown solid in front and dashed behind. A radius from the centre to the left edge is labelled r cm.

title: Prism cross-section length
body:
The diagram shows the prism \(ABCDEF\) with cross section triangle \(ABC\).
Angle \(BEC=40^\circ\), angle \(ACB\) is obtuse, \(AC=6\text{ cm}\), \(CE=13\text{ cm}\), and the area of triangle \(ABC\) is \(22\text{ cm}^2\).
Calculate the length of \(AB\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique triangular prism ABCDEF is shown. Triangle ABC is the front cross-section with A lower-left, B lower-right and C upper-left. Corresponding rear vertices are F, E and D. Solid edges include AB, AC, BC, BE, CD, DE and CE; hidden edges AF, FD and FE are dashed. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Cosine graph and function transformations
parts: The graph of \(y=a\cos(x+b)^\circ\) for \(0\le x\le360\) is shown. Find a and b.
Curve C has equation \(y=f(x)\) and minimum point \((4,5)\). Write the minimum point of (i) \(y=f(2x)\), (ii) \(y=f(x)-7\).
markscheme: One correct parameter value from the graph.
Note: oe representation \(a=-2.5,\ b=120\) is accept. SC: M1 for drawing an appropriate cosine curve.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A cosine curve is drawn on a square grid for 0 ≤ x ≤ 360 and −3 ≤ y ≤ 3. It starts at about (0,1.25), reaches a maximum (60,2.5), crosses the x-axis at 150, reaches a minimum (240,−2.5), crosses again at 330 and ends near (360,1.25). The x-axis is labelled every 60 degrees and the y-axis every 1 unit.

title: Velocity from displacement
body: A particle moves along a straight line. Its displacement from O at time \(t\ge0\) is \(s=t^3+4t^2-5t+7\) metres. At time T seconds its velocity is V m/s, where \(V\ge-5\). Find T in terms of \(V\) in the form \(\dfrac{-4+\sqrt{k+mV}}3\).
markscheme: Note: Award for two of the three terms differentiated correctly.
Complete the square or apply the quadratic formula, for example \(T=\dfrac{-8\pm\sqrt{8^2-4(3)(-5-V)}}6\).
Note: Condone one sign error in a, b or c and ft a quadratic with an error in a or b; condone + in place of ±.
Note: This line implies the preceding method mark.
Note: Choose the positive square-root branch because \(T\ge0\). Thus \(k=31\) and \(m=3\).

title: Index laws
parts: Write \(\dfrac{7^8\times7^4}{7^3}\) as a single power of 7.
markscheme: \(7^8\times7^4=7^{12}\), or \(7^8\div7^3=7^5\), or another correct step written as a power of 7.

title: Converting cubic units
body:
Change \(32.4\text{ m}^3\) into \(\text{cm}^3\).
Show your working clearly.

title: Adding mixed numbers
body:
Show that \(4\dfrac23+3\dfrac45=8\dfrac7{15}\).
Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: \(4\dfrac23=\dfrac{14}{3}\) and \(3\dfrac45=\dfrac{19}{5}\), or write the fractional parts over a common denominator.
Note: dep on both method marks; an oe proof evaluating both sides to \(\dfrac{127}{15}\) is accept.

title: Angles in a triangle
body:
The diagram shows a triangle.
The angles are \(30^\circ\), \((4x+10)^\circ\) and \((x+20)^\circ\).
Work out the value of \(x\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A triangle is drawn with its top angle labelled 30 degrees, bottom-left angle labelled (4x + 10) degrees and bottom-right angle labelled (x + 20) degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Constructing an angle bisector
body: Use ruler and compasses to construct the bisector of angle BAC. You must show all your construction lines.
markscheme: Construct equal-radius arcs from A to meet both arms, then equal-radius intersecting arcs from those two points.
Draw the straight angle bisector from A through the intersection of the second pair of arcs.
Note: B2 for a fully correct bisector with all relevant arcs. B1 for all arcs without the bisector, or a correct bisector within guidelines but missing or insufficient arcs.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two rays AB and AC meet at A, forming an acute angle opening to the right. B lies on the upper ray and C on the lower ray. No construction arcs or bisector are printed.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Preserve rays AB and AC. Show an arc centred at A crossing both rays, then two equal-radius arcs centred at those crossing points intersecting inside the angle. Draw the angle-bisector ray from A through that intersection.

title: Estimating frequency from probabilities
body:
A bag contains only red beads, blue beads, green beads and yellow beads. The table gives the probabilities that, when a bead is taken at random from the bag, the bead will be blue or yellow.
Colourredbluegreenyellow
Probability0.240.31
The probability that the bead will be green is twice the probability that the bead will be red.
Sofia takes at random a bead from the bag, writes down its colour and puts the bead back. She does this 180 times.
Work out an estimate for the number of times she takes a red bead from the bag.
markscheme: Note: oe expected-frequency route: 99 blue/yellow outcomes, leaving 81 red/green outcomes.
Note: An answer of \(\dfrac{27}{180}\) earns this method mark.
Note: If not M2 then award M1 for a correct equation connecting the four probabilities.

title: Inequality and quadratic equation
markscheme: Begin with \((x\pm8)(x\pm5)\), or \((x+a)(x+b)\) where \(ab=-40\) or \(a+b=-3\); alternatively substitute correctly into the quadratic formula.
Note: The accuracy mark is dep on at least one method mark.

title: Percentage comparisons and discount
body:
The table shows the cost, in euros, of Brigitte’s car insurance in each of the years 2016, 2017 and 2018.
Year201620172018
Cost of insurance (euros)500545592
Brigitte says, “The percentage increase from 2017 to 2018 is more than the percentage increase from 2016 to 2017.”
parts: Brigitte says the percentage increase from 2017 to 2018 is more than from 2016 to 2017. Is she correct? Show how you get your answer.
Henri pays 952 euros after a 15% discount. Work out the discount.
markscheme: Note: If not M3, M2 for one of the two correct expressions.

title: Mass from density
body:
The density of gold is \(19.3\text{ g/cm}^3\).
A gold bar has volume \(150\text{ cm}^3\). Work out the mass of the gold bar.

title: Speed unit conversion
body:
Change a speed of 50 metres per second to a speed in kilometres per hour.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Use at least one correct factor: \(50\times60\), \(50\div1000\), \(50\times60\times60\), or \(\dfrac{60\times60}{1000}=3.6\).
Note: dep on the first method mark. SC: B1 for both correct conversion factors applied in the wrong direction.

title: Semicircle and triangle perimeter
body:
The diagram shows a shaded shape \(ABCD\) made from a semicircle \(ABC\) and a right-angled triangle \(ACD\). \(AC\) is the diameter of the semicircle. \(AD=17\text{ cm}\) and \(CD=15\text{ cm}\). Work out the perimeter of the shaded shape.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: dep on both preceding method marks.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A right triangle ACD has A upper-left, C lower-left and D lower-right, with a right-angle marker at C. AD is labelled 17 cm and CD 15 cm. The semicircle with diameter AC bulges to the left through point B. The triangle interior and semicircle interior form one shaded shape. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Oil price comparison
body:
Astrid wants to buy some oil. She can buy it from Dane Oil or Arctic Oil.
Dane Oil offers \(4.2\times10^5\) litres for 2 500 000 Krone. Arctic Oil offers \(8.6\times10^5\) litres for 770 000 Dollars.
\(1\) Dollar \(=6.57\) Krone.
From which company should she buy her oil to get the better value for money?
You must show your working.
markscheme: Convert to the same currency: Arctic \(1.1168\ldots\div6.57=0.1699\ldots\) litres per Krone, or Dane \(0.168\times6.57=1.10376\) litres per dollar.
Arctic Oil, with the relevant comparative figures.
Convert the quoted prices: \(2500000\div6.57=380517.5\ldots\) dollars, or \(770000\times6.57=5058900\) Krone.
Dane gives \(0.168\) litres per Krone or \(1.103\ldots\) litres per dollar.
Arctic gives \(1.1168\ldots\) litres per dollar or \(0.1699\ldots\) litres per Krone.
Arctic Oil, with the relevant comparative figures.
Convert: Dane \(5.952\ldots\div6.57=0.9059\ldots\) dollars per litre, or Arctic \(0.895\ldots\times6.57=5.882\ldots\) Krone per litre.
Arctic Oil, with the relevant comparative figures.
oe amount from Dane costs \(2.0476\ldots\times2500000=5119047.6\ldots\) Krone; or oe amount from Arctic costs \(770000\div2.0476\ldots=376046.5\ldots\) dollars.
Convert so the costs are comparable: Dane \(=779154.9\ldots\) dollars versus Arctic 770000 dollars, or Arctic \(=2470625.6\ldots\) Krone versus Dane 2500000 Krone.
Arctic Oil, with the relevant comparative figures.
First convert a quoted price: \(2500000\div6.57=380517.5\ldots\) dollars, or \(770000\times6.57=5058900\) Krone.
Dane cost per litre \(=\dfrac{2500000}{4.2\times10^5}=5.952\ldots\) Krone, or \(\dfrac{380517.5\ldots}{4.2\times10^5}=0.9059\ldots\) dollars.
Arctic cost per litre \(=\dfrac{770000}{8.6\times10^5}=0.895\ldots\) dollars, or \(\dfrac{5058900}{8.6\times10^5}=5.882\ldots\) Krone.
Arctic Oil, with the relevant comparative figures.

title: Circle theorem angle
body:
\(A,B,C\) and \(D\) are points on a circle, centre \(O\).
\(AOD\) is a diameter. Angle \(CBD=28^\circ\) and angle \(BDA=32^\circ\).
Find the size of angle \(BDC\).
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
markscheme: For example, \(\angle CAD=28^\circ\) because angles subtended by chord CD at the circumference are equal; also \(\angle ACD=90^\circ\) because it is the angle in a semicircle.
Give all reasons relevant to the chosen method, including a correct circle theorem and the angle sum of a triangle.

Note: dep on the method mark. If not B2, B1 for one correct relevant circle-theorem reason. Other valid routes include same-segment, cyclic-quadrilateral, isosceles-triangle and centre-angle arguments.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle has A at lower-left, B at upper-left, C at upper-right and D at lower-right on its circumference; O lies on diameter AD. Chords AC, BC, CD, DA and BD are drawn. Angle CBD at B is marked 28 degrees and angle BDA between DB and DA is marked 32 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Probability tree without replacement
body: There are 13 large and 7 small glasses. Roberto takes two glasses at random without replacement.
parts: Work out the probability that Roberto takes two small glasses.
markscheme: After large: \(\dfrac{12}{19}\) large and \(\dfrac7{19}\) small; after small: \(\dfrac{13}{19}\) large and \(\dfrac6{19}\) small.
Note: Accept the stated decimal equivalents to at least 2 decimal places.
Note: Award B1 for at least three correct probabilities on the tree.
Note: ft probabilities less than 1 from part (a).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An incomplete two-stage probability tree has first-stage branches labelled large and small, each with a dotted probability blank. Each then splits into large and small, with four dotted probability blanks.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill the first branches with 13/20 for large and 7/20 for small. From the first large branch fill 12/19 then 7/19; from the first small branch fill 13/19 then 6/19.

title: Recognising graph shapes
body:
Here are six graphs.
Complete the table below with the letter of the graph that could represent each given equation.
Write your answers on the dotted lines.
EquationGraph
\(y=\dfrac2{x^2}\)............................
\(y=-\dfrac12x^3\)............................
\(y=-\dfrac5x\)............................
markscheme: Note: B3 for all three, B2 for two, B1 for one.
Note: SC: award B1 for one correct graph match.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. One bordered 3-by-2 panel of six labelled sketch graphs, Graph A to Graph F, as the page prints them. A has reciprocal branches in quadrants I and III; B is a decreasing cubic through the origin, quadrant II to quadrant IV; C has two positive reciprocal-square branches above the x-axis; D has two negative reciprocal-square branches below it; E has reciprocal branches in quadrants II and IV; F is an increasing cubic through the origin, quadrant III to quadrant I.

title: Changing the subject with a square root
body:
Make \(x\) the subject of \(y=\sqrt{\dfrac{x+1}{x-4}}\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: oe form \(\dfrac{-4y^2-1}{1-y^2}\) accept; \(x=\) must be shown.

title: Algebraic proof with consecutive squares
body:
Prove that the difference between two consecutive square numbers is always an odd number.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Let the consecutive squares be \(n^2\) and \((n-1)^2\), or \((n+1)^2\) and \(n^2\).
\(2n-1\) or \(2n+1\) is always odd, so the result is proved.
Note: dep on both method marks. SC: B1 for comparing \((2n)^2\) with \((2n-1)^2\), or \((2n+1)^2\) with \((2n)^2\).

title: Histogram proportions and conditional probability
parts: Work out an estimate for the proportion of these customers who spent between 17 minutes and 35 minutes in the supermarket.
Given that a selected customer spent more than 30 minutes, find the probability that the customer spent more than 36 minutes.
markscheme: Note: oe small-square method gives 1200 squares. Allow one error in the total-area method; all correct bar values not added also earn the mark.
Area above 36 \(=4.8\times9=43.2\), and area above 30 \(=4.8\times15=72\), so form \(\dfrac{43.2}{72}\).
Note: Accept oe unsimplified ratios such as \(\dfrac9{15}\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A histogram has time 0–50 minutes on the horizontal axis and frequency density 0–5 on the vertical axis. Five adjacent bars cover 0–10 at height 0.7, 10–15 at 3.4, 15–24 at 1.0, 24–30 at 2.5, and 30–45 at 4.8. There is no bar from 45 to 50. Major gridlines are every 10 minutes and 1 density unit, with fine subdivisions.
body: The histogram gives information about the times, in minutes, that some customers spent in a supermarket.

title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
parts: Write an equation of a line parallel to \(y=7-4x\).
Line L passes through \((-3,1)\) and \((2,-2)\). Find the equation of the line perpendicular to L through \((-6,4)\), in the form \(ax+by+c=0\).
markscheme: Note: For example \(y=-4x\); an oe form is accept.
Note: ft and dep on the perpendicular-gradient mark.
Note: oe integer forms such as \(10x-6y+84=0\) or \(3y=5x+42\) are accept.

title: Rectangle width with surds
body:
The area of a rectangle is \(18\text{ cm}^2\). The length is \((\sqrt7+1)\text{ cm}\).

Without using a calculator and showing each stage of your working, find the width.

Give your answer in the form \(a\sqrt b+c\), where \(a,b\) and \(c\) are integers.
markscheme: Note: dep on the conjugate method; the numerator and denominator must be multiplied correctly.

title: Transformations of functions and curves
body:
The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation \(y=f(x)\).

There is one maximum point on this curve. The coordinates of this maximum point are \((4,6)\).
parts:
Write down the coordinates of the maximum point on the curve with equation

(i) \(y=f(x+4)\)

(ii) \(y=f(2x)\).
Curve C is \(y=x^2+3x+4\). It is translated by vector \(\begin{pmatrix}4\\6\end{pmatrix}\) to curve S. Find an equation of S; simplification is not required.
markscheme: Apply one translation, for example replace \(x\) by \(x-4\), or write \(y-6=x^2+3x+4\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A sketch of a downward-opening curve y = f(x) is shown on unscaled axes. It has a single maximum marked and labelled (4,6), lies to the right of the y-axis at the maximum, and crosses the x-axis once on each side of the maximum.

title: Line and circle intersections
body:
The line with equation \(y=x+2\) intersects the curve with equation \(x^2+y^2-2y=24\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Find the coordinates of \(A\) and \(B\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: \((x+4)(x-3)=0\), or solve the quadratic by a correct formula or completing-square method.
Note: dep on the substitution mark; ft their quadratic, allowing the stated tolerance for a sign error.
Note: Both coordinate pairs; dep on the substitution method mark.
\((y-5)(y+2)=0\), or solve the quadratic by a correct formula or completing-square method.

title: Ratio on a median using vectors
body:
\(ABC\) is a triangle. The midpoint of \(BC\) is \(M\). \(P\) is a point on \(AM\).
\(\overrightarrow{AB}=4\mathbf a\), \(\overrightarrow{AC}=2\mathbf b\), and \(\overrightarrow{AP}=\dfrac32\mathbf a+\dfrac34\mathbf b\).
