Find the ratio \(AP:PM\).
markscheme: \(\overrightarrow{AM}=\dfrac12(4\mathbf a+2\mathbf b)=2\mathbf a+\mathbf b\), so \(\overrightarrow{PM}=\overrightarrow{AM}-\overrightarrow{AP}=\dfrac12\mathbf a+\dfrac14\mathbf b\).

Note: oe; links include \(AP:AM=3:4\), \(AM:PM=4:1\), \(\overrightarrow{AM}=\dfrac43\overrightarrow{AP}\), or \(\overrightarrow{AM}=4\overrightarrow{PM}\), with vectors in the form \(p\mathbf a+q\mathbf b\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Triangle ABC has A at the left, B upper-right and C lower-right. M is marked as the midpoint of vertical-ish side BC. Segment AM is drawn, with P marked between A and M. Arrow AB is labelled 4a and arrow AC is labelled 2b; the printed question body gives the vector AP. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Algebraic fractions
body:
Express \(\left(\dfrac4{2x-5}-\dfrac3{2x-3}\right)\div\dfrac{9x-4x^3}{6x^2-17x+5}\) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: Award for complete factorisation of the numerator or denominator of the second fraction.
Note: oe forms include \(\dfrac{1-3x}{x(2x-3)^2}\); isw an incorrect denominator expansion after a correct factorised answer.

title: Arithmetic series saving plan
body:
Mario is going to save $50 in the year 2021.
He will continue to save, up to and including 2070, by increasing the amount he saves each year by $\(k\).
Mario will save a total of $33 125 from 2021 to 2070. Work out the value of \(k\).
markscheme: Note: For this method mark, allow n = 49.

title: Sector forming a cone
body:
Here is a sector, \(AOB\), of a circle with centre \(O\) and angle \(AOB=x^\circ\). The sector can form the curved surface of a cone by joining \(OA\) to \(OB\).
The height of the cone is 25 cm and its volume is \(1600\text{ cm}^3\).
Work out the value of \(x\).
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
The sector is marked “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
The cone is marked “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
markscheme: Sector radius, equal to cone slant height, \(l=\sqrt{7.8176^2+25^2}=26.193\ldots\text{ cm}\).
Note: dep on both preceding method marks.
\(49.1196\ldots=\dfrac{x}{360}\times2\pi(26.193\ldots)\), or equate the curved area to \(\dfrac{x}{360}\pi(26.193\ldots)^2\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A sector AOB has centre O at the top, straight radii OA and OB sloping down-left and down-right, and a circular arc AB below. The central angle AOB is marked x degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Separately, a cone is shown with apex O and circular base; the front base arc is solid and rear arc dashed. A dotted vertical height from O to the base centre has a downward arrow and is labelled 25 cm. The joined seam points A and B coincide at the right edge of the base and are labelled A B. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Powers and prime factors
parts: Write \(5^{17}\times5^2\) as a single power of 5.
Write 800 as a product of its prime factors. Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Use a factor tree or division ladder containing at least three factors other than 1, multiplying to 800 and including 2 and 5.
Note: Condone one error when the product is not 800.

title: Estimated total from grouped data
body:
The table gives information about the amount of money, in £, that Fiona spent in a grocery store in each of the 52 weeks of 2019.
Amount spent (£\(x\))Frequency
\(0\le x<20\)5
\(20\le x<40\)11
\(40\le x<60\)8
\(60\le x<80\)19
\(80\le x<100\)9
Work out an estimate for the total amount of money that Fiona spent in the grocery store in 2019.
markscheme: Note: M2 for correct midpoint products, allowing one error, with intention to add. If not M2, M1 for frequency products using consistent values within each interval, allowing one error, with intention to add; or midpoint products without addition.
Note: If not M2 then award M1 for at least four correct class midpoint products; oe.

title: Buttons in three tins
body:
Three tins, \(A, B\) and \(C\), each contain buttons. Tin \(A\) contains \(x\) buttons.
Tin \(B\) contains four times as many buttons as tin \(A\).
Tin \(C\) contains 7 fewer buttons than tin \(A\).
There are 137 buttons in total.
Work out the number of buttons in tin \(C\).
markscheme: Tin B contains \(4x\), or tin C contains \(x-7\).

title: Rectangle diagonal
body:
The diagram shows a rectangle and a diagonal of the rectangle.
The rectangle has side lengths 8.5 cm and 5.6 cm.
Work out the length of the diagonal.
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A horizontal rectangle has one vertical side labelled 5.6 cm and one horizontal side labelled 8.5 cm. A diagonal joins opposite corners. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Average speed
body:
A plane takes 3 hours 36 minutes to fly from the Cayman Islands to New York.
The distance is 2470 km.
Work out the average speed of the plane in km/h.
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

title: Constructing a perpendicular bisector
body:
Use ruler and compasses only to construct the perpendicular bisector of the line \(AB\).
You must show all your construction lines.
markscheme: Draw equal-radius arcs centred at A and B, with radius greater than half AB, so corresponding arcs intersect on both sides of AB.
Draw the straight line through the two arc intersections; this is the perpendicular bisector.

Note: B2 for a fully correct bisector with all arcs. B1 for all correct arcs without the bisector, or a correct bisector within the guidelines but without arcs. Correct arcs may lie on the same side of AB.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A horizontal line segment has endpoint A at the left and B at the right. No arcs, midpoint or perpendicular line are printed.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Preserve segment AB. Draw equal-radius compass arcs centred at A and B so that they intersect above and below AB, and draw the straight line through the two intersections. Keep all arcs visible.

title: Solving simultaneous equations
body: Solve the simultaneous equations\[3x+5y=6\]\[7x-5y=-11\]Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Add the equations to eliminate y: \(10x=-5\); equivalently scale equations correctly to eliminate x and obtain \(50y=75\), or use correct substitution.
Note: Both accuracy marks are dep on the method mark.

title: Compound depreciation
body:
Hamish buys a new car for $20 000.
The value of the car depreciates by 19% each year.
Work out the value of the car at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

title: Pressure on a rectangular face
body:
The diagram shows a box in the shape of a cuboid.
The box rests on a rectangular face of length 1.2 m and width \(x\) m.
The box exerts a force of 27 newtons on the floor. The pressure is \(30\text{ N/m}^2\).\[\text{pressure}=\dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}\]Work out the value of \(x\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique cuboid is shown resting on a rectangular base. One base edge is labelled 1.2 m and the perpendicular base edge is labelled x m. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Ocean areas in standard form
body:
The table shows information about the surface area of each of the world’s oceans.
OceanSurface area (square kilometres)
Pacific\(1.56\times10^8\)
Indian\(6.86\times10^7\)
Southern\(2.03\times10^7\)
Arctic\(1.41\times10^7\)
Atlantic\(1.06\times10^8\)
parts:
Work out the difference, in square kilometres, between the surface area of the Atlantic Ocean and the Indian Ocean.
Give your answer in standard form.
The Pacific is k times the Arctic. Find \(k\) to the nearest whole number.

title: Inequalities and a shaded region
parts: Write the three inequalities defining the shaded region R.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for including −2 as well, or for omitting 4 only.
Note: B2 for all three and B1 for two. SC: B2 for all three reversed. Strict signs are accept.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. On unscaled x-y axes, a shaded triangular region R is bounded above by the horizontal line y = 6, below-left by x + y = 5, and below-right by y = x − 3. All boundaries are solid and labelled.

title: Regular polygons and isosceles triangles
body:
The diagram shows two congruent isosceles triangles and parts of two congruent regular polygons, \(X\) and \(Y\).
Each triangle has two angles of \(66^\circ\). Each polygon has \(n\) sides.
Work out the value of \(n\).
markscheme: Polygon interior angle \(=\dfrac{360^\circ-48^\circ}{2}=156^\circ\), so exterior angle \(=180^\circ-156^\circ=24^\circ\).
Note: oe route: exterior angle \(=\dfrac12(48^\circ)=24^\circ\). Another accept route equates \(\dfrac{180(n-2)}n=156\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two congruent isosceles triangles point horizontally towards each other, the left one with apex B on the right and the right one with apex E on the left, B and E joined by a short horizontal segment, between partial outlines of two congruent regular polygons labelled X above and Y below. The four triangle base angles are each marked 66 degrees. Points A, B, C form the left triangle and D, E, F the right triangle, with the polygon edges meeting at the triangle vertices. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Trapezoidal prism volume
body:
The diagram shows prism \(ABCDEFGH\), with trapezium \(ABCD\) as its cross section.
\(BC\parallel AD\), \(BC=7\text{ cm}\), \(AD=12\text{ cm}\), the perpendicular height is \(h\) cm and \(DE=10\text{ cm}\).
The volume of the prism is \(608\text{ cm}^3\). Work out the value of \(h\).
markscheme: Note: If not M2, M1 for \(\dfrac h2(7+12)\times10\) without equating it to 608.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique prism has front cross-section trapezium ABCD with parallel horizontal sides BC = 7 cm and AD = 12 cm, separated by perpendicular height h cm. The prism extends to the rear by edge DE = 10 cm, with corresponding rear vertices EFGH. Hidden edges are dashed. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Interquartile range from raw data
body:
Max kept a record of the marks he scored in each of the 11 spelling tests he took one term.\[18,\ 5,\ 7,\ 12,\ 11,\ 18,\ 15,\ 16,\ 17,\ 13,\ 14\]

Find the interquartile range of the marks.

title: Table and graph of a quadratic
body:
The table gives some values of \(x\) and \(y\), where \(y=x^2-\dfrac{x}{2}-3\).
\(x\)−3−2−10123
\(y\)7.5−2.54.5
parts: Complete the table of values for \(y=x^2-\dfrac{x}{2}-3\).
On the grid, draw the graph of \(y=x^2-\dfrac{x}{2}-3\) for values of \(x\) from −3 to 3.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for two or three correct values.
Note: Award B1 for at least four correct table values.
Plot at least five points correctly, following through the table.
Note: dep on at least B1 in part (a).
Draw the correct smooth upward-opening curve through the plotted points.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Complete the table by placing 2 under x = −2, −1.5 under x = −1, −3 under x = 0, and 0 under x = 2.
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (−3,7.5), (−2,2), (−1,−1.5), (0,−3), (1,−2.5), (2,0), and (3,4.5), then draw a smooth upward-opening parabola through them.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank square coordinate grid has x from −3 to 3 and y from −4 to 8, with axes and integer labels. No points or curve are printed.

title: Counter probability tree
body:
Cody has two bags of counters, bag A and bag B.
Each of the counters has either an odd number or an even number written on it. There are 10 counters in bag A and 7 of these counters have an odd number written on them.
There are 12 counters in bag B and 7 of these counters have an odd number written on them. Cody is going to take at random a counter from bag A and a counter from bag B.
parts: Calculate the probability that the total of the numbers on the two counters will be an odd number.

Harriet also has a bag of counters.
Each of her counters also has either an odd number or an even number written on it. Harriet is going to take at random a counter from her bag of counters. The probability that the number on each of Cody’s two counters and the number on Harriet’s counter will all be even is \(\dfrac3{100}\) Find the least number of counters that Harriet has in her bag.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Complete with \(\dfrac3{10},\dfrac7{12},\dfrac5{12},\dfrac7{12},\dfrac5{12}\), in the corresponding branches.
Note: If not B2, B1 for \(\dfrac3{10}\), or B1 for all four correct Bag B probabilities. Decimal equivalents to 2 d.p. are accept.
Note: SC: award B1 for at least three correct probabilities on the tree.
Odd then even: \(\dfrac7{10}\times\dfrac5{12}\), or even then odd: \(\dfrac3{10}\times\dfrac7{12}\).
\(\dfrac3{10}\times\dfrac5{12}\times p=\dfrac3{100}\), where p is Harriet’s even-counter probability.
Note: dep on the first method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-stage probability tree starts with Bag A branches odd and even; the odd branch is labelled 7/10 and the even probability is blank. Each then splits into Bag B odd and even branches, all four probabilities blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill the Bag A even branch with 3/10. From each Bag A outcome, fill Bag B odd with 7/12 and Bag B even with 5/12.

title: Three-set Venn diagram
body:
Some students in a school were asked whether they have a dog, a cat or a rabbit.
28 have a dog, 18 have a cat, 20 have a rabbit, 8 have both a cat and a rabbit, 9 have both a dog and a rabbit, \(x\) have both a dog and a cat, 6 have all three, and 5 have none. A total of 50 students answered.
parts: Complete the Venn diagram, using x where necessary.
markscheme: Place: D only \(25-x\); C only \(16-x\); R only 9; D∩C only \(x-6\); D∩R only 3; C∩R only 2; all three 6; outside 5.
Note: B3 for all eight values, B2 for four to seven, B1 for two or three. Expressions involving x need not be simplified.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A three-circle Venn diagram inside universal set E has D as the left circle, C as the right circle and R as the lower circle, with all pairwise and triple overlaps. Every region is blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill D only with 25 − x, C only with 16 − x, R only with 9, D∩C only with x − 6, D∩R only with 3, C∩R only with 2, the triple intersection with 6, and outside all circles with 5.

title: Intersecting chords
body:
The diagram shows two chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersecting at \(P\).
\(AP=9\text{ cm}\), \(PB=6\text{ cm}\) and \(CP=8\text{ cm}\).
Calculate the length of \(PD\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two chords cross inside a circle at P. Chord AB runs from upper-left A through P to lower-right B, with AP labelled 9 cm and PB 6 cm. Chord CD runs from lower-left C through P to upper-right D, with CP labelled 8 cm. The circle boundary surrounds the four endpoints. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Fractional equation and quadratic inequality
markscheme: Note: dep on the first method mark.
\((5y+8)(y-5)\le0\), or correctly apply the quadratic formula to \(5y^2-17y-40=0\).

title: Surface areas of similar vases
body:
The diagram shows two similar vases, \(A\) and \(B\).
Their heights are 9 cm and 13 cm. The sum of their surface areas is \(1800\text{ cm}^2\).
Work out the surface area of vase \(A\).
markscheme: Area scale factor from A to B \(=\dfrac{13^2}{9^2}=\dfrac{169}{81}\), or reciprocal \(\dfrac{81}{169}\).
Note: ft and dep on the scale-factor mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two outline vases of the same shape are shown side by side. Vase A is smaller and labelled height 9 cm; vase B is larger and labelled height 13 cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Algebraic fractions and indices
parts: Given \(2^{2y}\times2^{3y+2}=\dfrac{8^{5y}}{4^n}\), find \(n\) in terms of \(y\), showing clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: dep on at least two method marks.

title: Arithmetic series term
body:
The first term of an arithmetic series \(S\) is −6.
The sum of the first 30 terms of \(S\) is 2865. Find the 9th term of \(S\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: dep on the series-sum method mark.

title: Completing the square
body:
Express \(7-12x-2x^2\) in the form \(a+b(x+c)^2\), where \(a,b\) and \(c\) are integers.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: SC: B2 for \(-2(x+3)^2+\text{constant}\) or \(25-2(x+\text{positive constant})^2\); B1 for \(-2(x-3)^2+\text{constant}\).

title: Area from perpendicular lines
body:
\(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are two straight lines.
\(L_1\) has equation \(5x+10y=8\). \(L_2\) is perpendicular to \(L_1\), passes through \((8,6)\), crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(A\), and meets \(x=-3\) at \(B\).
\(O\) is the origin. Find the area of triangle \(AOB\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: cao; dep on both earlier method marks.

title: Proof of a multiple of 20
body:
\(N\) is a multiple of 5.
\(A=N+1\) and \(B=N-1\).
Prove algebraically that \(A^2-B^2\) is always a multiple of 20.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Since \(N=5k\), \(4N=20k\), which is a multiple of 20.
Their difference is \(20k\), a multiple of 20.

title: Intersection in a vector trapezium
body:
The diagram shows trapezium \(OACB\).
\(\overrightarrow{OA}=3\mathbf a\), \(\overrightarrow{OB}=6\mathbf b\), and \(\overrightarrow{AC}=4\mathbf b\).
\(N\) lies on \(OC\) and \(A,N,B\) are collinear.
Find \(\overrightarrow{ON}\) as a simplified expression in terms of \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\).
markscheme: Equate coefficients: \(t(3\mathbf a+4\mathbf b)=3\mathbf a+s(-3\mathbf a+6\mathbf b)\), giving \(t=0.6,\ s=0.4\).
Equating coefficients gives \(t=0.6,\ s=0.4\), so \(\overrightarrow{AN}=-1.2\mathbf a+2.4\mathbf b\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Trapezium OACB has O lower-left, A upper-left, C upper-right and B lower-right, with AC parallel to OB. Diagonal OC is drawn. Arrow OA is labelled 3a, arrow AC is labelled 4b, and arrow OB is labelled 6b. Point N and line ANB are not drawn. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Sets and probability
body:
The numbers from 1 to 14 are shown in the Venn diagram. The universal set is \(E\), with subsets \(A\) and \(B\).
Use the information shown in the Venn diagram to answer each part. One of the integers is chosen at random.
parts: One integer is chosen at random. Find the probability that it is in A but not in B.
markscheme: There are 3 members in A but not in B, out of 14 members of the universal set.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A rectangle represents the universal set. Two overlapping circles are labelled A on the left and B on the right. A-only contains 8, 14 and 10; the intersection contains 2, 6, 4 and 12; B-only contains 1 and 3; outside both circles are 9, 13, 11, 7 and 5.

title: Faulty cars
body:
Toy cars are made in a factory.
5 toy cars are made every 12 seconds.
The factory makes toy cars for 15 hours each day.
The probability that a toy car is faulty is 0.002.
Work out an estimate of the number of faulty toy cars that are made each day.
markscheme: Note: Award both first method marks for a complete oe rate calculation.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Drawing a straight-line graph
body:
On the grid, draw the graph of \(y=7-4x\) for values of \(x\) from −2 to 3.
Plot the required points accurately and join them with a straight line.
markscheme: Calculate or plot at least two correct points, for example \((-2,15),(0,7),(3,-5)\).
Draw the straight line through the correct points.
Note: B3 overall for the fully correct line over the stated interval; otherwise award according to the stated point and line tolerances.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
Note: If B3 not awarded, award B2 for a correct line with one plotting error, or B1 for at least two correct points.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank coordinate grid has x from −2 to 3 and y from −5 to 15, with labelled axes and integer scales.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw the straight line segment through (−2,15), (−1,11), (0,7), (1,3), (2,−1) and (3,−5).

title: Mean and median
body:
Here is a list of six numbers written in order of size.\[4,\ 7,\ x,\ 10,\ y,\ y\]The median is 9 and the mean is 11.
Find the value of \(x\) and the value of \(y\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Standard form
parts: Work out \(\dfrac{3\times10^5-2.7\times10^4}{6\times10^{-2}}\). Give the answer in standard form.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
body: Give each answer in the required form. Show all stages in your working.

title: Rocket travel time
body:
A rocket travelled 100 km at an average speed of 28 440 km/h. Work out how long it took the rocket to travel the 100 km.
Give your answer in seconds, correct to the nearest second.
markscheme: Convert the speed: \(28440\div3600=7.9\text{ km/s}\), or first calculate \(100\div28440=0.0035\ldots\) hours.
Time \(=100\div7.9=12.658\ldots\) seconds, or complete the oe hours-to-seconds conversion.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Algebraic manipulation and equations
markscheme: Find factors with product −48 and sum −2.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Reflex angle in a decagon
body:
Here is a 10-sided polygon.
Eight of its interior angles are \(134^\circ,134^\circ,168^\circ,168^\circ,150^\circ,150^\circ,125^\circ\) and \(125^\circ\). Another interior angle is \(148^\circ\).
Work out the value of the reflex angle \(x\).
markscheme: Note: If not M2, M1 for at least three correctly calculated exterior angles used in a consistent sum.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A convex decagon, drawn roughly regular and symmetric about a vertical line, with one vertex at the top and one at the bottom. Nine of its interior angles are marked with small arcs inside the outline: 148 degrees at the top vertex, then 150 degrees at the vertex on each side of it, then 168 degrees on each side, then 134 degrees on each side, then 125 degrees on each side. At the tenth vertex, at the bottom, the angle OUTSIDE the polygon is marked x, with a large arc sweeping right round the outside of that vertex to show that it is reflex. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Reverse percentage
body:
In a sale, normal prices are reduced by 20%.
The sale price of a bag is $1080.
Work out the normal price of the bag.
markscheme: The sale price is 80% of the original, so use multiplier \(0.8\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Prime powers
body:
\(A=2\times3^{43}\) and \(B=16\times3^{37}\).
Use these prime-factor forms to answer both parts. Give each answer in its simplest form.
parts: Find the highest common factor of A and B.
Write AB as a product of powers of its prime factors.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Isosceles trapezium
body:
The diagram shows trapezium \(ABCD\), in which \(BC\) and \(AD\) are parallel.
The trapezium has exactly one line of symmetry.
\(AD=17.6\text{ cm}\), \(BC=8.4\text{ cm}\), and the area is \(179.4\text{ cm}^2\).
Work out the size of angle \(ABC\).
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
markscheme: Use \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{4.6}{13.8}\) for the lower base angle, or \(\tan\phi=\dfrac{13.8}{4.6}\) for the complementary angle.
Note: The mark scheme also accepts a complete Pythagoras followed by sine or cosine route.
\(\angle ABX=18.434\ldots^\circ\), equivalently \(\angle BAX=71.565\ldots^\circ\) (the base angle at \(A\) on the longer parallel side).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An isosceles trapezium has shorter horizontal top BC = 8.4 cm and longer horizontal base AD = 17.6 cm. The equal sloping sides join A to B and D to C. The interior angle at B is the required angle. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[7x-2y=34\]\[3x+5y=-3\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Eliminate one variable correctly, for example multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by 2, then add to obtain \(41x=164\).
Substitute the first value into either original equation, or repeat elimination for the other variable.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Compound interest rate
body:
Jan invests $8000 in a savings account.
The account pays compound interest at a rate of \(x\)% per year.
After 6 years, the investment is worth $8877.62.
Work out the value of \(x\).
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Inverse-square proportion
body:
\(F\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(v\).

When \(v=4\), \(F=6.5\).

Find a formula for \(F\) in terms of \(v\).
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Spinner probability tree
body: Harry has two fair 5-sided spinners, spinner \(A\) and spinner \(B\). Spinner \(A\) has two red sectors and three green sectors. Spinner \(B\) has four red sectors and one green sector. Harry spins each spinner once.
parts: Find the probability that at least one spinner lands on green.
markscheme: From each A branch, B red \(=\dfrac45\) and B green \(=\dfrac15\).
Note: Award B1 for at least three correct probabilities.
Form a relevant path product, such as \(\dfrac25\times\dfrac45\).
Use the complement: \(1-\dfrac25\times\dfrac45=1-\dfrac8{25}\); or sum the other three outcomes \(\dfrac{12}{25}+\dfrac3{25}+\dfrac2{25}\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE, three figures. Spinner A, a fair five-sided spinner with two red sectors and three green; spinner B, with four red and one green; and the BLANK PROBABILITY TREE that part (a) asks the student to complete, headed Spinner A and Spinner B with red and green branches and all six probabilities blank.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Fair five-sided spinner B has four red sectors and one green sector, with sectors equal in size.
figureNote3: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-stage probability tree first branches to red and green for spinner A, then each branch splits to red and green for spinner B. All branch probabilities are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. On the tree, label spinner A branches red 2/5 and green 3/5. From each, label spinner B branches red 4/5 and green 1/5.

title: Circle theorems
body: \(L,M,N\) and \(P\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\). Angle \(MNP=58^\circ\). Use the circle theorem information in the diagram and give a reason where requested.
parts:
(i) Find the size of angle \(MLP\).

(ii) Give a reason for your answer.
Find the size of the reflex angle \(MOP\).
markscheme: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to \(180^\circ\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle with centre O contains cyclic quadrilateral LMNP. M and P are endpoints of two chords meeting at N, where angle MNP is marked 58 degrees. Chords LM and LP form the opposite angle at L. Radii OM and OP are drawn so the reflex angle MOP is identifiable. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Upper bound for density
body:
A metal block has a mass of 5 kg, correct to the nearest 50 grams.
Its volume is \(1.84\times10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\), correct to 3 significant figures.\[\text{density}=\dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}\] Work out the upper bound for the density of the block.
Give your answer in \(\text{kg/m}^3\), correct to 1 decimal place.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Histogram of plant heights
body:
The table gives information about the heights, in centimetres, of some plants.
Height (\(h\) cm)Frequency
\(10<h\le20\)35
\(20<h\le35\)45
\(35<h\le50\)75
\(50<h\le70\)40
\(70<h\le80\)8
parts: On the grid, draw a histogram for this information.
Estimate the number of plants taller than 40 cm.
markscheme: Use frequency density = frequency ÷ class width; obtain at least two correct bar heights.
Bar heights are \(3.5,3,5,2,0.8\) for the five intervals.
Draw all five touching bars with correct widths, heights and a labelled frequency-density scale.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
Note: SC: award B1 for at least three correct frequency densities.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw touching histogram bars over 10–20, 20–35, 35–50, 50–70 and 70–80 with frequency densities 3.5, 3, 5, 2 and 0.8 respectively.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank histogram grid has plant height in centimetres on the horizontal axis from 10 to 80 and frequency density on the vertical axis.

title: Rationalising a denominator
body:
Without using a calculator, rationalise the denominator of \(\dfrac6{3-\sqrt7}\).
Simplify your answer.
Show each stage of your working.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Similar solids
body:
\(R\) and \(S\) are two similar solid shapes.
Their surface areas are \(108\text{ cm}^2\) and \(300\text{ cm}^2\). The volume of \(R\) is \(135\text{ cm}^3\).
Work out the volume of shape \(S\).
markscheme: Linear scale factor \(=\sqrt{300/108}=\dfrac53\), or use the reciprocal \(\dfrac35\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Algebraic fractions
body:
Express \(\dfrac1{3x-2}\times\dfrac{9x^2-4}{3x^2-13x-10}-\dfrac7{x-1}\) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Using both factorisations, cancel to obtain \(\dfrac1{x-5}\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Rhombus diagonal and coordinate geometry
body:
\(ABCD\) is a rhombus.
Diagonal \(AC\) lies on the line \(2y+7x=20\). The diagonals intersect at \(M=(6,-11)\). Diagonal \(BD\) crosses the \(y\)-axis at \(P\).
Find the exact coordinates of \(P\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Because the rhombus diagonals are perpendicular, gradient of BD is \(\dfrac27\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A rhombus ABCD is shown with both diagonals AC and BD crossing at M. Diagonal BD extends to meet the y-axis at P. The coordinate axes are schematic rather than scaled. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Decreasing cubic function
body:
Curve \(C\) has equation \(y=px^3-mx\), where \(p\) and \(m\) are positive integers. Find the range of values of \(x\), in terms of \(p\) and \(m\), for which the gradient of \(C\) is negative.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Arithmetic-series partial sum
body:
Here are the first five terms of an arithmetic sequence.\[8,\ 15,\ 22,\ 29,\ 36\] Work out the sum of all the terms from the 50th term to the 100th term inclusive.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: There are 51 terms, so sum \(=\dfrac{51}{2}(351+701)\), equivalently \(\dfrac{51}{2}[2(351)+50(7)]\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Graph transformations
parts: Describe fully the transformation from \(y=g(x)\) to \(y=-g(x)\).
The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is shown. On the grid, draw \(y=2f(x-1)\).
markscheme: Reflection in the x-axis, equivalently the line \(y=0\).
Draw the curve through transformed points \((2,6),(3,0),(5,-6),(7,0),(8,6)\).

Note: If not B2, award B1 for at least three correct target points, or for a consistent single transformation such as \(2f(x)\), \(f(x-1)\), \(2f(x+1)\), or a clear horizontal translation with the correct vertical scale.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A smooth U-shaped curve y = f(x) is drawn on a coordinate grid, passing through approximately (1,3), (2,0), (4,−3), (6,0) and (7,3), with its minimum at (4,−3).
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw the same U-shaped curve translated one unit right and stretched vertically by scale factor 2, through (2,6), (3,0), (5,−6), (7,0) and (8,6), with minimum at (5,−6).
body: The curve with equation \(y=g(x)\) is transformed to the curve with equation \(y=-g(x)\). A separate grid shows the graph of \(y=f(x)\). Answer both transformation questions using the printed axes.

title: Product of mixed numbers
body:
Show that \(3\dfrac34\times\dfrac79=2\dfrac{11}{12}\).
Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: \(\dfrac{15}{4}\times\dfrac79=\dfrac{105}{36}\), or cancel correctly before multiplying to obtain \(\dfrac{35}{12}\).
Note: The accuracy mark depends on both method marks and requires the multiplication result or correct prior cancellation. Use of decimals scores no marks.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Constructing an angle bisector
body:
Using ruler and compasses only, construct the bisector of angle ABC.
You must show all your construction lines.
markscheme: Draw an arc centred at B meeting BA and BC, then equal-radius arcs from those two intersection points so the arcs meet inside the angle.
Note: Also award the method mark for a correct bisector without visible arcs.
Draw the straight line from B through the intersection of the two inner arcs.
Note: The correct arcs must be visible for the accuracy mark.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two rays BA and BC form an acute angle at B, opening to the right. A is on the upper ray and C on the lower ray. No construction arcs or bisector are printed.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Preserve rays BA and BC. Draw an arc centred at B crossing both rays; from those two crossings draw equal-radius arcs that intersect inside the angle; draw the ray from B through that intersection. Keep all arcs visible.

title: Indices, substitution and a linear equation
markscheme: \(5x-8x=12+3\), so \(-3x=15\); or an oe correct rearrangement with x-terms on one side and constants on the other.
Note: dep on at least the first method mark. SC: B2 for x = −2 from 5x − 3 = 8x + 3, or x = 5 from 5x − 3 = 2x + 12.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
body: Answer all three algebra questions. Simplify fully where requested and show clear algebraic working for the equation.

title: Grouped-data mode and mean
body:
The table gives information about the length of time, in minutes, that each of 60 students takes to travel to school.
Time (\(t\) minutes)Frequency
\(0<t\le10\)4
\(10<t\le20\)10
\(20<t\le30\)15
\(30<t\le40\)25
\(40<t\le50\)6
parts: Write down the modal class interval.
Estimate the mean travel time, correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: M2 for correct midpoint products, allowing one error, with intention to add. If not M2, M1 for frequency products using consistent values within the intervals, allowing one error, with intention to add; or correct midpoint products without addition.
Note: dep on at least M1 above.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
Note: If not M2 then award M1 for at least four correct midpoint-frequency products.

title: Percentage change
parts: A village population rose from 7500 in 2017 to 8265 in 2019. Find the percentage increase.
Normal prices are reduced by 30%. A T-shirt sale price is 31.50 euros. Find its normal price.
markscheme: The sale price is 70% of normal, so calculate \(31.50\div(1-0.3)\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Midpoint coordinates
body:
Point \(A\) has coordinates \((-3,11)\). Point \(B\) has coordinates \((47,b)\). The midpoint of \(AB\) is \((a,-19)\). Find the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Use \(a=(-3+47)/2=22\), or \((11+b)/2=-19\), giving \(b=-49\); an oe midpoint displacement method is accept.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Average speed
body:
Pedro drove from Toulouse to Montpellier in 2 hours 42 minutes. His average speed was 90 km/h.
Janine drove along the same route in 3 hours.
Work out Janine’s average speed for the journey.
Give your answer in km/h.
markscheme: Distance \(=90\times2.7=243\text{ km}\), or set up an oe proportion equation.
Note: Allow use of 2.42 hours for this method mark.
Janine’s speed \(=243\div3\), or solve the proportion equation.
Note: dep on the preceding method mark.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Compound appreciation
body:
Harold bought an antique clock for £1200.
The value of the clock increases by 8% each year.
Find the value of the clock exactly 3 years after Harold bought it.
Give your answer correct to the nearest pound.
markscheme: Complete three years: \(1200\times1.08^3=1511.6544\), equivalently multiply successively by 1.08.

Note: Award the first two method marks for a direct \(1200\times1.08^3\). If only one direct-power step is shown, M1 is available for \(1200\times1.08^2=1399.68\). Alternatively award M2 for \(1200\times1.08^4=1632.59\) at this stage.
Note: Accept 1511–1512 before final rounding. SC: if no other marks, M1 for \(0.24\times1200\), 288 or 1488.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Pressure on a square face
body: A box is put on a horizontal table. The box rests on a square face of side 1.5 m. The pressure on the table is \(34.8\text{ N/m}^2\).\[\text{pressure}=\dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}\]Work out the force exerted by the box on the table.
markscheme: Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Cake sales and profit
body:
Alex makes 80 cakes to sell. The ratio chocolate : lemon : fruit is \(3:2:5\). He sells all the chocolate cakes, \(\dfrac34\) of the lemon cakes and \(\dfrac78\) of the fruit cakes. The profit on each sold cake is £2.00, £1.70 and £2.40 respectively.
Work out the total profit that Alex makes from the cakes he sells.
markscheme: Numbers made are chocolate \(3(8)=24\), lemon \(2(8)=16\), fruit \(5(8)=40\).
Note: The first two marks may be awarded together as M2 for a complete correct allocation; otherwise M1 for one correct cake count or for 80 ÷ 10.
Note: Award for a method to find either the lemon or fruit profit.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Cumulative frequency
body:
The frequency table gives information about the ages of the 80 people in a train carriage.
Age (\(a\) years)Frequency
\(0<a\le20\)9
\(20<a\le30\)19
\(30<a\le40\)17
\(40<a\le50\)18
\(50<a\le60\)13
\(60<a\le70\)4
parts:
Complete the cumulative frequency table.
Age (\(a\) years)Cumulative frequency
\(0<a\le20\)
\(0<a\le30\)
\(0<a\le40\)
\(0<a\le50\)
\(0<a\le60\)
\(0<a\le70\)
Use the graph to estimate the median age.
markscheme: Plot \((20,9),(30,28),(40,45),(50,63),(60,76),(70,80)\) and join with a curve or line segments.

Note: If not B2, B1 for five or six correct points at interval ends joined; five or six unjoined correct points; or five or six table values plotted consistently within their intervals and joined. ft one arithmetic error in the table.
Read horizontally from cumulative frequency 40 to the graph, then vertically down to the age axis.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
Note: Award B1 for at least four correct cumulative frequencies.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill the cumulative-frequency column with 9, 28, 45, 63, 76 and 80.
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (20,9), (30,28), (40,45), (50,63), (60,76) and (70,80), joining them with a smooth increasing curve or straight line segments. To estimate the median, draw across from cumulative frequency 40 and down to an age between 35 and 38.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank cumulative-frequency table has columns \(\text{Age }(a\text{ years})\) and Cumulative frequency, with rows \(0<a\le20\), \(0<a\le30\), \(0<a\le40\), \(0<a\le50\), \(0<a\le60\), \(0<a\le70\) and all six cumulative-frequency cells empty. Beside it a blank cumulative-frequency grid has age in years from 0 to 70 horizontally and cumulative frequency from 0 to 80 vertically.

title: Simultaneous equations
body: Solve the simultaneous equations\[7x+2y=5.5\]\[3x-5y=17\]Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Eliminate a variable correctly, for example \(35x+10y=27.5\) and \(6x-10y=34\), giving \(41x=61.5\); or use a correct substitution.
Substitute the found value into an original equation, or repeat the elimination method for the second variable.
Note: dep on the first method mark.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Differentiation and gradient points
body: The curve \(C\) has equation \(y=5x^3-x^2-6x+4\)
parts:
There are two points on the curve \(C\) at which the gradient of the curve is 2 Find the \(x\) coordinate of each of these two points.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for two of the three terms \(15x^2,-2x,-6\) correct.
Factorise \((3x+2)(5x-4)=0\), or correctly apply the quadratic formula or complete the square.

Note: For factorisation, allow brackets producing two of the three terms correctly. For the formula or completing the square, allow one sign error and some simplification, including \((2\pm\sqrt{4+480})/30\).
Note: dep on the first two method marks. Accept −0.66 or better; both values are required. Ignore any subsequent attempt to find y-coordinates.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Expanding three brackets
body:
Expand and simplify \((4x+1)(x-3)(5x+6)\).
Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: Multiply any two brackets correctly enough, for example \((4x+1)(x-3)=4x^2-11x-3\).
Note: Require at least three of the four terms correct before collection.
Note: dep on the first method mark; ft the first product and require at least three of six, or four of eight, product terms correct.
Expand directly to the eight terms \(20x^3+24x^2-60x^2+5x^2-15x+6x-72x-18\).
Note: If not B2, B1 for four or five of the eight terms correct; B2 requires at least six.
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Circle-theorem proof of parallel lines
body:
B, D, E and F lie on a circle. ABC is tangent at B. Angle EDF = 40° and angle FBC = 70°. Prove that ABC is parallel to EF, giving a reason for every stage.
Prove that \(ABC\) is parallel to \(EF\).
Give a reason for every stage of your working.
markscheme: The angle between tangent BC and chord BF equals the angle subtended by BF in the alternate segment.
\(\angle EFB=180^\circ-(70^\circ+40^\circ)=70^\circ\), because opposite angles in cyclic quadrilateral BDEF sum to \(180^\circ\).
\(\angle CBF=\angle EFB\); equal alternate angles imply \(ABC\parallel EF\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle touches horizontal tangent line ABC at B, with A left of B and C right of B. Points D and E lie on the left side of the circle and F on the upper right. Chords DB, DE, DF, EF and FB are drawn. Angle EDF is 40 degrees and the angle between BF and tangent BC is 70 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Composite and inverse functions
body: Functions are \(f:x\mapsto5x-7\) and \(g:x\mapsto\dfrac{5x}{x+4}\).
parts: State the value excluded from any domain of g.
markscheme: Note: SC: award B1 for one correct inverse-function step.
From \(fg(x)=2\), write \(g(x)=f^{-1}(2)=\dfrac95\), with an attempt at \(f^{-1}\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Angles and lengths in a prism
body:
Prism ABCDEFGH has horizontal square base EFGH of side 12 cm. In trapezium cross-section ADEF, AF and DE are vertical. DE = CH = 10 cm and AD = BC = 15 cm.
The diagram shows prism \(ABCDEFGH\) with a horizontal base. The base \(EFGH\) is a square of side 12 cm. \(DE=CH=10\text{ cm}\) and \(AD=BC=15\text{ cm}\).
parts: Find the angle between CF and base EFGH, correct to one decimal place.
Find BE, correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: \(\tan\angle CFH=\dfrac{10}{16.970}\ldots\); alternatively find \(CF=\sqrt{FH^2+10^2}=\sqrt{388}\) and use a correct sine statement.
Note: ft the base diagonal from part (a).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique prism has horizontal square base EFGH. E is front-right, F front-left, G rear-left and H rear-right; base sides FE and EH are each labelled 12 cm. Vertical edges AF and DE rise from F and E, with DE labelled 10 cm. Corresponding rear vertices B above G and C above H give CH = 10 cm. Sloping prism edges AD and BC are each 15 cm; BC is labelled. Hidden edges BG, GH and HC are dashed where appropriate. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Arithmetic-series sum
body:
In an arithmetic series, the 6th term is 39 and the 19th term is 7.8. Find the sum of the first 25 terms.

body:

markscheme: \(HE=10+2(10\sin45^\circ)=10+10\sqrt2=24.142\ldots\text{ cm}\); an oe sine-rule method is accept.
Perpendicular height of triangle ACD \(=10\sin45^\circ=5\sqrt2\), or find \(AC=18.477\ldots\) by a correct cosine/sine-rule method.
Area of triangle ACD \(=\dfrac12(24.142\ldots)(7.071\ldots)=85.355\ldots\text{ cm}^2\), or \(\dfrac12(10)(18.477\ldots)\sin112.5^\circ\).
Find an exterior, interior or central octagon angle of \(45^\circ\) or \(135^\circ\).
Area of one of the eight central triangles \(=\dfrac12(10)(5)\tan67.5^\circ=60.355\ldots\), hence octagon area \(=482.843\ldots\text{ cm}^2\).
Octagon area minus those two unshaded regions \(=326.776\ldots\), so \(327\text{ cm}^2\).
Note: oe; ft where indicated; dep on the preceding method mark.

title: Mass of platinum cylinders
body:
Platinum nuggets are in the shape of a solid cylinder. The radius of each cylinder is 2.5 cm.
The length of each cylinder is 15 cm. The density of platinum is 21.5 g/cm\(^3\) The greatest mass that Jacques can carry is 30 kg. Can Jacques carry 5 platinum nuggets at the same time?
You must show all your working.
markscheme: Five masses \(=31.661\ldots\text{ kg}\), or calculate that 30 kg carries only \(4.7376\ldots\) nuggets, or compare oe per-nugget limits.
Note: A correct comparable figure must be shown: accept 31.6–31.7 kg, 1.6–1.7 kg over, or 4.70–4.74 nuggets.
Use \(21.5=30000/v\), or divide 30000 by 5 before applying density.
Maximum total volume \(=\dfrac{30000}{21.5}=1395.35\ldots\text{ cm}^3\), or maximum per nugget \(=279.070\ldots\text{ cm}^3\).
Compare with five-nugget volume \(5(294.5243\ldots)=1472.62\ldots\text{ cm}^3\), or compare per-nugget volumes.
No; the required volume exceeds the allowable volume.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A horizontal solid cylinder is drawn in perspective. Its circular radius is labelled 2.5 cm and its axial length is labelled 15 cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Circle angles
body:
\(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\) and \(E\) are points on a circle.

Angle \(EAC=40^\circ\)
parts:
(i) Write down the size of angle \(EBC\).

(ii) Give a reason for your answer.
markscheme: Angles in the same segment are equal; equivalently, angles at the circumference subtended by the same arc are equal.
Note: Also accept a valid two-step cyclic-quadrilateral argument.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Five points A, B, C, D and E lie around a circle. Chords AE and AC form angle EAC = 40 degrees at A. Chords BE and BC form the corresponding angle at B, and chords DE and DC form the supplementary angle at D. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

body:
Given that \(n>0\)

make \(n\) the subject of the formula \(y=\dfrac{n^2+d}{n^2}\)

title: Cubic graph and graphical equation
body:
The table gives values for \(y=\dfrac12x^3-2x+3\).
\(x\)−3−2−10123
\(y\)−4.533
parts: On the grid, draw the graph of \(y=\dfrac12x^3-2x+3\) for \(-3\leq x\leq3\)
By drawing a suitable straight line on the grid, find an estimate for the solution of the equation \(\dfrac12x^3-x+4=0\)
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for any two of the four missing values correct. Correct plotted values may earn the table mark.
Plot the seven points and draw the correct smooth cubic curve.
Note: If not B2, B1 for a correct smooth curve, or at least five correct points; ft the table for plotting only when B1 was earned in part (a). Tolerance is half a small square.
Rearrange to draw \(y=-x-1\), using two correct points, and identify its intersection with the cubic.

Note: ft their curve; dep on drawing the line.

answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Complete the y-row with −4.5, 3, 4.5, 3, 1.5, 3 and 10.5 beneath x = −3 through 3.
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (−3,−4.5), (−2,3), (−1,4.5), (0,3), (1,1.5), (2,3) and (3,10.5), join with a smooth cubic curve, and draw the straight line y = −x − 1. Its left intersection gives x between −2.3 and −2.4.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank coordinate grid has x from −3 to 3 and y from −5 to 11. No points, curve or straight line are printed.

title: Sector area and circle theorem
body:
\(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\) and radius 12 cm. The area of the sector \(OADC\) of the circle is 100 cm\(^2\) Work out the size of angle \(ABC\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: ft a central angle below 360 degrees; dep on the first method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle with centre O and radius 12 cm has radii OA and OC bounding the minor sector OADC of area 100 cm²; D lies on the minor arc AC. Point B lies on the opposite arc and chords BA and BC form the required angle at B. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Inverse-square proportion
body:
\(T\) is inversely proportional to \(m^2\)

\(T=30\) when \(m=0.5\)
parts: Find a formula for \(T\) in terms of \(m\).
Work out the value of \(T\) when \(m=0.1\)
markscheme: Note: Do not allow the constant to be assumed as 1.
Note: dep on the first method mark; both method marks may be awarded directly for k = 7.5.
Note: SC: B2 for an otherwise correct relation with T and m interchanged/multiplied, such as \(Tm^2=7.5\), when not rearranged to the requested form.

title: Reading a histogram
body:
The histogram gives information about the times, in minutes, some customers had to wait to be served in a restaurant.

14 customers had to wait less than 10 minutes to be served.

Work out the number of customers who had to wait less than 60 minutes to be served.
markscheme: First-bar density \(=\dfrac{14}{10}=1.4\); equivalently determine one small-square or area-to-frequency scale.
Note: oe scaled-area totals are accept. Allow one error, including one missing bar total.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A histogram has waiting time in minutes on the horizontal axis from 0 to 60 and frequency density vertically. Bars cover 0–10, 10–25, 25–30, 30–40 and 40–60 minutes. Their printed relative heights correspond respectively to frequency densities 1.4, 3.2, 3.6, 0.6 and 0.2, although the vertical axis has no numerical labels.

title: Line-curve intersections and distance
body:
The curve with equation \(x^2-x+y^2=10\) and the straight line with equation \(x-y=-4\) intersect at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Work out the exact length of \(AB\).
Show your working clearly and give your answer in the form \(\dfrac{\sqrt{a}}{2}\) where \(a\) is an integer.
markscheme: From the line, substitute \(x=y-4\) into the curve, or \(y=x+4\).
Factorise \((2y-5)(y-2)=0\), or \((2x+3)(x+2)=0\), or solve the quadratic correctly.
Note: ft a three-term quadratic; allow factors yielding two of three terms correctly, or one sign error/some simplification in a formula or completing-square route.
Note: dep on the substitution method mark.
Note: dep on the first three method marks.
Note: SC: award B1 for one correct intersection point.

title: Perpendicular bisector
body:
\(P\) and \(Q\) are two points. The coordinates of \(P\) are \((-1,6)\) The coordinates of \(Q\) are \((5,-4)\) Find an equation of the perpendicular bisector of \(PQ\).
Give your answer in the form \(ax+by+c=0\) where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are integers.
markscheme: Use \(y-1=\dfrac35(x-2)\), equivalently substitute (2,1) into \(y=\dfrac35x+c\) to obtain \(c=-\dfrac15\).
Note: dep on the midpoint and perpendicular-gradient marks.
For a general point \((x,y)\), write its squared distances to P and Q.
Cancel the common quadratic terms and collect to a linear equation.

title: Completing the square
parts: Write \(7+12x-3x^2\) in the form \(a+b(x+c)^2\) where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are integers.

The curve \(C\) has equation \(y=7+12x-3x^2\)
The point \(A\) is the turning point on \(C\). Using your answer to part (a), write down the coordinates of \(A\).
markscheme: Note: ft part (a), dep on at least one method mark there.

title: Vector intersection ratio
body:
\(OAN\), \(OMB\), \(APB\) and \(MPN\) are straight lines. \(OA:AN=1:4\) \(OM:MB=1:1\)
\(\overrightarrow{OA}=2\mathbf a\) \(\overrightarrow{OB}=2\mathbf b\) By using a vector method, find the ratio \(AP:PB\)
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: Find a key vector, for example \(\overrightarrow{AB}=2\mathbf b-2\mathbf a\) or \(\overrightarrow{MN}=10\mathbf a-\mathbf b\).
Write a vector to P in one parametric way, for example \(\overrightarrow{AP}=k(2\mathbf b-2\mathbf a)\).
Write the same vector in a second way through M or N, for example \(\overrightarrow{AP}=8\mathbf a+\lambda(\mathbf b-10\mathbf a)\).
Note: Together these two rows are M2 for two valid expressions for the same vector; if only one is written, M1. The mark scheme lists oe parameterisations using MP, PN, AP or AM.
Equate coefficients of \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\) and solve the resulting pair, obtaining an AP fraction \(k=\dfrac49\) (or an oe parameter value).
Note: dep on all three preceding method marks.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two rays from O form a triangle-like wedge: O, A and N are collinear on the upper ray in that order, and O, M and B are collinear on the lower ray in that order. Straight line AB crosses straight line MN at P inside the wedge, with P between A and B and between M and N. OA:AN = 1:4 and OM:MB = 1:1 are stated in the question text. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Intersecting secants with surds
body:
\(A\), \(B\), \(D\) and \(E\) are points on a circle.
\(ABC\) and \(EDC\) are straight lines. \(BC=(2+\sqrt5)\) cm \(ED=(4+\sqrt5)\) cm \(DC=2\sqrt5\) cm Show that the length of \(AB\) is \((p\sqrt5+q)\) cm, where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers whose values are to be found.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: dep on the intersecting-secants mark. An oe equation using AB directly is accept.
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(2-\sqrt5\).
Note: Independent, provided the fraction has the form \((a+b\sqrt5)/(c+d\sqrt5)\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. From exterior point C at the right, two secants enter a circle. On the upper secant the order is C, B, A; BC is labelled (2 + √5) cm. On the lower secant the order is C, D, E; DC is labelled 2√5 cm and internal segment DE is labelled (4 + √5) cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Currency shares in a ratio
body:
Pieter owns a currency conversion shop. Last Monday, Pieter changed a total of 20 160 rand into a number of different currencies. He changed \(\dfrac{3}{10}\) of the 20 160 rand into euros.
He changed the rest of the rands into dollars, rupees and francs in the ratios 9 : 5 : 2 Pieter changed more rands into dollars than he changed into francs. Work out how many more.
markscheme: Note: The first two marks may be awarded together as M2 for \((9-2)/(9+5+2)\times14112\).

title: Emptying a prism
body:
The diagram shows a container for water in the shape of a prism. The rectangular base of the prism, shown shaded in the diagram, is horizontal.
The container is completely full of water. Tuah is going to use a pump to empty the water from the container so that the volume of water in the container decreases at a constant rate. The pump starts to empty water from the container at 10 30 and at 12 00 the water level in the container has dropped by 20 cm. Find the time at which all the water has been pumped out of the container.
markscheme: Find a relevant volume: pumped volume \(=30(20)(125)=75000\text{ cm}^3\), remaining volume \(=85(40)(125)=425000\text{ cm}^3\), or total volume \([60(30)+(85-30)(40)]125=500000\text{ cm}^3\).
Use the 1.5-hour interval to find rate or a time ratio, for example \(\dfrac{75000}{1.5}=50000\text{ cm}^3/\text{h}\), or \(\dfrac{425000}{75000}=\dfrac{17}3\).
Note: M2 may be awarded for a complete ratio-time calculation such as \(\dfrac{425000}{75000}\times1.5=8.5\) h or \(\dfrac{500000}{75000}\times1.5=10\) h.
Remaining time \(=\dfrac{425000}{50000}=8.5\) hours after noon, equivalently total pumping time 10 hours from 10:30.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A container in the shape of a prism, drawn receding to the upper right, length 125 cm. Its cross-section is an L-shaped step: a horizontal base 85 cm wide, a 60 cm vertical on the left, a 30 cm horizontal top, a 20 cm drop, then a 40 cm vertical on the right. Right angles are marked at the corners of the cross-section and the horizontal rectangular base is shaded. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Compound growth and reverse depreciation
parts:
Chen invests 40 000 yuan in a fixed-term bond for 3 years. The fixed-term bond pays compound interest at a rate of 3.5% each year. Work out the value of Chen’s investment at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer to the nearest yuan.

Wang invested \(P\) yuan.
The value of his investment decreased by 6.5% each year. At the end of the first year, the value of Wang’s investment was 30 481 yuan. Work out the value of \(P\).
markscheme: Note: accept 44 348–44 349. SC: if no other marks, M1 for \(0.105(40000)\), 4200 or 44200.

title: Perimeter of a semicircular path
body:
The region, shown shaded in the diagram, is a path. The boundary of the path is formed by two semicircles, with the same centre \(O\), and two straight lines. The inner semicircle has a radius of 7 metres.
The path has a width of 2 metres. Work out the perimeter of the path.
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Inner semicircle arc \(=7\pi\), or outer arc \(=9\pi\).
Note: M1 for a method to find the length of the two arcs with intention to add; allow \(7\pi+9\pi+2\) or \(7\pi+9\pi+2+2\) oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A shaded half-annulus has centre O at the midpoint of its straight diameter boundary. Inner radius is labelled 7 m and radial width 2 m. The boundary consists of two concentric semicircular arcs and two short straight radial end segments. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Indices and a quadratic
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for two of coefficient 16, exponent 12 and exponent 20 correct.
Choose factors with magnitudes 9 and 4, or factors a,b with \(ab=-36\) or \(a+b=5\).

title: Perimeter of an isosceles triangle
body:
Here is isosceles triangle \(ABC\). \(D\) is the midpoint of \(AC\) and \(DB=16\) cm. Angle \(DAB=65^\circ\) Work out the perimeter of triangle \(ABC\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Use \(\sin65^\circ=16/AB\), or an equivalent correct trig ratio for AB or AD.
\(AB=16/\sin65^\circ=17.654\ldots\text{ cm}\) and \(AD=16/\tan65^\circ=7.460\ldots\text{ cm}\), using trigonometry or Pythagoras for the second length.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Isosceles triangle ABC has apex B at the lower-right and vertical-ish base AC on the left, with equal sides AB and BC. D is the midpoint of AC and segment DB is drawn perpendicular to AC, labelled 16 cm. Angle DAB at A is 65 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Reading a cumulative-frequency graph
body: The cumulative frequency graph gives information about the weights, in grams, of 90 bags of sweets.
parts: Find an estimate for the median of the weights of these bags of sweets.

Roberto sells the bags of sweets to raise money for charity.
Bags with a weight greater than \(d\) grams are labelled large bags and sold for 3.75 euros each bag. The total amount of money he receives by selling all the large bags is 93.75 euros. Find the value of \(d\).
markscheme: Read the graph at cumulative frequency 45.
Bags at or below d have cumulative frequency \(90-25=65\); read the graph at 65.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A cumulative-frequency curve for 90 bags is drawn on axes with weight from 120 to 180 grams horizontally and cumulative frequency from 0 to 90 vertically. The curve increases smoothly from near (125,0) to near (175,90). No median, d or guide lines are drawn.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. For part (a), draw across from cumulative frequency 45 to the curve and down to about 146 g. For part (b), draw across from cumulative frequency 65 and down to about 151 g.

title: Algebraic fractions and expansion
parts:
Express \(\dfrac4{x-2}-\dfrac3{x+1}\) as a single fraction.
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: Numerator \(=4x+4-3x+6\), with the denominator retained correctly.
Note: allow one numerator expansion error if the common denominator is correct; expanded denominator is accepted.
Multiply one stage correctly, for example \(2x(x-5)=2x^2-10x\) or \((x-5)(x-3)=x^2-8x+15\).
Multiply the intermediate product by the remaining factor, for example \(2x(x^2-8x+15)=2x^3-16x^2+30x\).
Note: dep on the first method mark; ft and require at least three product terms correct.

title: Probability tree
body:
Ding is going to play one game of snooker against each of two of his friends, Marco and Judd.

The probability tree diagram gives information about the probabilities that Ding will win or lose each of these two games.
parts: Work out the probability that Ding will win both games.
Work out the probability that Ding will win exactly one of the games.
markscheme: Note: ft part (a) in the complement route.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-stage probability tree first branches to Ding wins Marco (0.6) and loses Marco (0.4). From the win branch, Judd outcomes are win 0.9 and lose 0.1; from the lose branch, Judd outcomes are win 0.25 and lose 0.75. All probabilities are printed.

title: Upper bound of acceleration
body:
\(a=\dfrac{v-u}{t}\)
\(v=9.6\) correct to 1 decimal place
\(u=3.8\) correct to 1 decimal place
\(t=1.84\) correct to 2 decimal places Calculate the upper bound for the value of \(a\).
Give your answer as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
Show your working clearly.

title: Bearing between ships
body:
The diagram shows the positions of three ships, \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\). Ship \(B\) is due north of ship \(A\). The bearing of ship \(C\) from ship \(A\) is \(120^\circ\) Calculate the bearing of ship \(C\) from ship \(B\).
Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.
markscheme: Use a correct sine or cosine rule for \(\angle ABC\) or \(\angle ACB\), for example \(\sin B/275=\sin120^\circ/373.33\ldots\).
Note: dep on the cosine-rule mark; ft their BC.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Ship A is lower-left and ship B directly above it, with AB labelled 150 m. The north line at A is AB produced, its arrowhead above B, and the second north arrow is at C - NOT at B. Ship C is to the lower-right of B and AC is labelled 275 m. The clockwise angle from north at A to AC is 120 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Maximum volume expression
body:
A solid, \(S\), is made from a hemisphere and a cylinder. The centre of the circular face of the hemisphere and the centre of the top face of the cylinder are at the same point. The radius of the cylinder and the radius of the hemisphere are both \(x\) cm.
The height of the cylinder is \((20-4x)\) cm.
The volume of \(S\) is \(V\) cm\(^3\) where \(V=\dfrac13\pi y\)
Find the maximum value of \(y\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Equate to \(\dfrac13\pi y\) and simplify consistently.
\(dy/dx=120x-30x^2=0\), so the positive stationary value is \(x=4\).
Note: Correct answer only, dep on all three method marks.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A hemisphere sits directly on a vertical cylinder with coincident circular faces. Both have radius x cm, shown by a horizontal radius arrow on the join. The cylinder height is labelled (20 − 4x) cm. Hidden rear arcs of the circular joins are dashed. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Surd identity with a prime
body:
Given that \((8-\sqrt{x})(5+\sqrt{x})=y\sqrt{x}+21\) where \(x\) is a prime number and \(y\) is an integer, find the value of \(x\) and the value of \(y\).

Show each stage of your working clearly.

title: Nonlinear simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations \(x^2-9y-x=2y^2-12\)
\(x+2y-1=0\)
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: From \(x=1-2y\), substitute into the first equation.
Factorise \((2y-3)(y-4)=0\), or \((x+7)(x+2)=0\), or solve the quadratic correctly.
Note: dep on the first method mark; ft a three-term quadratic and allow one sign error/some formula simplification or factors producing two terms correctly.
Note: Pairs must be matched correctly; dep on the first method mark.

title: Surface area of similar solids
body:
\(A\) and \(B\) are two similar solids. \(A\) has a volume of 1836 cm\(^3\)
\(B\) has a volume of 4352 cm\(^3\) \(B\) has a total surface area of 1120 cm\(^2\) Work out the total surface area of \(A\).
markscheme: Linear scale factor B:A \(=\sqrt[3]{4352/1836}=\dfrac43\), or A:B \(=\dfrac34\).
Area of A \(=1120\left(\dfrac34\right)^2\), equivalently divide by \(\left(\dfrac43\right)^2\).

title: Function and trigonometric graph transformations
body:
A curve has equation \(y=f(x)\)

The coordinates of the minimum point on this curve are \((-9,15)\)
parts:
(i) Write down the coordinates of the minimum point on the curve with equation \(y=f(x+3)\)

(ii) Write down the coordinates of the minimum point on the curve with equation \(y=\dfrac13f(x)\)

The graph of \(y=a\cos(x+b)^\circ\) for \(0\leq x\leq360\) is drawn on the grid below.

Given that \(a>0\) and that \(0<b<360\)

find the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).

title: Inverse of a restricted quadratic
body:
The function \(f\) is such that \(f(x)=x^2-8x+5\) where \(x\leq4\)

Express the inverse function \(f^{-1}\) in the form \(f^{-1}(x)=...\)
markscheme: Complete the square: \(y=(x-4)^2-11\), equivalently \(x=(y-4)^2-11\) after interchanging variables.
Rearrange to a quadratic and substitute into the quadratic formula, allowing one sign error in the setup.

title: Vector ratio on a median
body:
\(OAB\) is a triangle. \(\overrightarrow{OA}=2\mathbf a\) and \(\overrightarrow{OB}=2\mathbf b\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\).
\(N\) is the point on \(OB\) such that \(ON:NB=2:1\) \(P\) is the point on \(AN\) such that \(OPM\) is a straight line. Use a vector method to find \(OP:PM\)
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Find a side or half-side vector, for example \(\overrightarrow{AB}=2\mathbf b-2\mathbf a\) or \(\overrightarrow{AM}=\mathbf b-\mathbf a\).
Find \(\overrightarrow{OM}=\mathbf a+\mathbf b\), or \(\overrightarrow{AN}=\dfrac43\mathbf b-2\mathbf a\).
Write \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\lambda(\dfrac43\mathbf b-2\mathbf a)+2\mathbf a\), or an equivalent parameterisation along AN or OM.
Equate this with \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\mu(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)\), or set up an equivalent vector equation for MP.
Equating coefficients gives \(\mu=\dfrac45\), equivalently the remaining MP fraction is \(\dfrac15\).
Note: Correct answer only, dep on the first three method marks.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Triangle OAB has O lower-left, A upper-left and B upper-right. M is the midpoint of AB, N lies on OB closer to B with ON:NB = 2:1, and line AN meets line OM at P. Segments AN and OM are drawn. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Arithmetic-series identity
body:
An arithmetic series has first term \(a\) and common difference \(d\). The sum of the first \(2n\) terms of the series is four times the sum of the first \(n\) terms of the series. Find an expression for \(a\) in terms of \(d\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: dep on the first method mark.
Simplify to a correct linear relation, for example \(2a+(2n-1)d=4a+2(n-1)d\), hence \(2a=d\).
Note: dep on both first method marks.

title: Multiplying mixed numbers
body: Show that \(3\dfrac15\times1\dfrac56=5\dfrac{13}{15}\)
markscheme: \(\dfrac{16}{5}\times\dfrac{11}{6}=\dfrac{176}{30}\) oe, with correct cancelling or multiplication of numerators and denominators without cancelling.
Note: dep on M2 for conclusion to \(5\dfrac{13}{15}\) from correct working. NB: use of decimals scores no marks.
