title: Average speed
body:
A train journey from Paris to Amsterdam took 3 hours 24 minutes.
The total distance the train travelled was 433.5 km. Work out the average speed of the train.
Give your answer in kilometres per hour.

title: Volumes and cubic-unit conversion
parts:
Work out the volume of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
markscheme: Note: M1 ft dep on M1; accept 572–573.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A rectangular cuboid has edges labelled x cm, 12 cm and 5 cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. A right circular cylinder has base radius x cm and vertical height 2x cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.
body:
The diagram shows a cuboid and a cylinder. The dimensions of the cuboid are \(x\) cm by 12 cm by 5 cm.
The volume of the cuboid is 270 cm\(^3\) The radius of the cylinder is \(x\) cm.
The height of the cylinder is \(2x\) cm.

title: Three years of compound interest
body:
Kuro invests 50 000 yen for 3 years in a savings account.
She gets 2.4% per year compound interest. Work out how much money Kuro will have in her savings account at the end of the 3 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest yen.
markscheme: Complete three years: \(50000(1.024)^3=53687.0912\); equivalently values 51200, 52428.8, 53687.0912, or interest amounts 1200, 1228.8 and 1258.2912.
Note: A direct correct three-year calculation earns both method marks; \(50000(1.024)^2=52428.8\) earns one.

title: Angles around regular polygons
body:
The diagram shows a regular pentagon, \(ABCDE\), a regular hexagon, \(CFGHID\), and a quadrilateral, \(EDIJ\). \(AEJ\) and \(HIJ\) are straight lines. Work out the size of the angle marked \(x\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Regular pentagon interior angle \(=108^\circ\), equivalently exterior angle \(72^\circ\).
Regular hexagon interior angle \(=120^\circ\), equivalently exterior angle \(60^\circ\).
At the other shared vertex, the quadrilateral angle is \(360-108-120=132^\circ\).
Note: dep on both preceding method marks; an equivalent exterior-angle route is allowed.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A regular pentagon and a regular hexagon share one side of a four-sided central gap. Their vertices meet the gap at two points. Angle x is the interior angle EJI at J, the remaining lower vertex of the gap. Equal-side tick marks identify the regular polygons. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: HCF and LCM in index form
body: \(A=2^8\times3^5\times11^4\) \(B=2^6\times3\times11^8\)
parts: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of \(A\) and \(B\).

Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of \(2A\) and \(3B\).
Give the LCM as a product of powers of its prime factors.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for two correct prime exponents.
Note: If not B2, B1 for two correct prime exponents or oe value.

title: Paint needed for a wall
body:
The diagram shows one face of a wall.
This face is in the shape of a pentagon with exactly one line of symmetry. Omondi is going to paint this face of the wall once.
He has to buy all the paint that he needs to use. The paint in each tin of paint Omondi is going to buy will cover 16 m\(^2\) of the face of the wall. Work out the least number of tins of paint Omondi will need to buy.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Half the triangular base is 5 m, so roof height \(=\sqrt{7^2-5^2}=\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6=4.898\ldots\text{ m}\).
Use the roof height in a complete area method; an equivalent trigonometric route, including apex angle \(91.169\ldots^\circ\), is allowed.
Note: The final mark depends on at least two method marks and requires rounding up.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A wall shaped as a rectangle topped by an isosceles triangular roof has one vertical line of symmetry. The base is 10 m, each vertical side is 6 m, and each sloping roof side is 7 m. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Cumulative frequency
body:
The manager of a call centre asked the 120 people, who rang the call centre last week, how long they each waited before their call was answered. The table gives information about their replies.
Time waited (\(t\) minutes)Frequency
\(08
\(515
\(1017
\(1528
\(2033
\(2519
parts:
Complete the cumulative frequency table.
Time waited (\(t\) minutes)Cumulative frequency
\(0
\(0
\(0
\(0
\(0
\(0
On the grid below, draw a cumulative frequency graph for your table.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the median of the times waited.

Using your graph, find an estimate for the percentage of the 120 people who said that they waited longer than 23 minutes before their call was answered.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Join the points with a correct increasing curve or polygon.
Read at cumulative frequency 60: about 17–20 minutes.
Read cumulative frequency a at 23 minutes and calculate \((120-a)/120\times100\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. The empty grid the student draws the cumulative frequency graph on: time waited 0 to 30 minutes, cumulative frequency 0 to 120.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank cumulative-frequency grid has time from 0 to 30 minutes horizontally and cumulative frequency from 0 to 120 vertically.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. The cumulative frequency graph plotted at the upper class boundaries (5, 8), (10, 23), (15, 40), (20, 68), (25, 101), (30, 120).
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (5,8), (10,23), (15,40), (20,68), (25,101) and (30,120), join with a smooth increasing curve or polygon, and use horizontal reading guides at cumulative frequency 60 and from t = 23 as needed.

title: Indices and algebraic fractions
parts: Write \(\dfrac{2x+1}{4}+\dfrac{x-2}{3}\) as a single fraction in its simplest form.

Given that \(4^{k+3}=16\times2^k\) find the value of \(k\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for two of coefficient 4 and exponents 5 and 3 correct.
Convert one side to base 2, for example \(4^{k+3}=2^{2k+6}\) or \(16\times2^k=2^{k+4}\).
Note: The answer mark depends on both base-conversion method marks. oe base-4 working is allowed.

title: Vector subtraction
body:
Here are two vectors.
\(\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\3\end{pmatrix}\) \(\overrightarrow{CB}=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\4\end{pmatrix}\)
Find, as a column vector, \(\overrightarrow{AC}\)

title: Circle theorems
body:
\(B\), \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\) are points on a circle. \(ABC\) is the tangent at \(B\) to the circle.
Angle \(ABD=39^\circ\)
Angle \(EFD=18^\circ\) Work out the size of angle \(BDE\).
Give reasons for your working.
markscheme: \(\angle BFD=39^\circ\) by the alternate segment theorem, and hence the corresponding cyclic angle used in triangle BDE is \(39^\circ\).
Identify the required equal or supplementary cyclic angle, using angles in the same segment or opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral.
Note: The stated reasons mark depends on relevant angle working.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Points B, D, E and F lie on a circle. A straight tangent ABC touches the circle at B. Chords BD, BF, DE, DF and EF are drawn as printed. Angle ABD between the tangent and chord BD is 39 degrees; angle EFD is 18 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Recurring decimals and rationalising
parts:
Show that \(\dfrac2{6-3\sqrt2}\) can be written in the form \(\dfrac{a+\sqrt a}{b}\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(6+3\sqrt2\).

title: Expansion and completing the square
parts: Express \(x^2-10x+40\) in the form \((x+a)^2+b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
markscheme: Multiply any two factors correctly, for example \((x+4)(x-2)=x^2+2x-8\).
Multiply the intermediate quadratic by the remaining factor.

title: Nonlinear simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations
\(x-6y=5\)
\(xy-2y^2=6\)
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Factorise \((4y-3)(y+2)=0\), or otherwise solve the quadratic.
Note: dep on the first method mark; ft a suitable three-term quadratic.

title: Mean from a histogram
body:
The histogram and the table give some information about the amounts of time, in hours, that Year 11 students at Bergdesh Academy spent, in total, on their homework last week.
No student in Year 11 spent longer than 9 hours on their homework.
Time spent on homework (\(t\) hours)Frequency
\(028
\(2
\(4
\(5
\(6
Using the information in the histogram and in the table, work out an estimate for the mean amount of time the Year 11 students spent on their homework last week.
Give your answer in hours correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: The first bar has width 2 and frequency 28, so its frequency density is \(\dfrac{28}2=14\); use this to set the vertical scale.
Read the other bar densities and multiply by widths: frequencies \(40,30,24,36\) for \(2<t\le4,4<t\le5,5<t\le6,6<t\le9\).
Note: Award for at least three of these four frequencies correct.
Note: dep on the frequency work; ft their frequencies.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A histogram has time t from 0 to 10 hours horizontally and an unnumbered frequency-density axis vertically. Bars cover 0–2, 2–4, 4–5, 5–6 and 6–9 hours, with relative heights corresponding to densities 14, 20, 30, 24 and 12.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-column table lists intervals 0<t≤2, 2<t≤4, 4<t≤5, 5<t≤6 and 6<t≤9. Only the first frequency, 28, is printed; the other four cells are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Use the first bar and frequency 28 to calibrate density 14; the remaining bar densities are 20, 30, 24 and 12.
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE. Complete the frequency column with 28, 40, 30, 24 and 36.

title: Lower bound of a formula
body:
\(k=\dfrac{t}{a-h}\)
\(t=14\) correct to 2 significant figures
\(a=7.8\) correct to 2 significant figures
\(h=3.4\) correct to 2 significant figures Work out the lower bound for the value of \(k\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Relevant bounds include \(13.5\le t<14.5\), \(7.75\le a<7.85\), and \(3.35\le h<3.45\).
Note: B1 for sight of a correct upper or lower bound. accept 3.449 for 3.45 or 7.849 for 7.85 or 14.49 recurring for 14.5.

title: Minimum speed from displacement
body:
A particle \(P\) is moving along a straight line.
The fixed point \(O\) lies on the line. At time \(t\) seconds \((t\geq0)\), the displacement of \(P\) from \(O\) is \(s\) metres where \(s=t^3-9t^2+33t-6\) Find the minimum speed of \(P\).
markscheme: Note: Award for at least two correctly differentiated terms.
Acceleration \(dv/dt=6t-18\), or complete the square for v.
Set \(6t-18=0\), giving \(t=3\); equivalently identify the vertex at t = 3.

title: Arithmetic sequence from a sum condition
body:
The \(n\)th term of an arithmetic series is \(u_n\) where \(u_n>0\) for all \(n\)
The sum to \(n\) terms of the series is \(S_n\) Given that \(u_4=6\) and that \(S_{11}=(u_6)^2+18\) find the value of \(u_{20}\)
markscheme: Substitute one relation into the other to form an equation in a single variable.
Note: dep on both preceding method marks.

title: Perpendicular bisector in coordinates
body:
\(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle with \(AB=AC\). \(B\) is the point with coordinates \((-1,5)\)
\(C\) is the point with coordinates \((2,10)\)
\(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\). Find an equation of the line through the points \(A\) and \(M\).
Give your answer in the form \(py+qx=r\) where \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\) are integers.
markscheme: Because \(AB=AC\), A lies on the perpendicular bisector, whose gradient is \(-\dfrac35\).

title: Average train speed
body:
A train takes 6 hours 39 minutes to travel from New Delhi to Kanpur.
The train travels a distance of 429 km. Work out the average speed of the train.
Give your answer in km/h correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: \(6\text{ hrs }39\text{ mins}=6.65\text{ hrs}\) or \(6\dfrac{39}{60}\) or \(6\dfrac{13}{20}\) or \(\dfrac{133}{20}\) or 399 mins
Note: Use of \(S=D\div T\) (use of their time in hours). allow \(429\div6.39\) if B0 awarded.

title: A set with given statistics
body:
Ava writes down five whole numbers.

For these five numbers

the median is 7

the mode is 8

the range is 5

Find a possible value for each of the five numbers that Ava writes down.
markscheme: Note: If B3 not awarded, award B2 for a list of 5 numbers with 2 of: median of 7, mode of 8, range of 5. Award B1 for a list of 5 or 6 numbers with 1 of: median of 7, mode of 8, range of 5.

title: Profit and sale price
parts:
Gladys buys a table for $465 to sell in her shop. She sells the table for $520 Work out the percentage profit that Gladys makes from the sale of the table.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Gladys has a sale in her shop. She decreases all the normal prices by 12%
The normal price of an armchair was $550 Work out the sale price of the armchair.

title: Regions defined by inequalities
parts:
(i) On the grid, draw and label the straight line with equation \(x=1.5\) (ii) On the grid, draw and label the straight line with equation \(y=x\)
(iii) On the grid, draw and label the straight line with equation \(x+y=6\)

Show, by shading on the grid, the region that satisfies all three of the inequalities

\(x\geq1.5\) \(y\geq x\) \(x+y\leq6\)

Label the region \(R\).
markscheme: Note: dep on B3 for correctly indicating the region \(R\). accept unlabelled or unshaded if clear. Shading can be ‘in’ or ‘out’.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank first-quadrant coordinate grid has both axes from 0 to 7. No lines or shading are printed.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw the vertical line x = 1.5, the diagonal y = x, and the descending line through (0,6) and (6,0). Mark the triangular common region to the right of x = 1.5, above y = x and below x + y = 6 as R.

title: Algebraic manipulation and inequalities
parts:
Given that \(\dfrac{y^5\times y^n}{y^6}=y^{13}\)

work out the value of \(n\).

(i) Solve the inequality \(7t-8<2t+7\)

(ii) On the number line below, represent the solution set of the inequality solved in part (c)(i)
markscheme: Note: allow three correct terms or all four terms condoning incorrect signs.
Apply an index law or form the exponent equation \(5+n-6=13\).
Note: Allow an incorrect inequality sign or an equation at the method stage.
An open circle at 3 with a line and arrow to the left.
Note: B1ft; ft their inequality. allow a line without an arrow if it reaches to at least −5; with an arrow it can be any length.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A horizontal number line is labelled at consecutive integers from −5 to 5, with no solution marked.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Put an open circle at 3 and draw the solution ray to the left.

title: Zero index and standard form
parts:
Work out \(\dfrac{9.6\times10^{141}+6.4\times10^{140}}{3.2\times10^{16}}\)

Give your answer in standard form.
markscheme: Rewrite to a common power, for example \(9.6\times10^{141}+0.64\times10^{141}=10.24\times10^{141}\).

title: Missing value from a mean
body:
There are 5 cocoa pods in a bag.
The mean weight of the 5 cocoa pods is 398 grams. A sixth cocoa pod is put into the bag.
The mean weight of the 6 cocoa pods is 401 grams. Work out the weight of the sixth cocoa pod that is put into the bag.
markscheme: Total of five \(=5(398)=1990\), or total of six \(=6(401)=2406\).

title: Shaded area in a circle
body:
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\). \(AOC\) is a diameter of the circle. \(AB=8\) cm \(BC=15\) cm Angle \(ABC=90^\circ\) Work out the total area of the regions shown shaded in the diagram.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A full circle with centre O has AC as a diameter passing through O. Point B lies on the circle, with chords AB = 8 cm and BC = 15 cm meeting at a right angle at B. The whole region of the circle outside triangle ABC is shaded, i.e. the half-disc on the far side of AC together with the two segments cut off by chords AB and BC. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: LCM in prime-factor form
body:
\(A=2^3\times3^2\times5^2\times11\)
\(B=2^4\times3\times5^4\times13\)
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of \(A\) and \(B\).
Give your answer as a product of powers of prime numbers.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for 12 870 000, a correct unsimplified product, at least one correct variable exponent in \(2^m3^n5^p\times11\times13\), or \(2^4\times3^2\times5^4\).

title: Full-time employees
body:
The people working for a company work in Team A or in Team B. number of people in Team A : number of people in Team B = 3 : 4 \(\dfrac45\) of Team A work full time.
24% of Team B work full time. Work out what fraction of the people working for the company work full time.
Give your fraction in its simplest form.
markscheme: \(\dfrac45\times\dfrac37=\dfrac{12}{35}\) oe or \(0.24\times\dfrac47=\dfrac{96}{700}\) oe, or \(\dfrac45\times3=2.4\) and \(0.24\times4=0.96\), or scaled totals oe.
Note: or 0.48 or 48% or correct unsimplified fraction eg \(\dfrac{84}{175}\).

title: Negative power of a monomial
body: Simplify fully \(\left(\dfrac{9t^4w^9}{18t^6w^{10}}\right)^{-2}\)
markscheme: Fully correct cancellation of any two parts of their fraction at any stage of working; M1 indep.
Correctly apply the negative power to the whole of their bracket, or correctly square all parts or terms, or correctly apply the negative power and square at least two parts; M1 indep.
Note: allow \((2t^2w)^2\) after the correct answer. ALTERNATIVE: M2 for 2 correct terms; M1 for 1 correct term.

title: Interquartile range
body:
15 people were asked how long, in minutes, they had been waiting for a bus. Here are the results.
2 3 3 4 5 6 6 8 9 10 11 13 14 15 18
Find the interquartile range of these times.

title: Angles in a circle
body:
\(P\), \(Q\), \(R\), \(S\) and \(T\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\).

\(QOS\) is a diameter of the circle.

angle \(POS=124^\circ\) angle \(PRS=m^\circ\) angle \(PTS=n^\circ\)
parts:
(i) Find the value of \(m\)

(ii) Find the value of \(n\)
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle contains points P upper-left, T upper-right, Q lower-left, S lower-right and R at the bottom. Diameter QS passes through centre O. Radii OP and OS form central angle POS = 124 degrees. Chords needed for angles PRS = m and PTS = n are drawn. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Solving and rearranging formulae
parts: Make \(c\) the subject of the formula \(p=\sqrt{\dfrac{ac+8}{3+c}}\)
markscheme: Note: oe common-denominator setup; if expanded numerator, allow one error.
Note: Allow no more than one sign error in expansion and denominator multiplication.
Note: M1ft for gathering terms in \(c\) on one side and other terms the other side; ft their equation dep on two terms in \(c\) and two other terms.

title: Histogram frequencies and probability
body:
A postman records the weight of each parcel that he delivers.

The histogram shows information about the weights of all the parcels that the postman delivered last Monday. No parcels weighed more than 6 kg.

63 of the parcels that the postman delivered last Monday each had a weight between 0.5 kg and 2 kg.
parts: Work out the total number of parcels the postman delivered last Monday.

The postman picks at random two of the records of the parcels he delivered last Monday.

Work out an estimate for the probability that each parcel weighed more than 2.25 kg.
markscheme: \(63\div1.5=42\) or a correct value written on the frequency-density scale; or 10 small squares = frequency density 10; or 10 squares = 1 parcel; or 1 big square = 2.5 parcels oe.
Note: M1 for use of area related to frequency, eg showing a correct unambiguous value on the frequency-density scale or calculating the area in some form.
Note: Accept a total-frequency method with one bar error, or an equivalent small-square area calculation.
Note: M1ft dep on M1 in (a); ft figures from (a).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A frequency-density histogram has weight from 0 to 6 kg horizontally and an unnumbered vertical scale. Five bars cover 0–0.5, 0.5–2, 2–3, 3–4 and 4–6 kg. Their areas correspond respectively to frequencies 9, 63, 24, 30 and 16; no numerical frequency-density labels are printed.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Calibrate the 0.5–2 kg bar to density 42, then read the five bar frequencies as 9, 63, 24, 30 and 16. For part (b), split the 2–3 kg bar at 2.25 kg so that three quarters of its area is included.

title: Three-set Venn diagram
body:
Some students were asked the following question. “Which of the subjects Russian \(R\), French \(F\) and German \(G\) do you study?” Of these students 4 study all three of Russian, French and German
10 study Russian and French
13 study French and German
6 study Russian and German
24 study German
11 study none of the three subjects
the number who study Russian only is twice the number who study French only. Let \(x\) be the number of students who study French only.
parts: Show all this information on the Venn diagram, giving the number of students in each appropriate subset, in terms of \(x\) where necessary.

Given that the number of students who were asked the question was 80

work out the number of these students that study Russian.
markscheme: Place 4 in the triple intersection; then pair-only regions are \(R\cap F=6\), \(F\cap G=9\), \(R\cap G=2\). German-only is \(24-(9+4+2)=9\); French-only is x, Russian-only is 2x, and outside is 11.
Note: If not B3, B2 for five or six correct sections excluding x; B1 for three or four.
Note: Follow through their completed Venn diagram.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A universal set E contains three overlapping circles labelled R, F and G. The F-only region is prelabelled x; all other regions are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Put 4 in the centre; 6 in R∩F only; 9 in F∩G only; 2 in R∩G only; 9 in G only; 2x in R only; retain x in F only; and put 11 outside all circles.

title: Surface area and angle in a prism
body:
The diagram shows a solid prism \(ABCDEFGH\). The trapezium \(ABCD\), in which \(AD\) is parallel to \(BC\), is a cross section of the prism.
The base \(ADEH\) of the prism is a horizontal plane.
\(ADEH\) and \(BCFG\) are rectangles.
The midpoint of \(BC\) is vertically above the midpoint of \(AD\) so that \(BA=CD\). \(AD=37\) cm \(GF=28\) cm \(DE=24\) cm The perpendicular distance between edges \(AD\) and \(BC\) is 20 cm.
parts: Work out the total surface area of the prism.

Calculate the size of the angle between \(AF\) and the plane \(ADEH\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: \(2\times\text{‘650’}+2\times\text{‘20.5’}\times24+37\times24+28\times24\); ft their area of trapezium; ignore incorrect areas.
Note: Require at least four correct faces; follow through their trapezium area and ignore extra incorrect face areas for this method mark.
Horizontal projection from A to the point below F has length \(\sqrt{24^2+(37-4.5)^2}=40.4\ldots\text{ cm}\), or find \(AF=\sqrt{24^2+20^2+(37-4.5)^2}=45.08\ldots\text{ cm}\).
Use \(\tan x=\dfrac{20}{40.4}\ldots\), \(\sin x=\dfrac{20}{45.08}\ldots\), or an equivalent cosine-rule statement.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. An oblique view of prism ABCDEFGH shows trapezium ABCD as the front cross-section and congruent trapezium EFGH behind it. Parallel sides AD = 37 cm and BC = 28 cm are horizontal, their perpendicular separation is 20 cm, and joining prism edges such as DE are 24 cm. The shorter side is centred above the longer side so BA = CD. Base ADEH is horizontal. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Rectangle coordinates and perimeter
body:
A rectangle \(ABCD\) is to be drawn on a centimetre grid such that \(A\) has coordinates \((-4,-2)\)
\(B\) has coordinates \((1,10)\)
\(C\) has coordinates \((19,a)\)
\(D\) has coordinates \((b,c)\)
parts: Work out the value of \(a\), the value of \(b\) and the value of \(c\).
Calculate the perimeter, in centimetres, of rectangle \(ABCD\).
markscheme: Because opposite sides are parallel, the vertical coordinate shift from B to C equals that from A to D; parallelogram coordinates give \(b=14\).
For perpendicular \(BC\), gradient \(=-\dfrac5{12}\) oe. M1 ft correct use of \(m_1m_2=-1\) for their gradient of \(AB\), or \(a=2.5\) or \(c=-9.5\).

title: Displacement when at rest
body:
A particle \(P\) is moving along a straight line.
The fixed point \(O\) lies on this line. At time \(t\) seconds where \(t\geq0\), the displacement, \(s\) metres, of \(P\) from \(O\) is given by \(s=t^3+5t^2-8t+10\) Find the displacement of \(P\) from \(O\) when \(P\) is instantaneously at rest.
Give your answer in the form \(\dfrac ab\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
markscheme: Note: Award for at least two terms differentiated correctly.
Note: their \(v=0\), dep on M1; could be implied by correct values.

Note: M1 dep on M1 for correct values of \(t\), or correct method to solve their three-term quadratic; if factorising, allow brackets giving two of three terms; if using formula or completing the square, allow one sign error and some simplification.
Note: oe but numerator and denominator must be integers.

title: Hexagon with triangular cut-out
body:
The diagram shows a shaded region \(T\) formed by removing an equilateral triangle \(PQR\) from a regular hexagon \(ABCDEF\).

The points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on \(AB\) such that \(AB=1.5\times PQ\)

Given that the area of region \(T\) is \(72\sqrt3\) cm\(^2\)

work out the length of \(PQ\).
markscheme: Note: Equivalent one-variable expressions using half-side substitutions or base-height area are allowed.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A regular hexagon ABCDEF has horizontal top side AB. Points P and Q lie on AB, and an inverted equilateral triangle PQR extends into the hexagon with vertex R below PQ. The hexagon excluding triangle PQR is shaded and labelled T. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Algebraic fractions
body:
Write \(\dfrac{25x^2-64}{5x^2-13x-6}\times\dfrac{x^2-8x+15}{5x+8}-(x-7)\) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: M2 for factorising at least two quadratics correctly; if not M2 then M1 for factorising at least one of the three quadratics correctly.
Cancel to \(\dfrac{(5x-8)(x-5)}{5x+2}\), then use common denominator: \(\dfrac{(5x-8)(x-5)-(x-7)(5x+2)}{5x+2}\).
Note: M1 indep, ft if M2 awarded; for writing the fractions over a common denominator, with or without brackets removed.

title: Sector and triangle perimeters
body:
The diagram shows a sector \(OBC\) of a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \((6+x)\) cm. \(A\) is the point on \(OB\) and \(D\) is the point on \(OC\) such that \(OA=OD=6\) cm Angle \(BOC=50^\circ\) Given that the perimeter of sector \(OBC\) = 2 × the perimeter of triangle \(OAD\) find the value of \(x\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: condone missing brackets around \((6+x)\) for this mark only.
Note: M1 dep on M3 for a correct equation for \(x\).
Collect and isolate the x terms in the correct equation.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Sector OBC has centre O, radius 6 + x cm and central angle 50 degrees. Points A and D lie on radii OB and OC with OA = OD = 6 cm, and chord AD forms isosceles triangle OAD. The radial portions AB and DC are each x cm. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Core algebra skills
parts: Work out the value of \(w\) when \(y=-2\)
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for \(p(8p-2)\), \(2(4p^2-p)\), or the correct full factor with one bracket term correct.
Note: If not B2, B1 for either term correct.
Note: allow four correct terms ignoring signs, or three correct terms with correct signs, or \(5x^2+18x+...\), or \(...+18x-8\).

title: Rectangle outside a semicircle
body:
The diagram shows a rectangle \(ABCD\) and a semicircle with diameter \(AB\) where \(AB=12\) cm. The point \(E\) lies on \(DC\) and also on the semicircle. Work out the area of the shaded region.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: M1 dep M1 for a complete method.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Rectangle ABCD has horizontal side AB = 12 cm and height equal to the radius of a semicircle with diameter AB. The arc rises to touch the opposite side DC at E. The portions of the rectangle outside the semicircle are shaded. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Set operations
parts:
(i) List the members of the set \(A\cap B\)

(ii) List the members of the set \(A'\)

\(C=\{23,25,29\}\)
Using set notation, find an expression for \(C\) in terms of \(A\) and \(B\).
markscheme: \((A\cup B)'\) or \(A'\cap B'\) or \((B\cup A)'\) or \(B'\cap A'\).

title: Index laws
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for 81 or \(k^8\) in the final answer.
Note: If not B2, B1 for \(7m^4\) or \(n^6\) in a product with no other m or n terms.

title: Transformations on grids
parts:
On the grid, rotate shape \(P\) \(180^\circ\) about the point \((-3,2)\)
Label the new shape \(Q\).

On the grid, translate shape \(P\) by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}10\\8\end{pmatrix}\)
Label the new shape \(R\).

Here are triangle \(T\) and triangle \(U\) drawn on a grid of squares.

Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle \(T\) onto triangle \(U\).
markscheme: Note: If not B2, B1 for a congruent image in the correct orientation but wrong position, or for two or three correct vertices.
Note: accept enlargement, enlarge, etc so long as no mention of rotation, reflection or translation; centre \((-3,3)\), accept about/from with no mention of line or column vector.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Grid with x from −10 to 14 and y from −8 to 10, ruled every 1 and numbered every 2. Shape P is the shaded quadrilateral (−3,−5), (0,−2), (3,−2), (3,−5); no image shapes are drawn.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE, part (c). A separate grid with x from −4 to 12 and y from 0 to 7, ruled and numbered every 1. Triangle T has vertices (1,2), (1,4), (4,2) and triangle U has vertices (5,1), (5,5), (11,1). Both shaded. No construction lines or centre are marked.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw Q through (−9,6), (−9,9), (−3,9), (−6,6), joining in corresponding order, and label it Q. Draw R through (7,3), (10,6), (13,6), (13,3), joining in corresponding order, and label it R.
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE. If illustrating part (c), draw rays through corresponding vertices of T and U back to the enlargement centre (−3,3); U has scale factor 2 from T.

title: Reverse percentage price
body:
On Wednesday, the price of 1 litre of petrol was £1.26
The price of petrol on Wednesday was 5% more than the price of petrol on the previous Monday. Calculate the price of 30 litres of petrol on the previous Monday.
markscheme: Note: cao. If no marks awarded, SC B1 for one operation used correctly, even with another incorrect operation, eg \(1.26\times0.95\times30\) oe.

title: Inequalities from a region
body:
The shaded region \(R\), shown in the diagram below, is bounded by the straight line with equation \(y=3x-2\) and by two other straight lines.

Write down the three inequalities that define region \(R\).
markscheme: Note: allow \(1\leq y\leq7\) and \(1\leq x\leq3\). Condone strict signs throughout. SC B1 if no marks awarded for recognition of \(x=3\) and \(y=1\); allow incorrect inequality and condone equals signs.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. On coordinate axes, region R is a triangle bounded below by horizontal line y = 1, on the right by vertical line x = 3, and on the left/above by the rising line y = 3x − 2. The triangular region is shaded.

title: Ocean coastlines in standard form
body:
The table gives the length of the coastline, in kilometres, of each of five oceans.
OceanLength of coastline (km)
Arctic\(4.539\times10^4\)
Atlantic\(1.119\times10^5\)
Pacific\(1.357\times10^5\)
Indian\(6.653\times10^4\)
Southern\(1.797\times10^4\)
parts: Which ocean has the greatest length of coastline?

Calculate the difference between the length of the Atlantic Ocean’s coastline and the length of the Southern Ocean’s coastline.
Give your answer in standard form.

title: Solving a quadratic
body:
Solve \(x^2-21x+20=0\)
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Find factors or use a valid quadratic method, for example seek \((x\pm20)(x\pm1)\).
\((x-20)(x-1)=0\), or a correctly processed formula/completing-square expression.
Note: A1 dep on first M1 with no incorrect working.

title: Missing frequency from estimated mean
body:
A mathematics teacher at a school asked a group of students how far, in kilometres, each student had travelled to get to school that day. The table gives information about their answers.
Distance travelled (\(d\) km)Number of students
\(0\(x\)
\(211
\(48
\(66
\(85
The teacher calculated that an estimate for the mean distance travelled by the whole group of students was 4.25 km. Work out the value of \(x\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: allow one numerical product error, with intention to add.
Note: M1 dep M1 for correct equation, ft their known total.
Note: A1 dep first M1. Alternative: let total pupils be \(y\), form \(4.25y=160+[y-(11+8+6+5)]\) oe, then \(y=40\), \(x=10\).

title: Perimeter of a major sector
body:
A circle centre \(O\) has radius 9 cm. Calculate the perimeter of the shaded sector of the circle.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Major arc \(=\dfrac{320}{360}\times2\pi(9)=16\pi=50.26\ldots\), equivalently circumference minus the minor arc.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle of radius 9 cm has two radii enclosing a 40-degree minor sector. The complementary major sector is shaded. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Simultaneous linear equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations
\(2x+7y=17\)
\(5x+3y=-1\)
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Eliminate one variable, for example \(10x+35y=85\) and \(10x+6y=-2\), then subtract to get \(29y=87\).
Note: allow an oe isolation/substitution method; condone one arithmetic error.
Substitute the found value into either original equation, or correctly eliminate the second unknown.
Note: Accuracy marks depend on the first method mark.

title: Height from angle of depression
body:
The diagram shows two hot air balloons.
\(A\) is a point on the base of one of the balloons and \(B\) is a point on the base of the other balloon. The distance between \(A\) and \(B\) is 500 metres.
The angle of depression of \(B\) from \(A\) is \(23^\circ\) Calculate the vertical height of \(A\) above \(B\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: A correct expression involving height \(h\), eg \(\sin23^\circ=\dfrac{h}{500}\) oe, or cosine/Pythagoras route oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Points A and B lie on horizontal bases of two balloons, with A higher and left of B. Segment AB is labelled 500 m. A horizontal dashed line through A and the downward sightline AB enclose an angle of depression of 23 degrees. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Equal annual percentage increases
body:
Simon bought a house at the beginning of 2018
The value of Simon’s house had decreased by 15% by the end of 2018 The house increased in value during both 2019 and 2020
The percentage increases in the value of the house during 2019 and 2020 were the same. The value of Simon’s house at the end of 2020 was 2.85% greater than the amount he paid for his house at the beginning of 2018 Calculate the percentage increase in the value of the house during 2019
markscheme: Let annual multiplier be \(x\): \(0.85x^2=1.0285\) or \(85x^2=102.85\) oe.
Note: M2 for a correct equation or division; if not, M1 for sight of 0.85 or 1.0285.
Let the percentage be y and form \(0.85(1+y/100)^2=1.0285\), equivalently \((1+y/100)^2=1.21\).
\(1+y/100=1.10\), or correctly solve the resulting quadratic.

title: Proof that odd times odd is odd
body: Prove algebraically that the product of any two odd numbers is always an odd number.
markscheme: Represent two different odd numbers, for example \((2m+1)(2n+1)\).
Note: M2 requires different variables and two odd expressions. If not, M1 for a product of odd expressions using the same variable.

title: Venn diagram probabilities
body:
Two events \(A\) and \(B\) are such that \(n(A)=62\), \(n(B)=30\) and \(n(A\cup B)=68\)

Given that \(n(E)=80\)
parts: complete the Venn diagram to show the number of elements in each region.

An element is chosen at random from \(E\). Using the Venn diagram, find the probability that this element is in
(i) \(A\cap B\)
(ii) \(A\cup B'\)
markscheme: Regions are A-only 38, intersection 24, B-only 6 and outside 12.
Note: If not B2, B1 for two or three correct values in their correct regions.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A universal set E contains two overlapping circles A and B. All four region values are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Put 38 in A only, 24 in the intersection, 6 in B only and 12 outside both circles.

title: Functions and inverse functions
body:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined as
\(f(x)=x^2+6\)
\(g(x)=x-10\)
parts:
Solve the equation \(fg(x)=f(x)\)
Show clear algebraic working.

The function \(h\) is defined as \(h(x)=\dfrac{2x-4}{x}\)

State the value of \(x\) that cannot be included in the domain of \(h\)
Express the inverse function \(h^{-1}\) in the form \(h^{-1}(x)=...\)

title: Equation with algebraic fractions
body:
Solve the equation
\(\dfrac5{x+2}+\dfrac3{x^2+2x}=2\)
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Factorise \(x^2+2x=x(x+2)\) in a correct expression on the left, or write the two fractions over a common denominator.
\((2x-3)(x+1)=0\); M1ft indep for solving their three-term quadratic.
Note: if factorising, allow brackets giving two of three terms; formula or completing square may have one sign error and some simplification.
Note: oe dep on M3. Alternative: \(\dfrac{5(x^2+2x)+3(x+2)}{(x^2+2x)(x+2)}=2\) oe, giving \(2x^3+3x^2-5x-6=0\), \((x+1)(2x-3)(x+2)=0\); do not award A1 if extra solution \(-2\) is given.

title: Powers of two
parts:
Simplify \(8^2\times\sqrt[3]{4^6}\)
Give your answer in the form \(2^a\) where \(a\) is an integer.
Show each stage of your working clearly.

Given that \(n^{-\frac45}=\left(\dfrac12\right)^4\) where \(n>0\)

find the value of \(n\).
markscheme: Note: isw if \(2^{10}\) is obtained and then only 10 is written.
Note: If not M2, M1 for one correct algebraic stage such as \(n^{-1/5}=\dfrac12\).

title: Radius from a segment area
body:
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\). Angle \(ABC=75^\circ\) The area of the shaded segment is 200 cm\(^2\) Calculate the radius of the circle.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: M1 dep first M1; require complete triangle-area method in \(r\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle with centre O has points A and C on the lower-left and lower-right circumference and B at the top. Chords BA and BC form angle ABC = 75 degrees. Chord AC and the minor arc AC below it enclose the minor segment, which is shaded. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Bead probability equation
body:
A bag contains \(n\) beads.
6 of the beads are red and the rest are blue. Ravi is going to take at random 2 beads from the bag. The probability that the 2 beads will be of the same colour is \(\dfrac9{17}\)
Using algebra, and showing each stage of your working, calculate the value of \(n\).
markscheme: Use both products and no others: \(\dfrac6n\dfrac5{n-1}+\dfrac{n-6}{n}\dfrac{n-7}{n-1}\).
Note: allow oe ordered red-blue complement equation.
Note: allow any correct quadratic method; if factorising, allow brackets giving two of three terms; formula/completing square may have one sign error and partial simplification.
Note: cao dep M3; do not accept the non-integer solution as an additional answer.

title: Angle between a line and a plane
body:
\(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle in a horizontal plane.
The point \(T\) is vertically above \(B\). Angle \(ABC=140^\circ\)
\(AB=BC=8\) cm
\(TB=10\) cm
\(M\) is the midpoint of \(AC\). Calculate the size of the angle between \(MT\) and the horizontal plane \(ABC\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: A correct expression involving MB or MB² is required.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Isosceles triangle ABC lies in a horizontal plane with AB = BC = 8 cm, base AC, angle ABC = 140 degrees and midpoint M on AC. Point T is vertically above B with TB = 10 cm. Segments MT and TB are drawn. Print “Diagram NOT accurately drawn”.

title: Average speed with mixed time units
body:
A plane flew from Madrid to Dubai. The distance the plane flew was 5658 km.
The flight time was 8 hours 12 minutes. Work out the average speed of the plane.
markscheme: Note: For use of speed = distance ÷ time (use of their time in hours – if used minutes, then must multiply by 60). Allow \(5658\div8.12\) for this mark if B0 awarded (allow 696–697).

title: Arithmetic sequence nth term
body:
Here are the first 4 terms of an arithmetic sequence.
85 79 73 67
Find an expression, in terms of \(n\), for the \(n\)th term of the sequence.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, award B1 for \(-6n+k\), where \(k\) may be zero or absent.
Note: For a correct answer in any form, e.g. \(91-6\times n\), \(-6n+91\) or \(85+(n-1)(-6)\), oe. Award full marks for e.g. \(x=91-6n\) or nth term \(=91-6n\), but only B1 for \(n=91-6n\).

title: Area of an irregular pentagon
body:
The diagram shows the shape \(ABCDE\).

The area of the shape is 91.8 cm\(^2\)

Work out the value of \(x\).
markscheme: A correct component area, for example \(8x\), \(14x\), \(6x\), \(\dfrac12(14-8)(13-x)=39-3x\), or \(11x\).
A complete area expression, for example \(14x+\dfrac12\times6(13-x)\), \(11x+39\), or \(182-(143-11x)\).
A fully correct equation, for example \(11x+39=91.8\).

Note: The second M1 is ft from a correct working expression for the total area of the shape, with no parts omitted or duplicated. The third M1 is for a fully correct equation with no fractions and no brackets.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Irregular pentagon ABCDE, not to scale. AB is horizontal at the top and labelled x cm; BC is vertical downward and labelled 8 cm; CD slopes down to the right; DE is horizontal left and labelled 13 cm; EA is vertical upward and labelled 14 cm. Right-angle markers are shown at A, B and E. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Combining ratios
body:
On a farm there are chickens, ducks and pigs. The ratio of the number of chickens to the number of ducks is 7 : 2
The ratio of the number of ducks to the number of pigs is 5 : 9
There are 36 pigs on the farm. Work out the number of chickens on the farm.
markscheme: Note: For a correct calculation to find the number of chickens. Award M2 for \(70:20:36\), or a different order if the intention is clear, e.g. by labels.

title: Algebraic manipulation and indices
parts: Make \(t\) the subject of the formula \(p=at-d\).
Given that \(\dfrac{w^5\times w^n}{w^3}=w^{10}\), work out the value of \(n\).
markscheme: Note: For part (a), expansion must show, for example, \(6x^2\), not just \(3x\times2x\). For part (c), trial and error gains full marks if correct and no marks if incorrect unless a rule of indices is clearly shown.

title: Biased spinner probabilities
body:
Grace has a biased 5-sided spinner. Grace is going to spin the arrow on the spinner once. The table below gives the probabilities that the spinner will land on red or on blue or on green.
ColourRedBlueGreenOrangePink
Probability0.200.120.08
The probability that the spinner will land on orange is 3 times the probability that the spinner will land on pink.
parts: Work out the probability that the spinner will land on orange.

Grace spins the arrow on the spinner 150 times.

Work out an estimate for the number of times the spinner lands on blue.
markscheme: Note: For part (a), sight of \(0.15\) in the table for Orange or Pink, or \(0.45\) for Pink, gains M2. If no answer is on the answer line, check the correct space in the table; a value on the answer line takes precedence.

title: Integer and linear inequalities
parts: \(-4\leq2y<6\). The value of \(y\) is an integer. Write down all the possible values of \(y\).
Solve the inequality \(7t-3\leq2t+31\). Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: B1 for four correct values and no incorrect values, or six values with no more than one incorrect value.
Note: For part (b), condone \(=\) rather than \(\leq\), or any other sign, for M1. The A1 is dep on M1 and the correct sign must be on the answer line.

title: Population calculations in standard form
body:
The table shows the populations of five countries.
CountryPopulation
China\(1.4\times10^9\)
Germany\(8.2\times10^7\)
Sweden\(9.9\times10^6\)
Fiji\(9.1\times10^5\)
Malta\(4.3\times10^5\)
parts: Work out the difference between the population of China and the population of Germany. Give your answer in standard form.

Given that \(\text{population of Fiji}=\dfrac1k\times\text{population of Sweden}\)
work out the value of \(k\).
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
markscheme: Note: For part (a), allow \(1.32\times10^9\) or \(1.3\times10^9\). For part (b), SC: if M1 is not scored, award B1 for an answer of \(\dfrac1{11}\).

title: Factorising and solving by expansion
markscheme: Note: If not B2, award B1 for a correct partial factorisation containing at least two of the numerical, \(a\), and \(c\) factors.

title: Required mark for a target mean
body:
Jethro has sat 5 tests.
Each test was marked out of 100 and Jethro’s mean mark for the 5 tests is 74 Jethro has to sit one more test that is also to be marked out of 100 Jethro wants his mean mark for all 6 tests to be at least 77 Work out the least mark that Jethro needs to get for the last test.
markscheme: Note: M2 may be awarded for \(74+(3\times6)\), or \(77+(3\times5)\), oe, where \(3=77-74\). Trial and error scores no marks unless correct, when it gains full marks.

title: Equations involving indices
markscheme: Note: For part (a), A1 is dependent on M1. For part (b), A1 is dep on M1, as working is required.

title: Arc length of a sector
body:
The diagram shows a sector of a circle with radius 7 cm. Work out the length of the arc of the sector.
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: Students may use \(\pi\), \(3.14\), \(3.142\) or \(\dfrac{22}{7}\). Accept answers in the range 6.05–6.2.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A sector of a circle, not to scale, with central angle 50 degrees and one radius labelled 7 cm. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Expanding three algebraic factors
body: Expand and simplify \(4x(3x+1)(2x-3)\). Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Correctly expand two of the three factors, allowing one error.
Expand by the third factor, follow through, allowing one error.
Note: The second M1 is dep and ft for expanding by the third factor, allowing one error. isw a correct factorisation, but do not isw an incorrect simplification.

title: Interquartile range from a list
body:
Here is the number of goals that Henri’s team scored one summer in each water polo match.
5 8 9 11 13 13 14 15 16 17 20
Find the interquartile range of the numbers of goals.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: The values 9 and 16 must be clearly identified, either in a list or stated. A second 13 may also be shown, provided it is not intended as the lower or upper quartile. A1 is dep on M1.

title: Circle theorem angle with a tangent
body:
\(P\), \(Q\) and \(R\) are points on a circle, centre \(O\).
\(TRV\) is the tangent to the circle at \(R\). Reflex angle \(POR=238^\circ\)
Angle \(QRV=60^\circ\) Calculate the size of angle \(OPQ\).
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
markscheme: A correct intermediate angle, for example \(\text{ORQ}=30^\circ\), \(\text{OQR}=30^\circ\), \(\text{PQR}=61^\circ\), \(\text{QPR}=60^\circ\), or \(\text{OPR}=29^\circ\).
Fully correct reasons for the method used.

Note: If not B2, award B1 dependent on M1 for at least one correct reason. Accept: angle between tangent and radius is \(90^\circ\); angles around a point total \(360^\circ\); angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference; angles in a triangle total \(180^\circ\); base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal; or the alternate segment theorem.
Note: B2 is dep on a fully correct method that should lead to the answer. B1 is dep on M1 for at least one reason for the method used.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle with centre O and points P at lower left, Q at top and R at lower right on the circumference. Chords PQ and QR and radii OP and OR are drawn. The reflex angle POR is marked 238 degrees. A tangent line T-R-V runs from lower left through R to upper right, and angle QRV between chord RQ and the tangent ray RV is marked 60 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Recurring decimal as a fraction
body: Use algebra to show that \(0.28\dot1\dot3=\dfrac{557}{1980}\).
markscheme: Let \(x=0.281313\ldots\). Form two recurring decimals whose subtraction terminates, for example \(100x=28.1313\ldots\) and \(x=0.281313\ldots\), with the intention to subtract.
Note: This is a ‘use algebra to show that’ question, so algebra and all stages of working must be seen to award full marks.

title: Proof with consecutive even numbers
body: Using algebra, prove that, given any 3 consecutive even numbers, the difference between the square of the largest number and the square of the smallest number is always 8 times the middle number.
markscheme: Represent three consecutive even numbers, for example \(2n,2n+2,2n+4\).
Square the largest and smallest and subtract: \((2n+4)^2-(2n)^2=16n+16\).
Let \(a<b<c\) be consecutive even numbers, with \(a+c=2b\) and \(c-a=4\).
Note: SCB1 for \((p+4)^2-p^2\). SCB2 for \((p+4)^2-p^2=8p+16=8(p+2)\), and M2A1 if the student also states that it is true for all numbers, so it must be true for even numbers, oe.

title: Histogram and estimated probability
body:
The table and histogram give information about the distance travelled, in order to get to work, by each person working in a large store.
Distance (\(d\) km)Frequency
\(0\leq d<10\)40
\(10\leq d<15\)
\(15\leq d<20\)
\(20\leq d<30\)
\(30\leq d<60\)30
parts: Using the information in the table and in the histogram, complete the table.

One of the people working in the store is chosen at random.

Work out an estimate for the probability that the distance travelled by this person, in order to get to work, was greater than 25 km.
markscheme: Use frequency density, with area proportional to frequency; for example identify the first bar's frequency density as 4, or obtain two correct missing frequencies.
Draw the bar for \(30\leq d<60\) with the correct width and frequency density 1.
Note: For part (c), M1 is ft from their stated value for \(20\leq d<30\), for a total greater than 25, or ft their three values in the table. A1ft is dep on a completed table.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A histogram on a square grid with horizontal axis Distance travelled (km) from 0 to 60, labelled every 10. The vertical axis is Frequency density and has no numbered scale except 0. Printed bars cover 0 to 10, 10 to 15, 15 to 20, and 20 to 30, with respective frequency densities 4, 7, 7.8 and 5.6. There is no printed bar from 30 to 60.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Add a bar spanning 30 to 60 with frequency density 1.

title: Counting Venn diagram regions
body:
The Venn diagram shows a universal set, \(E\) and sets \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\).

12, 5, 9, 10, 6, 3, 4 and 8 represent the numbers of elements.
parts:
(i) Find \(n(A\cup B)\)
(ii) Find \(n(A'\cap B')\)
(iii) Find \(n([A\cap B]\cup C)\)
markscheme: Note: Award one independent B1 for each of \(45\), \(12\) and \(28\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A rectangle labelled universal set E contains a three-circle Venn diagram. A is the left circle, B the right circle and C the lower circle. Region counts are: A only 12; B only 9; C only 4; A intersection B only 5; A intersection C only 10; B intersection C only 3; all three 6; outside all circles 8.

title: Upper bound of a quotient
body: \(P=\dfrac{t-w}{y}\), where \(t=9.7\) correct to 1 decimal place, \(w=5.9\) correct to 1 decimal place, and \(y=3\) correct to 1 significant figure. Calculate the upper bound for \(P\). Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: For M1 use \(\dfrac{UB_t-LB_w}{LB_y}\), where \(9.7

title: Substitution into an algebraic fraction
body: Given that \(x=\dfrac{5}{9y+5}\) and that \(y=\dfrac{5}{5a-2}\), find an expression for \(x\) in terms of \(a\). Give your expression as a single fraction in its simplest form.
markscheme: Note: Do not isw if the student has tried incorrect cancelling; for example \(x=\dfrac{5a-2}{7+5a}=\dfrac{-2}{7}\) gets M3A0.

title: Angle between a line and a plane
body:
The diagram shows a triangular prism \(ABCDEF\) with a horizontal base \(ABEF\). \(AC=BC=FD=ED=12\) cm \(AB=10\) cm \(BE=15\) cm Calculate the size of the angle between \(AD\) and the base \(ABEF\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Let M be the midpoint of EF. Find two of \(AM=\sqrt{5^2+15^2}=\sqrt{250}\), \(AD=\sqrt{12^2+15^2}=\sqrt{369}\), and \(DM=\sqrt{12^2-5^2}=\sqrt{119}\).
Note: If not M2, award M1 for a complete method to find one of AM, AD or DM.
Note: Other longer methods may be used but must be complete. Use \(10\div2\) as 5 throughout. For the final M1, the followed-through values must come from correct working.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A triangular prism ABCDEF, not to scale, with congruent triangular ends ABC and FDE. Base quadrilateral ABEF is horizontal. AB is labelled 10 cm and BE is labelled 15 cm. AC = BC = FD = ED = 12 cm. Hidden base edges AF and FD are dashed; AD is not drawn. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. A valid working diagram may add M as the midpoint of EF and draw AM, DM and AD to show the right triangle used for the angle between AD and the base.

title: Number of terms in an arithmetic series
body:
The sum of the first \(N\) terms of an arithmetic series, \(S\), is 292
The 2nd term of \(S\) is 8.5
The 5th term of \(S\) is 13 Find the value of \(N\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Solve the resulting quadratic, for example \(3N^2+25N-1168=0\), by a correct method.
Note: The quadratic-solving M1 is dep on the previous M1. Allow one sign error and some simplification in a correct method. The final A1 is dep on M2.

title: Composite and inverse functions
body:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined as \(f(x)=5x^2-10x+7\) where \(x\geq1\)
\(g(x)=7x-6\)
parts: Express the inverse function in the form \(f^{-1}(x)=\ldots\).
markscheme: Note: The positive root is required because the domain of \(f\) is \(x\geq1\).
Note: For part (b), the answer must be in terms of \(x\). \(f^{-1}(x)=1\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{x-2}{5}}\) gains 3 marks.

title: Area of overlap of two circles
body:
The diagram shows two circles such that the region \(R\), shown shaded in the diagram, is the region common to both circles. One of the circles has centre \(O\) and radius 5 cm.
The other circle has centre \(P\) and radius 4 cm.
Angle \(AOB=50^\circ\) Calculate the area of region \(R\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Subtract the two triangles from the two sectors: \(10.908\ldots-\dfrac12(5)(5)\sin50^\circ+8.904\ldots-\dfrac12(4)(4)\sin63.77\ldots^\circ\).
Note: For the second M1, other methods may be used but must give a complete method for angle APB or angle OPA. For the fourth M1, \(2\times31.88\ldots=63.77\ldots\). Allow 3–3.1 for A1.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two intersecting circles, not to scale, with the larger circle centred O on the left and radius 5 cm, and the smaller circle centred P on the right and radius 4 cm. They intersect at A above and B below. Radii OA, OB, PA and PB are drawn. The common lens-shaped region R is shaded. Angle AOB is marked 50 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Intersection of diagonals in a trapezium
body:
\(OACB\) is a trapezium. \(\overrightarrow{OA}=2\mathbf a\) \(\overrightarrow{OB}=5\mathbf b\) \(\overrightarrow{AC}=3\mathbf b\) The diagonals, \(OC\) and \(AB\), of the trapezium intersect at the point \(P\).
Find and simplify an expression, in terms of \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\), for \(\overrightarrow{OP}\)
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Equate coefficients and form an equation in one scalar, for example \(5m=3n\) and \(n=1-m\).
Note: Working is required. The final A1 is dep on M1, and the terms in \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\) must be simplified.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Trapezium OACB, not to scale, with O at lower left, A at upper left, C at upper right and B at lower right. AC and OB are horizontal and parallel. Diagonals OC and AB cross at P. Vector OA is labelled 2a, OB is labelled 5b and AC is labelled 3b. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Prime factor decomposition
body:
Write 600 as a product of powers of its prime factors.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: At least two correct factorisation stages producing two prime factors, for example \(600=2\times300=2\times2\times150\).
Note: Working is required and the answer must be given as a product of powers of prime factors. A1 is dep on M2; factors may be in any order.

title: Division of mixed numbers
body: Show that \(2\dfrac47\div1\dfrac18=2\dfrac27\).
markscheme: Note: Use of decimals scores no marks.
Note: A1 is dep on M2 for the conclusion \(2\dfrac27\) from correct working. Use of decimals scores no marks.

title: Reverse bearing
body:
The bearing of Paris from London is \(149^\circ\)

Work out the bearing of London from Paris.
markscheme: Note: Working is not required, so the correct answer scores full marks.

title: Set operations with letters
body:
\(E=\{\text{letters of the alphabet}\}\)
\(B=\{b,r,a,z,i,l\}\)
\(I=\{i,r,e,l,a,n,d\}\)
parts:
List the members of the set
(i) \(B\cup I\)
(ii) \(B\cap I'\)

\(K=\{k,e,n,y,a\}\) Cody writes down the statement \(B\cap K=\varnothing\)
Cody's statement is wrong. Explain why.
markscheme: \(\{a,b,d,e,i,l,n,r,z\}\), in any order with no repeats.
\(\{b,z\}\), in either order with no repeats.
Note: For part (a), no repeats; letters may be in any order and capital letters are condoned.
The letter \(a\) is in both sets, so \(B\cap K=\{a\}\) and the intersection is not empty.
Note: If a letter is named it must be \(a\); do not allow ‘letters’ or ‘elements’ in the plural.

title: Angles in parallel lines and a triangle
body:
\(ABCD\) and \(FGHI\) are parallel straight lines.
\(EBGJ\) and \(ECH\) are straight lines. \(BE=CE\)
Angle \(BEC=44^\circ\) Work out the size of angle \(JGH\).
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
markscheme: A method reaching an angle one step from JGH, for example \(\text{BGH}=68^\circ\) or \(\text{BGF}=112^\circ\).
Fully correct reasons for the method used.

Note: If not B2, award B1 dependent on M1 for one appropriate reason. Accept isosceles triangle, angles in a triangle total \(180^\circ\), angles on a straight line total \(180^\circ\), vertically opposite angles, corresponding angles, alternate angles, allied angles, or angles at a point.

Note: Reasons must include the stated theorem words. B1 for one correct reason appropriate to their method, dep on M1. All angles must be clearly stated as the correct angle or shown in the correct position on the diagram.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two horizontal parallel lines ABCD above and FGHI below, each labelled left to right. E is above the upper line. Straight line E-B-G-J slopes down left through both parallels; straight line E-C-H slopes down right through both. Tick marks show BE = CE and angle BEC is marked 44 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Percentage decrease from a ratio
body:
Mariana sells bags of bird food. The bags that Mariana sold last week each contained 12 kg of seeds. The bags that she is going to sell next week will each contain a mixture of nuts and seeds where for each bag weight of nuts : weight of seeds \(=4:5\) The total weight of the nuts and the seeds in each bag will be 19.35 kg The weight of seeds in each bag that Mariana sells next week will be less than the weight of seeds in each bag that Mariana sold last week. Work out this decrease as a percentage of the weight of seeds in each bag that Mariana sold last week.
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: M2 may be awarded for \(\dfrac{5\times19.35}{9}=10.75\). Accept 10.4–10.42. SCB1 for \(\dfrac59\times12\), oe.

title: Hypotenuse using sine
body:
Here is a right-angled triangle. Work out the value of \(x\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: The second M1 may be awarded for a complete Pythagoras method. If the complete statement is given with nothing before it, award M2. Accept 9.7–9.72.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A right-angled triangle, not to scale, with a horizontal base, vertical left side labelled 6.5 cm, hypotenuse sloping down to the right labelled x cm, a right-angle marker at the lower-left vertex, and the lower-right angle marked 42 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Linear simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations
\(5a+2c=10\)
\(2a-4c=7\)
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Multiply or rearrange one or both equations correctly to eliminate or substitute one variable.
Use the first value in either original equation to find the second variable.
Note: The second M1 is dep on the previous M1 but not on a correct first value. A1 is dependent on the first M1.

title: Factorising and solving a quadratic
markscheme: \((x\pm6)(x\pm4)\), with a correct factor pair identified.
\(x=-6\) or \(x=4\), following from the factors in (i).
Note: The answers in (ii) must follow through from two factors in (i), as the question says ‘Hence solve’. Award the marks wherever the working is shown, provided there is no ambiguity.

title: Volume of a triangular prism
body:
Here is a triangular prism. Work out the volume of the prism.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: A correct first step to find the perpendicular height, for example \(11.2^2-7.4^2\).

Note: SCB2, if M0, for \(0.5\times7.4\times\sqrt{11.2^2+7.4^2}\times15\). SCB1, if M0, for \(7.4\times\sqrt{11.2^2+7.4^2}\times15\), \(0.5\times7.4\times\sqrt{11.2^2+7.4^2}\), \(0.5\times7.4\times11.2\times15\), or 622. Accept 466–467.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A triangular prism, not to scale, whose triangular end faces are right triangles. On the front triangle, the base is labelled 7.4 cm and a right-angle marker shows the unlabelled height is perpendicular to it. The corresponding sloping side on the rear triangle is labelled 11.2 cm, and the prism length is labelled 15 cm. Hidden rear base and height edges are dashed. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: House values and percentages
parts:
Work out how much Chengbo paid for the house.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Zhi bought a house on 1st January 2017
When she bought the house, its value was 120 000 yuan. The value of the house increased by 1.8% per year. Work out the value of Zhi's house on 1st January 2020
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: If a correct answer is seen in working and then rounded incorrectly, award full marks. If the number of zeros is misread by one, award up to M2 for a correct method using that misread value. If no marks are awarded in (a), SCB1 for 223 200 or 223 000; in (b), SC: award M1 for \(1.054\times120000\), 126 480 or 6480.
body:
Chengbo sold a house for 180 000 yuan.

The amount for which he sold the house is 24% more than the amount he paid for the house.

title: Cumulative frequency comparison
body:
The cumulative frequency table gives information about the distance, in kilometres, that each of 80 workers travel from home to work at Office A.
Distance travelled (\(d\) km)Cumulative frequency
\(017
\(032
\(057
\(070
\(076
\(080
parts: On the grid, draw a cumulative frequency graph for the information in the table.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the median distance travelled.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the interquartile range of the distances travelled.

For Office B, the median distance workers travel from home to work is 15 km and the interquartile range is 5 km. Use the information above to compare the distances that workers at Office A and workers at Office B travel from home to work.
Write down two comparisons.
markscheme: Plot at least four cumulative-frequency points correctly at the upper class boundaries.
Plot all points correctly and join with a curve or line segments.
An estimate from the graph in the range \(10.5\) to \(12\text{ km}\).
Use cumulative frequencies 20 and 60 to read the lower and upper quartiles from the graph.
An interquartile range in the range \(8.5\) to \(11.5\text{ km}\).
Office B workers have a higher median, so they tend to travel further.
Office A has a larger interquartile range, so its workers' distances are more spread out or varied.
Note: For part (a), a bar-chart type graph scores zero. Part (b) is B1ft from an ascending cumulative-frequency graph. In part (d), to award both marks at least one comparison must be in context.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank cumulative-frequency grid with horizontal axis Distance travelled (km) from 0 to 30 in steps of 5 and vertical axis Cumulative frequency from 0 to 80 in steps of 10.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (5,17), (10,32), (15,57), (20,70), (25,76) and (30,80), optionally starting at (0,0), and join with a smooth increasing curve or line segments. Quartile reading lines may be drawn from cumulative frequencies 20, 40 and 60.

title: Independent race probabilities
body:
Emilie takes part in two races. The probability that she wins the first race is 0.7
The probability that she wins the second race is 0.4
The outcomes of the two races are independent.
parts: Work out the probability that Emilie wins exactly one of the two races.

Emilie is going to take part in a third race.

If she wins both of the first two races, the probability that she will win the third race is 0.6

If she wins exactly one of the first two races, the probability that she will win the third race is 0.3

Work out the probability that Emilie will win exactly two of the three races.
markscheme: Second-race branches \(0.6,0.4,0.6\) in the correct positions.

Note: For part (b), M marks are ft from their tree diagram with probabilities less than 1. For part (c), follow through from parts (a) and (b) on M marks only. Allow decimals, fractions or percentages with a percent sign as oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-stage probability tree. First-race branches are Emilie wins, labelled 0.7, and Emilie does not win, with a blank probability. From each branch, second-race branches lead to Emilie wins and Emilie does not win. The upper second-race winning branch is labelled 0.4; the other three second-race probabilities are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill the first-race losing branch with 0.3. For each second-race split, label winning 0.4 and not winning 0.6.

title: Negative fractional indices
body: Simplify fully \(\left(\dfrac{9x^4}{16y^{10}}\right)^{-\frac12}\).
markscheme: Note: If not B3, award B2 for two of: correct numerical factor \(\dfrac43\), \(x^2\) in the denominator, and \(y^5\) in the numerator. Award B1 for one of these, or for correctly applying either the reciprocal or square root to at least three of the four factors.

Note: If not B3 then award B2 for two of: the correct fraction, the correct \(x\) term, or the correct \(y\) term. If not B2 then award B1 for one of these, or for applying one of the powers correctly to at least three of the four factors.

title: Table and graph of a reciprocal function
parts:
Complete the table of values for \(y=\dfrac1x(x^2+4)\)
\(x\)0.250.51248
\(y\)16.258.5
On the grid, draw the graph of \(y=\dfrac1x(x^2+4)\) for \(0.25\leq x\leq8\)
markscheme: Note: If not B2, award B1 for two or three correct values.
Plot five or six points correctly, following through from the table.
A fully correct graph with all points correct and joined by a smooth curve.
Note: In part (b), M1 is ft their table and dep on B1 in part (a). If the table is blank but a fully correct graph is drawn, award the marks in part (a).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank coordinate grid for part (b), with x-axis from 0 to 8 in unit steps and y-axis from 0 to 17 in unit steps.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot (0.25,16.25), (0.5,8.5), (1,5), (2,4), (4,5) and (8,8.5), then join them with a smooth curve.

title: Inverse-square proportionality
body:
\(A\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(r\)

\(A=5\) when \(r=0.3\)
parts: Find a formula for \(A\) in terms of \(r\)
markscheme: Note: For part (a), \(k\) may be any letter but must be a letter and not 1. For part (b), the first M1 is ft from part (a) and dep on M2 there; the second M1 must include \(A^3\).

title: Perpendicular line intercept
body:
The straight line \(L\) passes through the points \((4,-1)\) and \((6,4)\)

The straight line \(M\) is perpendicular to \(L\) and intersects the \(y\)-axis at the point \((0,8)\)

Find the coordinates of the point where \(M\) intersects the \(x\)-axis.
markscheme: Note: The gradient of M mark is ft from their clearly stated gradient of L. The equation-of-a-line M1 is dep on the preceding M1. An answer of 20 gains M3 if clearly intended as the x-coordinate.

title: Perimeter of a cyclic quadrilateral
body:
\(ABCD\) is a quadrilateral where \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) are points on a circle. \(AB=8\) cm
\(BC=7.5\) cm
Angle \(ABC=98^\circ\)
Angle \(ACD=35^\circ\) Work out the perimeter of quadrilateral \(ABCD\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: The calculation for AD or DC is dep on the first and second M marks. Accept 32.7–32.9.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle, not to scale, with cyclic quadrilateral ABCD. A is upper left, B upper right, C right, and D lower left. Sides AB, BC, CD and DA and diagonal AC are drawn. AB is labelled 8 cm, BC is labelled 7.5 cm, angle ABC is marked 98 degrees, and angle ACD between AC and CD is marked 35 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations
\(y=3-2x\)
\(x^2+y^2=18\)
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Solve the quadratic by a correct method, for example \((5x+3)(x-3)=0\).

Note: The quadratic-solving M1 is ft and dep on the preceding M1. If using the formula allow one sign error and some simplification. Both final A marks are dep on M2 and the pairs must be clearly matched.

title: Similar solids from surface areas
body:
Mathematically similar wooden blocks are made in a workshop.

There are small blocks and there are large blocks.

The volume of each small block is 300 cm\(^3\)

Given that

the surface area of each small block : the surface area of each large block \(=25:36\)

work out the volume of each large block.
markscheme: The linear scale factor small to large is \(5:6\), or the volume ratio is \(125:216\).
Note: The first M1 may be for a correct length or volume scale factor, or a correct equation for the large-block volume. Allow 518.

title: Stationary point with a parameter
body:
The point \(A\) is the only stationary point on the curve with equation \(y=kx^2+\dfrac{16}{x}\) where \(k\) is a constant.
Given that the coordinates of \(A\) are \(\left(\dfrac23,a\right)\)
find the value of \(a\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: If not M2, award M1 for one term differentiated correctly.
Note: The equation \(2kx-16x^{-2}=0\) is ft and dep on M1. The substitution mark is not ft. A1 is dep on M4 and working must be seen.

title: Transformations of a quadratic graph
body:
The curve \(S\) has equation \(y=f(x)\) where \(f(x)=x^2\)
The curve \(T\) has equation \(y=g(x)\) where \(g(x)=2x^2-12x+13\) By writing \(g(x)\) in the form \(a(x-b)^2-c\), where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are constants, describe fully a series of transformations that map the curve \(S\) onto the curve \(T\).
markscheme: Note: If not B2, award B1 for one of \(a=2\), \(b=3\), or \(c=5\).
Identify a stretch in the y-direction with scale factor 2 and a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix}3\\-5\end{pmatrix}\).
Stretch in the y-direction by scale factor 2, followed by translation by \(\begin{pmatrix}3\\-5\end{pmatrix}\).
Translate by \(\begin{pmatrix}3\\-2.5\end{pmatrix}\), followed by a stretch in the y-direction by scale factor 2.
The same transformations in that stated order.

Note: The word translation or translate and the word stretch must be included. The transformations must be in the correct order. An alternative is translation by \(\binom{3}{-2.5}\), followed by stretch scale factor 2 in the y-direction.

title: Unknown total from sequential probability
body:
Pippa has a box containing \(N\) pens. There are only black pens and red pens in the box.
The number of black pens in the box is 3 more than the number of red pens. Pippa is going to take at random 2 pens from the box.
The probability that she will take a black pen followed by a red pen is \(\dfrac9{35}\)
Find the possible values of \(N\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: The probability that the first pen is black is \(\dfrac{N+3}{2N}\), using black \(=\dfrac{N+3}{2}\) and red \(=\dfrac{N-3}{2}\).
Note: The equation mark is dep on the previous M1 and must use one variable, or define one variable in terms of the other. A1 is cao and dep on M4; working must be seen.

title: Index division and bracket expansion
markscheme: Note: For part (a), accept \(e^6\). For part (b), expansion must show the four terms before collecting, or an equivalent correct method.

title: Missing side using Pythagoras
body:
Here is a right-angled triangle. Calculate the value of \(h\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: Use Pythagoras with 52 as the hypotenuse. Accept the correctly rounded value to 3 significant figures.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A right-angled triangle, not to scale, with horizontal top side labelled 30 cm, vertical right side labelled h cm, sloping hypotenuse labelled 52 cm, and a right-angle marker at the top-right vertex. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Changing a proportion of fish
body:
There are 54 fish in a tank.
Some of the fish are white and the rest of the fish are red. Jeevan takes at random a fish from the tank.
parts:
The probability that he takes a white fish is \(\dfrac49\)
Work out the number of white fish originally in the tank.

Jeevan puts the fish he took out, back into the tank.
He puts some more white fish into the tank. Jeevan takes at random a fish from the tank.
The probability that he takes a white fish is now \(\dfrac12\)
Work out the number of white fish Jeevan put into the tank.
markscheme: \(\dfrac{24+n}{54+n}=\dfrac12\), or note there are 30 red fish and make white equal to red.
Note: For part (a), allow \(0.44\dot4\times54\), oe. In part (b), M1 is ft if their original white-fish value is less than 27.

title: Varnish for a door with a window
body:
The diagram shows the front of a wooden door with a semicircular glass window. Julie wants to apply 2 coats of wood varnish to the front of the door, shown shaded in the diagram. 250 millilitres of wood varnish covers 4 m\(^2\) of the wood. Work out how many millilitres of wood varnish Julie will need.
Give your answer correct to the nearest millilitre.
markscheme: Note: M1 is for the rectangle area, M1 for the circle or semicircle area, and M1 for subtraction. Allow 175–176.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A shaded rectangular door, not to scale, 2 m high and 0.75 m wide. An unshaded semicircular window near the top has horizontal diameter 0.5 m. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Dimensions from arranged rectangular tiles
body:
Yasmin has some identical rectangular tiles.
Each tile is \(L\) cm by \(W\) cm. Using 9 of her tiles, Yasmin makes rectangle \(ABCD\), shown in the diagram. The area of \(ABCD\) is 1620 cm\(^2\) Work out the value of \(L\) and the value of \(W\).
markscheme: Note: If not M2, award M1 for one correct equation or for \(1620\div9=180\).
Form a correct equation in one variable only, for example \(4L^2+4(180)=1620\).
Note: If not A2, award A1 for one correct value.
Note: M2 for any two of the four stated equations; if not M2, award M1 for one correct equation or \(1620\div9=180\). A2 for both answers; A1 for one. Award 4 marks for \(L=12,W=15\), dep on M3.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A single tile is shown as a vertical rectangle with height L cm and width W cm. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Rectangle ABCD, not to scale, is formed from nine identical tiles in two rows: the top row has five upright tiles and the bottom row has four tiles rotated horizontally. The outer rectangle has A top-left, B top-right, C bottom-right and D bottom-left. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Cost of apples and pears
body:
Alison buys 5 apples and 3 pears for a total cost of $1.96
Greg buys 3 apples and 2 pears for a total cost of $1.22 Michael buys 10 apples and 10 pears. Work out how much Michael pays for his 10 apples and 10 pears.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Let apple cost \(a\) and pear cost \(p\): \(5a+3p=1.96\), \(3a+2p=1.22\).
Use elimination or substitution correctly to find one price.
Note: The substitution M1 is dep on M2 and requires their positive value in one equation. The final method mark is dep on M3. A1 is dep on M2 and working is required.

title: Prime factors of 3600
body:
Write \(3.6\times10^3\) as a product of powers of its prime factors.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: At least two correct factorisation stages producing prime factors.
Note: Working is required. A1 is dep on M2; prime factors may be in any order. SCB1 for \(3.6\times2^3\times5^3\).

title: Finding a total from a percentage
body:
In 2018, the population of Sydney was 5.48 million.
This was 22% of the total population of Australia. Work out the total population of Australia in 2018
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: Accept an answer awrt 24.9 million, or awrt 24 900 000 if working in individuals.

title: Compound inequality on a number line
parts:

A solid aluminium cylinder has radius 10 cm and height \(h\) cm. The mass of the cylinder is 5.4 kg.
