title: Cliff and radio mast heights
body:
The diagram shows a vertical cliff with a vertical radio mast on top of the cliff and a buoy in the sea. The height of the cliff is 100 metres.
The buoy is at the point \(B\) that is \(d\) metres from the base of the cliff.
The angle of elevation from \(B\) to the top of the cliff is \(20^\circ\)
parts:
Calculate the value of \(d\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

The point \(A\) at the top of the radio mast is vertically above the top of the cliff.
The angle of elevation from \(B\) to \(A\) is \(25^\circ\) Calculate the height of the radio mast.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: Part (b) is ft from part (a). Accept 28–28.2 for the mast height.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A vertical cliff at left with height 100 m and a vertical radio mast on top whose upper point is A. A horizontal sea-level line runs right to buoy B and is labelled d m. A dotted line from B to the cliff top makes a 20-degree angle with the horizontal at B. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Upper bound using the sine rule
body:
Here is a triangle \(XYZ\). The length \(XZ\) and the angles \(YXZ\) and \(XYZ\) are each given correct to 2 significant figures. Calculate the upper bound for the length \(YZ\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: For the bounds mark, accept \(16.49\dot9\), \(25.49\dot9\) and \(134.\dot9\). A1 requires correct working and accepts 32.5–32.6.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Triangle XYZ, not to scale, with X at the top, Y lower left and Z lower right. Side XZ is labelled 16 cm, angle YXZ at X is 130 degrees and angle XYZ at Y is 25 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Vectors and area in concentric hexagons
body:
\(ABCDEF\) and \(GHIJKL\) are regular hexagons each with centre \(O\). \(GHIJKL\) is an enlargement of \(ABCDEF\), with centre \(O\) and scale factor 2
\(\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a\) \(\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b\)
parts:
Write the following vectors, in terms of \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\).
Simplify your answers.
(i) \(\overrightarrow{AB}\)
(ii) \(\overrightarrow{KI}\) (iii) \(\overrightarrow{LD}\)

The triangle \(OAB\) has an area of 5 cm\(^2\)

Calculate the area of the shaded region.
markscheme: A valid path, for example \(\overrightarrow{KI}=2(\mathbf b-\mathbf a)+2\mathbf b\).
A valid path, for example \((\mathbf b-\mathbf a)+(\mathbf b-\mathbf a)-\mathbf a\).
Outer hexagon area \(=6\times5\times2^2=120\text{ cm}^2\), or inner hexagon area \(=6\times5=30\text{ cm}^2\).
Note: For part (a)(ii) and (iii), M1 is ft from (i) for any valid path, oe, and A1 requires a simplified vector. Correct answers score full marks unless from obvious incorrect working.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two concentric regular hexagons, not to scale. Inner ABCDEF and outer GHIJKL share centre O and corresponding orientation with horizontal top and bottom sides. The annular region between them is shaded. Inner vertices clockwise from upper left are A, B, C, D, E, F; outer vertices clockwise from upper left are G, H, I, J, K, L. Vectors OA and OB are drawn and labelled a and b. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Chess scores and probability
body:
Magnus and Garry play 2 games of chess against each other.
The probability that Magnus beats Garry in any game is \(\dfrac29\)
The probability that any game between Magnus and Garry is drawn is \(\dfrac49\)
The result of any game is independent of the result of any other game.
parts:
For each game of chess, the winner gets 2 points and the loser gets 0 points; when the game is drawn, each player gets 1 point.

Work out the probability that, after 2 games, Magnus and Garry have the same number of points.

Magnus and Garry now play a third game of chess.

Work out the probability that, after 3 games, Magnus and Garry have the same number of points.
markscheme: Each second-game set of branches is \(\dfrac29,\dfrac49,\dfrac39\) for win, draw, loss.
One valid equal-score path product, from win-loss, loss-win, or draw-draw.
One valid equal-score path product, from a permutation of win-loss-draw or from three draws.
Note: In part (a), the second B1 is ft for all second-game branch values. In parts (b) and (c), M marks are ft from their tree and allow probabilities rounded or truncated to 2 decimal places.
Note: Alternative counting methods for equal points are allowed, with M1ft for one correct product and M1ft for a complete method.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A two-stage probability tree. Each stage has three outcome branches in order Magnus wins, game drawn, Magnus loses. On the first stage, win is labelled 2/9, draw 4/9, and loss blank. All nine second-stage branch probabilities are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill the first-stage loss branch with 3/9. On every second-stage split, label win 2/9, draw 4/9 and loss 3/9.

title: Three-set Venn diagram
body:
There are 32 students in a class.
In one term these 32 students each took a test in Maths (\(M\)), in English (\(E\)) and in French (\(F\)). 25 students passed the test in Maths.
20 students passed the test in English.
14 students passed the test in French.
18 students passed the tests in Maths and English.
11 students passed the tests in Maths and French.
4 students failed all three tests.
\(x\) students passed all three tests. The incomplete Venn diagram gives some more information about the results of the 32 students.
parts: Use all the given information about the results of students who passed the test in Maths to find the value of \(x\).
Use your value of \(x\) to complete the Venn diagram to show the number of students in each subset.

A student who passed the test in Maths is chosen at random.

Find the probability that this student failed the test in French.
markscheme: Complete the remaining regions with M∩E only 11, all three 7, M∩F only 4, M only 3, E∩F only 2, E only 0, F only 1, and outside 4.
Note: If not B2, award B1 for four or five correct remaining values.
Note: Part (b) is B2ft for six correct remaining values, dep on M1 in part (a) and \(x<12\); B1ft for four or five correct values. Part (c) is B1ft, oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A rectangle labelled universal set E contains three overlapping circles: M left, E right and F below. The M-only region contains 3 and the E-and-F-only region contains 2. All other regions are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Fill M-only 3, E-only 0, F-only 1, M∩E only 11, M∩F only 4, E∩F only 2, all three 7, and outside all circles 4.

title: Advanced algebraic manipulation
parts: Express \(4x^2-8x+7\) in the form \(a(x+b)^2+c\) where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are integers.
markscheme: Split the middle term, for example \(6y(y-1)+5(y-1)\).
Note: For part (a), condone a different letter from \(y\). In part (b), the gathering-terms M1 is ft and dep on two terms in \(f\) and two other terms. In part (c), allow \(a=4,b=-1,c=3\).

title: Recurring decimal with a variable digit
body:
\(0.4\dot{x}\) is a recurring decimal.
\(x\) is a whole number such that \(1\leq x\leq9\) Find, in terms of \(x\), the recurring decimal \(0.4\dot{x}\) as a fraction.
Give your fraction in its simplest form.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Let \(y=0.4xxx\ldots\). Form two correct recurring expressions, for example \(100y=40+x.xxx\ldots\) and \(10y=4.xxx\ldots\), with subtraction indicated.
Note: M1 requires two correct recurring-decimal expressions and an indicated subtraction. A1 is dep on M2 and working is required.

title: Optimising a rectangle with an equilateral roof
body:
\(ABCED\) is a five-sided shape. \(ABCD\) is a rectangle.
\(CED\) is an equilateral triangle. \(AB=x\) cm \(BC=y\) cm The perimeter of \(ABCED\) is 100 cm.
The area of \(ABCED\) is \(R\) cm\(^2\)
parts:
(i) Find the value of \(x\) for which \(R\) has its maximum value.
Give your answer in the form \(\dfrac{p}{q-\sqrt3}\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers.
(ii) Explain why the maximum value of \(R\) is given by this value of \(x\).
markscheme: Note: A1 requires the area in the given form with full working and at least one intermediate step.
Note: The differentiation M1 may be implied by subsequent working.
R is a quadratic with a negative coefficient of \(x^2\), equivalently \(\dfrac{d^2R}{dx^2}<0\), so the stationary point is a maximum.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A house-shaped pentagon ABCED, not to scale. ABCD is a rectangle with A lower left, B lower right, C upper right and D upper left. Equilateral triangle CED sits on top with apex E. AB is labelled x cm, BC y cm, and the shared edge DC is dotted. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Area from a perpendicular bisector
body:
The straight line \(L\) passes through point \(A(-6,2)\) and point \(B(5,3)\)
The straight line \(M\) is perpendicular to \(L\) and passes through the midpoint of \(A\) and \(B\).
The line \(M\) intersects the line \(x=-1\) at point \(C\). Calculate the area of triangle \(ABC\).
markscheme: Note: The gradient-perpendicular mark is ft from their gradient of AB. The line-equation M1 must give the y-coordinate at C. Allow 30.4–30.5.
Note: Alternative area methods using subtraction from a rectangle, perpendicular sides, equal-height triangles or Heron's formula gain M1 for a correct start and M1 for a complete method.

title: Index laws
parts: Write down the value of \(m\), given that \(3^4\times3^5=3^m\)
Write down the value of \(n\), given that \((5^3)^7=5^n\)
Find the value of \(p\), given that \(\dfrac{7^8\times7^2}{7^p}=7^6\)
markscheme: Note: For part (a), allow \(3^9\); for part (b), allow \(5^{21}\). In part (c), accept an embedded index equation, oe.

title: Equation from rectangle areas
body:
Here are two rectangles, rectangle A and rectangle B. The area of rectangle B is twice the area of rectangle A. Work out the value of \(x\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Set up one correct area expression: \(4(5-x)\) or \(5(2x-1)\).
Note: The equation M1 requires terms in \(x\) on one side and constants on the other. A1 is dep on M1 and working is required.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Rectangle A, not to scale, has width 4 cm and height (5 - x) cm. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Rectangle B, not to scale, has width 5 cm and height (2x - 1) cm. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Grouped spending data
body:
The table gives information about the amounts of money, in euros, that 70 of Anjali's friends spent last Saturday.
Money spent (\(S\) euros)Frequency

parts:
One of Anjali's 70 friends is going to be chosen at random.

Find the probability that this friend spent more than 24 euros last Saturday.

Work out an estimate for the mean amount of money spent by Anjali's friends last Saturday.
Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
markscheme: Use midpoints and at least four correct products, for example \(4\times6+12\times14+20\times19+28\times25+36\times6\).

Note: If not M2 in part (b), award M1 for consistent interval values in at least four added products, or four correct midpoints. The division M1 is dep on at least M1. Accept an answer awrt 21.26 or 21.3.

title: Lengths in similar triangles
body: \(ABC\) and \(DEF\) are similar triangles.
parts: Given that \(BC=54\) cm, work out the length of \(EF\).
markscheme: Note: The part (b) M1 may ft if M1 was scored in part (a). Correct answers score full marks unless from obvious incorrect working.

title: Angles in joined polygons
body:
The diagram shows a regular octagon \(ABCDHIJK\) and a pentagon \(DEFGH\). Angle \(GHD\) = angle \(FGH\). Work out the size of the angle marked \(x\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Remaining two equal pentagon angles total \(3\times180-112-102-96=230^\circ\).
Note: The second M1 is dep on the preceding mark; the octagon-angle M1 is independent. Withhold that mark if \(360\div8=45\) is shown as an interior angle. A1 is dep on M1 and working is required.

Pentagon continues D-E-F-G-H to the right. Interior pentagon angles at D, E and F are 112, 102 and 96 degrees. Equal double arcs mark angles GHD and FGH. title: Percentage profit on bottles
body:
Victor buys 12 bottles of apple juice for a total cost of $21
Victor sells all 12 bottles at $2.45 each bottle. Work out Victor's percentage profit.
markscheme: Note: The second M1 may also be earned by an answer of 140%. Correct answers score full marks unless from obvious incorrect working.

title: Comparing bank interest
body:
Ali and Badia each have 25 000 dollars to invest.
Cyclone BankTornado Bank
Invest 25 000 dollars
4.5% compound interest per year
for 3 years		Invest 25 000 dollars
Receive 1150 dollars interest each year
for 3 years
Ali invests in the Cyclone Bank for 3 years.
Badia invests in the Tornado Bank for 3 years. By the end of the 3 years, Ali will have received more interest than Badia. How much more?
Show your working clearly.
Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar.
markscheme: Find the first year's compound interest or amount, for example \(25000\times1.045=26125\), or find Tornado Bank interest \(1150\times3=3450\).
Compare compound interest \(3529.153\ldots\) with simple interest \(3450\).
Note: M2 may be awarded for \(1.045^3\times25000\). The final A1 is dep on M2. Allow 79–80 and working is required.

title: Zero index and quadratic factors
markscheme: Identify factors with product \(-36\) and sum \(-5\), for example \((x\pm4)(x\pm9)\).
Note: In part (b)(i), isw if the equation is also solved. Part (b)(ii) is B1ft from two factors in (i); award B0 for −4 and 9 when no marks were scored in (i).

title: Raindrops, bacteria and molecules
body:
A rainwater tank contains \(2.4\times10^7\) raindrops.
The rainwater tank also contains \(1.75\times10^6\) bacteria.
parts:
Work out the number of bacteria per raindrop in the tank.
Give your answer in standard form correct to 2 significant figures.

A drop of rainwater contains \(5.01\times10^{21}\) atoms. In a drop of rainwater the number of atoms is 3 times the number of molecules. Work out the number of molecules in the rainwater tank.
Give your answer in standard form correct to one significant figure.
markscheme: Note: For part (a), accept \(7.3\times10^{-2}\) or better. For part (b), accept \(4\times10^{28}\), \(4.0\times10^{28}\), \(4.01\times10^{28}\) or \(4.008\times10^{28}\).

title: Perimeter of an isosceles triangle
body:
\(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle with \(BA=BC\). \(N\) is the point on \(AC\) such that \(AN=9.3\) cm and \(BN\) is perpendicular to \(AC\). Work out the perimeter of triangle \(ABC\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: The first M1 may use trigonometry and Pythagoras. Accept an answer awrt 42.2.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Isosceles triangle ABC, not to scale, with apex B and horizontal base AC. Tick marks show BA = BC. N is the foot of a dashed perpendicular from B to AC with a right-angle marker. AN is labelled 9.3 cm and angle BAC is marked 38 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Circle angle from a tangent
body:
\(B\), \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\) are points on a circle, centre \(O\).
\(ABC\) is a tangent to the circle.
\(ODC\) is a straight line. \(BOE\) is a diameter of the circle. Angle \(BCD=48^\circ\) Find the size of angle \(DFE\).
markscheme: Note: The first M1 may be shown in the correct place on the diagram. The second M1 requires a fully correct method to find angle DFE.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circle, not to scale, with vertical diameter E-O-B. Line ABC is tangent at B, running roughly left to right. Point D lies on the lower-right circumference and O-D-C is a straight line extending to C on the tangent-side exterior. Point F lies on the left circumference. Chords FD and FE are drawn. Angle BCD at C is marked 48 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Indices, fractions and expansion
parts:
Write as a single fraction \(\dfrac{2}{3x}+\dfrac{4}{5x}-\dfrac{9}{10x}\)
Give your answer in its simplest form.

Expand and simplify \(4x(x-5)(2x+3)\)
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: If not B2, award B1 for two correct factors in the product.
Use denominator \(30x\), with at least two correct equivalent numerators.
Correctly expand two factors, for example \((x-5)(2x+3)=2x^2-7x-15\).
Multiply by the third factor to obtain \(8x^3-28x^2-60x\).
Note: For part (a), B1 for two correct terms in a product of three. In part (c), the second M1 is ft but dep on the preceding M1, allowing one further error or omission; A1 is dep on M1.

title: Inequalities defining a region
body:
The region \(R\), shown shaded in the diagram, is bounded by three straight lines.

Write down the three inequalities that define \(R\).
markscheme: Note: B3 for all three inequalities; B2 for two; B1 for one. Allow strict signs in place of inclusive signs.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Coordinate grid with region R shaded as a triangle. Its boundaries are the horizontal solid line y = -3, the descending solid line x + y = 1, and the ascending solid line y = 2x + 2, which is labelled. R lies above y = -3 and below both sloping lines.

title: Flight-delay histogram
body:
Manuel collected information about the flights that arrived late at an airport last month. The table gives information about the number of minutes that these flights were late.
Minutes late (\(L\) minutes)Frequency
\(08
\(1013
\(1519
\(2524
\(406
parts: On the grid, draw a histogram for this information.

Manuel selected at random a flight that was late by 25 minutes or less from his results.

Work out an estimate for the probability that this flight was late by 5 minutes or less.
markscheme: Note: If not B3, award B2 for at least three correct densities or bars, and B1 for two correct bars of different widths.
Estimate 4 flights in the first 5 minutes and use denominator \(8+13+19=40\).
Note: In part (a), B2 for at least three correct frequency densities or bars, or all bars with correct widths and proportional heights. In part (b), if M0 then SCB1 for \(\dfrac2{35}\), oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A blank histogram grid with horizontal axis Number of minutes late from 0 to 60 and vertical axis Frequency density from 0 upward, labelled at 1, 2 and 3.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Draw bars over 0-10, 10-15, 15-25, 25-40 and 40-60 with respective heights 0.8, 2.6, 1.9, 1.6 and 0.3.

title: Composite and inverse rational functions
body:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are such that
\(f(x)=2x-3\)
\(g(x)=\dfrac{x}{3x+1}\)
parts: State the value of \(x\) that cannot be included in any domain of \(g\)
Express the inverse function \(g^{-1}\) in the form \(g^{-1}(x)=...\)
markscheme: Note: In part (b), do not isw incorrect cancelling. In part (c), M1 is for moving and expanding the denominator; the second M1 is for collecting and factorising the variable correctly.

title: Same-colour counters
body:
A box contains 15 counters. There are 4 red counters, 5 green counters and the rest are yellow counters. Niklas takes at random a counter from the box and writes down the colour of his counter.
He then puts the counter back into the box. Sasha then takes at random a counter from the box and writes down the colour of her counter. Work out the probability that the counters taken by Niklas and Sasha both have the same colour.
markscheme: One correct product, for example \(\dfrac4{15}\times\dfrac4{15}\), \(\dfrac5{15}\times\dfrac5{15}\), or \(\dfrac6{15}\times\dfrac6{15}\).

Note: Allow products using decimals rounded or truncated to 2 decimal places. If no marks are awarded, SCB2 for \(\dfrac{31}{105}\) from non-replacement, or SCB1 for a fully correct non-replacement method.

title: Rationalising a surd denominator
body:
Express \(\dfrac8{\sqrt5-1}\) in the form \(\sqrt a+b\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: The rationalising M1 is awarded for the intention to multiply by \(\sqrt5+1\), or an equivalent conjugate. A1 is from correct working; B1ft accepts \(a=20,b=2\).

title: Area of a quadrilateral
body:
Here is a quadrilateral \(ABCD\). Calculate the area of quadrilateral \(ABCD\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: The second area M1 is independent; the triangle ACD area M1 is dep on the first M1. Final A1 is dep on M3, requires working and accepts an answer awrt 84.4.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Quadrilateral ABCD, not to scale, with A lower left, B upper left, C upper-right/centre, and D lower right. Sides AB, BC, CD, DA and diagonal AC are drawn. AB is 9 cm, BC 12 cm, CD 7 cm, angle ABC is 60 degrees and angle ACD is 84 degrees. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Midpoint of line-curve intersections
body:
The straight line \(L\) has equation \(x-y=3\)
The curve \(C\) has equation \(3x^2-y^2+xy=9\) \(L\) and \(C\) intersect at the points \(P\) and \(Q\). Find the coordinates of the midpoint of \(PQ\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Intersection coordinates are \((2,-1)\) and \((-3,-6)\), or directly obtain one correct midpoint coordinate.
Note: The quadratic-formation M1 is ft and dep on the substitution M1. The solving M1 is dep on M1. Both final A marks are dep on M2 and working is required.

title: Arithmetic series with a parameter
body:
Here are the first four terms of an arithmetic series.

\(k,\dfrac{3k}{4},\dfrac{k}{2},\dfrac{k}{4}\)

Given that the 15th term of the series is \((90+2k)\), calculate the sum of the first 30 terms of the series.
markscheme: Note: The equation M1 is dep on equating two expressions using their common difference. The sum-substitution M1 is dep on the preceding M1 and all substituted values must be numerical.

title: Graph transformations and cosine parameters
body:
The curve \(C\) has equation \(y=f(x)\) where \(f(x)=9-3(x+2)^2\)
The point \(A\) is the maximum point on \(C\).
parts:
The curve \(C\) is transformed to the curve \(S\) by a translation of \(\begin{pmatrix}4\\0\end{pmatrix}\)
Find an equation for the curve \(S\).

The curve \(C\) is transformed to the curve \(T\).
The curve \(T\) has equation \(y=3(x+2)^2-9\) Describe fully the transformation that maps curve \(C\) onto curve \(T\).

The graph of \(y=a\cos(x-b)^\circ+c\) for \(-180\leq x\leq360\) is drawn on the grid.

Find the value of \(a\), the value of \(b\) and the value of \(c\).
markscheme: Reflection in the x-axis, equivalently the line \(y=0\).
Note: Equivalent parameterisation \(a=-3\), \(b=90\), \(c=2\) is accepted. If not B3, award B2 for two consistent correct values or B1 for one.
Note: In part (c), accept reflection in \(y=0\) or the x-axis with no other transformation. In part (d), B2 for any two correct values and B1 for one; accept coterminal phase values as stated.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. For part (d), a cosine graph on axes from x = -180 to 360 degrees and y = -1 to 6. It has maxima at (-90,5) and (270,5), minimum at (90,-1), midline y = 2, and passes through (-180,2), (0,2), (180,2), and (360,2).

title: Surface area of a rectangular pyramid
body:
The diagram shows a sphere of diameter \(x\) cm and a pyramid \(ABCDE\) with a horizontal rectangular base \(BCDE\). The vertex \(A\) of the pyramid is vertically above the centre \(O\) of the base so that \(AB=AC=AD=AE\). \(BC=x\) cm, \(CD=2x\) cm and \(AO=5x\) cm. The volume of the sphere is \(288\pi\) cm\(^3\) Calculate the total surface area of the pyramid.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cm\(^2\)
markscheme: Slant height of faces CAD and BAE \(=\sqrt{(5x)^2+(x/2)^2}=6\sqrt{101}\) when \(x=12\).
Slant height of faces ABC and AED \(=\sqrt{(5x)^2+x^2}=12\sqrt{26}\) when \(x=12\).
Note: Both slant-height M marks are dep on the first M1 and use of their value for \(x\). The surface-area M1 is also dep on correct working for both triangle heights. Accept 2469–2470.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A sphere, not to scale, with horizontal diameter labelled x cm. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE. Pyramid ABCDE, not to scale, has rectangular horizontal base BCDE. B is front left, C front right, D rear right and E rear left. BC is labelled x cm and CD 2x cm. Apex A is vertically above base centre O; dotted AO is labelled 5x cm. Hidden base and sloping edges are dashed. Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Indices and changing the subject

Note: In part (c), if not B2 then award B1 for two correct parts in a product. In part (d), SCB1 for \(t=\dfrac{c+8v}{3}\), oe.

title: Money shared in a ratio
body:
Danil, Gabriel and Hadley share some money in the ratios \(3:5:9\)
The difference between the amount of money that Gabriel receives and the amount of money that Hadley receives is 196 euros. Work out the amount of money that Danil receives.
markscheme: Note: SCB1 for an answer from 34.5–34.6 or an answer of 42.

title: Right-triangle length
body:
The diagram shows triangle \(ABC\). Work out the length of the side \(AB\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: M1 for setting up a trigonometric equation in AB, followed by M1 for a complete method. Accept 7.61–7.613.

title: Percentage profit on mugs
body:
Sarah makes and sells mugs. One day she makes 150 mugs.
Her total cost for making these mugs is £1140 Of these mugs
\(\dfrac25\) are small mugs
32% are medium mugs
and the rest are large mugs Here is Sarah's price list for selling each mug.
MUGSPrice
Small£8.50
Medium£11.20
Large£14.20

title: Constructing data and reversing a mean
parts:
For the remaining four cards, write on each dotted line a number that could be on the card.
524

A basketball team plays 6 games.
After playing 5 games, the team has a mean score of 21 points per game.
After playing 6 games, the team has a mean score of 23 points per game. Work out the number of points the team scored in its 6th game.
markscheme: A valid ordered list, for example \(5,8,8,20,21,24\).
Note: Award B1 for correct endpoints and B1 for a unique mode of 8; the two middle values must sum to 28.
Note: In part (a), B2 for the correct pattern with the fifth card blank or invalid; B1 for a median of 14, a mode of 8, or middle cards summing to 28.
body:
Jenny has six cards. Each card has a whole number written on it so that the smallest number is 5
the largest number is 24
the median of the six numbers is 14

title: Angle in a prism
body:
The diagram shows the prism \(ABCDEFGHJK\) with horizontal base \(AEFG\). \(ABCDE\) is a cross section of the prism where
\(ABDE\) is a square
\(BCD\) is an equilateral triangle \(EF=2\times AE\)
\(M\) is the midpoint of \(GF\) so that \(JM\) is vertical. Angle \(MAJ=y^\circ\)
Given that \(\tan y^\circ=T\), find the value of \(T\), giving your answer in the form \(\dfrac{\sqrt p+\sqrt q}{17}\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers.
markscheme: Let \(AE=2x\), so \(EF=4x\). Use Pythagoras in the horizontal base to obtain \(AM=\sqrt{x^2+(4x)^2}=x\sqrt{17}\).
The height of equilateral triangle HJK is \(x\sqrt3\), so \(JM=x\sqrt3+2x\).
Rationalise by multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{17}\).

Note: The AM and equilateral-height method marks require correct numerical or algebraic methods. The tangent mark accepts a numerical value 0.9–0.91. The rationalising M1 precedes the simplified surd answer.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Oblique prism ABCDEFGHJK, not to scale, with house-shaped cross-section ABCDE: ABDE is a square and roof triangle BCD is equilateral. The corresponding rear cross-section is GHJK, joined by prism edges. AEFG is the horizontal rectangular base. M is the midpoint of GF and dashed JM is vertical. Angle MAJ is at A. Label EF = 2 x AE. markscheme: \("51.4\ldots"\times18\), or find \(r=\sqrt{"51.4\ldots"/\pi}=4.046\ldots\) and then use \(\pi r^2h\).
Allow use of \(\pi r^2\) to find the radius and then \(\pi r^2h\) to find the volume. Allow \(925\)–\(928\).
body:
A cylinder is placed on the ground. The height of the cylinder is \(18\text{ cm}\). The force exerted by the cylinder on the ground is \(72\) newtons.
The pressure on the ground due to the cylinder is \(1.4\text{ newtons/cm}^2\).\[\text{pressure}=\dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}\] Work out the volume of the cylinder. Give your answer correct to \(3\) significant figures.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Upright cylinder, not accurately drawn, with vertical height labelled \(18\text{ cm}\). Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Index laws
markscheme: \(8k^6m^{12}\). B2 for all correct; B1 for two correct from \(8\), \(k^6\), \(m^{12}\).
For part (c), B2 for all correct; B1 for two correct from \(8\), \(k^6\), \(m^{12}\).

title: Intersecting coordinate circles
markscheme: \(13+6>"17"\), with a correct reason, ft dependent on M1. Accept, for example, “They overlap by 2 cm” or “The distance between the centres is less than the sum of the radii”. Do not accept “19 is greater than the distance between the circles” oe or “The circumference of each circle overlaps”.
A correct reason is required and is ft dependent on M1. “The circumference of each circle overlaps” is not acceptable.
body:
Two circles, \(C_1\) and \(C_2\), are drawn on a centimetre grid, with a scale of \(1\text{ cm}\) for \(1\) unit on each axis. The centre of circle \(C_1\) is at the point with coordinates \((-1,3)\) and the radius of \(C_1\) is \(13\text{ cm}\).
The centre of circle \(C_2\) is at the point with coordinates \((7,18)\) and the radius of \(C_2\) is \(6\text{ cm}\).
parts: Work out the distance between the centre of \(C_1\) and the centre of \(C_2\).

title: Factorisation and algebraic fractions
markscheme: Two correct fractions with common denominator, or a single correct fraction, for example \(\dfrac{28x}{32x}-\dfrac{8(x+3)}{32x}\) oe.
Correct fraction(s) with brackets expanded and dealing with the negative signs, for example \(\dfrac{28x-8x-24}{32x}\) oe.
For part (b), M1 for correct fraction(s) with bracket(s) expanded and dealing with the negative signs.
parts: Express \(\dfrac78-\dfrac{x+3}{4x}\) as a single fraction in its simplest form.

title: Treadmill probability tree
markscheme: \(0.8\) and \(0.2\); \(0.3\) and \(0.7\); \(0.6\) and \(0.4\). B2 for all three correct pairs on the correct branches; B1 for two correct pairs. Allow equivalent fractions.
\("0.8"\times"0.3"\). Both probabilities must be less than 1.
B2 for all three correct probability pairs on the correct branches; B1 for two correct pairs. Allow equivalent fractions.
body:
Rudolf goes to the gym. The probability that he will use the treadmill is \(0.8\). When he uses the treadmill, the probability that he will use the cross trainer is \(0.3\).
When he does not use the treadmill, the probability that he will use the cross trainer is \(0.6\).
parts: Complete the probability tree diagram for this information.
Work out the probability that Rudolf uses both the treadmill and the cross trainer.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE for part (a). Two-stage probability tree. First split: use treadmill / does not use treadmill. Each then splits into use cross trainer / does not use cross trainer. All printed probability spaces are blank.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE for part (a). Complete first branches with \(0.8,0.2\); treadmill second branches with \(0.3,0.7\); non-treadmill second branches with \(0.6,0.4\).

title: Holiday payments
markscheme: \(\dfrac38+45\%=\dfrac{33}{40}\), or \(82.5\%\), or \(0.825\). Do not award M1 for, for example, \(\dfrac38+45\%+406\).
Do NOT award the first M1 for, for example, \(\dfrac38+45\%+406\).
body:
Antoine is going on holiday. He makes \(3\) separate payments to cover the total cost of his holiday. The following table shows how much money Antoine pays to the holiday company.
PaymentAmount paid
Payment \(1\)\(\dfrac38\) of the total cost
Payment \(2\)\(45\%\) of the total cost
Payment \(3\)\(\$406\)
Work out how much Antoine has to pay for Payment \(2\).

title: Inverse rational function
markscheme: \(y(x-6)=2x\), or \(x(y-6)=2y\). M1 for multiplying the denominator.
\(x(y-2)=6y\), or \(y(x-2)=6x\). M1 for isolating the \(x\) or \(y\) terms and factorising.
\(f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{6x}{x-2}\). Accept \(\dfrac{-6x}{2-x}\); must be a function of \(x\).
The inverse must be a function of \(x\).
body: The function \(f\) is defined as\[f:x\mapsto\dfrac{2x}{x-6}\qquad x\ne6\]
parts: Express the inverse function \(f^{-1}\) in the form \(f^{-1}:x\mapsto\ldots\).

title: Three-game total probability
markscheme: \(0.3\times0.2^2=0.012\) oe. M1 for finding WLL in any order.
\(0.5^3+3\times0.3\times0.2^2\) oe. M1 for a complete method. Alternatively, subtract the complete sum of the mutually exclusive unwanted outcomes from 1.
Award M1 for finding WWW or LLL; M1 for finding WWD, WWL, WDD, DDL, DLL or WDL in any order; and M1 for a complete complementary method.
body:
Abraham is going to play a computer game. Abraham can win the game, draw the game or lose the game. For any game that Abraham plays the probability that he wins the game is \(0.3\)
the probability that he draws the game is \(0.5\)
the probability that he loses the game is \(0.2\) When Abraham wins a game, he scores \(+10\) points.
When Abraham draws a game, he scores \(0\) points.
When Abraham loses a game, he scores \(-5\) points. Abraham plays \(3\) games and the points he scores in each of the \(3\) games are added together to get his total score. Work out the probability that when he has played \(3\) games his total score is \(0\) points.

title: Proving a surd identity
markscheme: \(\dfrac{12}{\sqrt2-1}\times\dfrac{\sqrt2+1}{\sqrt2+1}\), or an equivalent correct method for rationalising the denominator.
For example \(12\sqrt2+12-4\sqrt2\), or \(8\sqrt2+12\). Dependent expression must be in surd form.

Shown, dependent on M2, with working to the given answer. They may dismiss the \(+12\) and deal only with the surd part at this stage. Note: accept valid decompositions such as \(8\sqrt2=2\sqrt{32}\).
The final A1 is dependent on M2 for showing working to the given answer; candidates may dismiss the \(+12\) and deal only with the surd part.
body: Without using a calculator, show that \(\dfrac{12}{\sqrt2-1}-(\sqrt2)^5=2\sqrt{32}+12\). Show your working clearly.

title: Particle displacement at zero velocity
markscheme: Differentiate one term correctly, for example \(8t\) or \(\pm125t^{-2}\) oe.
Equate their \(8t\pm at^{-2}\) oe or \(bt\pm125t^{-2}\) oe to zero and solve for \(t\), with correct powers and at least one correct coefficient; \(t^3=\dfrac{125}8\), so \(t=2.5\).
Substitute into \(s\), for example \(4("2.5")^2+125/"2.5"\), dependent on the previous M mark.
The substitution mark is dependent on the previous M mark.
body:
A particle \(P\) moves along a straight line. The fixed point \(O\) lies on this line.

The displacement of \(P\) from \(O\) at time \(t\) seconds, \(t\geq1\), is \(s\) metres where\[s=4t^2+\dfrac{125}{t}\]

The velocity of \(P\) at time \(t\) seconds, \(t\geq1\), is \(v\text{ m/s}\).

Work out the distance of \(P\) from \(O\) at the instant when \(v=0\).

title: Angle in a scalene triangle
markscheme: Use their \(AC\), dependent on the first M1, in a correct sine rule, cosine rule, or triangle-area equation to find \(x\).
For example \(\sin x=9.7\sin115^\circ/"\sqrt{346}"\) oe, or the corresponding correct cosine-rule expression. Allow \(x=\sin^{-1}(\ldots)\) or \(x=\cos^{-1}(\ldots)\).
Use of their AC is dependent on the first M1. Allow \(x=\sin^{-1}(\ldots)\) or \(x=\cos^{-1}(\ldots)\).
body:
Here is triangle \(ABC\).

Work out the value of \(x\). Give your answer correct to \(3\) significant figures.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Scalene triangle \(ABC\), not accurately drawn, with \(A\) lower left, \(B\) upper centre, and \(C\) right. Label \(AB=9.7\text{ m}\), \(BC=12.3\text{ m}\), angle \(ABC=115^\circ\), and angle \(ACB=x^\circ\). Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Sector and circle areas
markscheme: Write a correct quadratic, for example \(5r^2-26r+5=0\) oe. Allow \(5r^2-26r=-5\).
Complete method to solve their three-term quadratic, dependent on M1. Allow one sign error and some simplification. Alternatively, \(4r-8=r+7\) oe.
\(r=5\), dependent on M2. The answer \(\dfrac15\) scores M1M1A1M1A0.
Allow \(ax^2+bx=c\). The quadratic-solving mark allows one sign error and some simplification.
body:
\(OAB\) is a sector \(S\) of a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \((r+7)\) metres.
Angle \(AOB=45^\circ\). A circle \(C\) has radius \((r-2)\) metres. The area of sector \(S\) is twice the area of circle \(C\). Find the value of \(r\). Show your working clearly.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Sector \(OAB\), not accurately drawn, with centre \(O\), radius labelled \((r+7)\text{ m}\), and central angle \(45^\circ\). Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Transforming a maximum point
body:
The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation \(y=f(x)\).

There is one maximum point on this curve. The coordinates of this maximum point are \((s,t)\).
parts:
Find, in terms of \(s\) and \(t\), the coordinates of the maximum point on the curve with equation

(i) \(y=f(x-2)\)

(ii) \(y=3f(x)\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Unscaled coordinate axes labelled \(x\) and \(y\), with origin \(O\). Draw a generic smooth curve \(y=f(x)\) with its single maximum marked and labelled \((s,t)\).

title: Estimating a frequency from a histogram
markscheme: \(10\div20=0.5\), or a correct value on the frequency-density scale and no errors, or \(25\) small squares \(=5\) children, or \(5\) small squares \(=1\) child oe, or \(29\) oe or \(48\) oe, or \(10\) associated with the 75–80 bar.
\((10\times2.9)+(15\times3.2)+(5\times2)\), or \(29+48+10\), or an equivalent fully correct method.
The second M1 requires a fully correct method.
body:
The histogram shows information about the total time, \(m\) minutes, taken by each child in a school to walk to school every day for one week. There are no children for whom \(m>100\).
There are \(10\) children for whom \(m\leq20\). Work out an estimate for the number of children for whom \(50
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Histogram with horizontal axis Time (\(m\) minutes) labelled \(0,20,40,60,80,100\), and unnumbered vertical axis Frequency density. Printed class boundaries are \(0,20,30,40,60,75,100\), with relative bar heights \(0.5,3.2,4.5,2.9,3.2,2.0\).

title: Cone and hemisphere volume
markscheme: Complete method: \(\dfrac12\times\dfrac43\pi20^3+\dfrac13\pi20^2\times"21"\), or equivalent. Award M4 for \(8133.3\ldots\) if \(\dfrac{24400}3\) is not seen.
\(\dfrac{24400}{3}\). As exact form was requested, \(8133.3\) or \(8133\dfrac13\) is A0. SC B4 for \(25551.62\ldots\) if no method shown.
Award M4 for \(8133.3\ldots\) if \(\dfrac{24400}3\) is not seen.
SC B4 for an answer of \(25551.62\ldots\) if no method is shown.
body:
A solid is made from a cone and a hemisphere. The circular plane face of the hemisphere coincides with the circular base of the cone.
The radius of the hemisphere and the radius of the circular base of the cone are both \(20\text{ cm}\). The curved surface area of the cone is \(580\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The volume of the solid is \(k\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Work out the exact value of \(k\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Cone above a hemisphere, not accurately drawn, sharing the same circular boundary. Label the common radius \(20\text{ cm}\). Print 'Diagram NOT accurately drawn'.

title: Polygon angles in arithmetic sequence
markscheme: Correctly substitute \(177\) and \(-2\) into \(S_n=\dfrac n2[2a+(n-1)d]\), for example \(S_n=\dfrac n2[2(177)+(n-1)(-2)]\).
Write a correct three-term quadratic, for example \(n^2+2n-360=0\) oe. Allow \(n^2+2n=360\).
Complete method to solve their three-term quadratic, dependent on M2. Allow one sign error and some simplification.
\(18\) only, dependent on M3. Alternatively use exterior angles \(3,5,7,\ldots\), with first term 3 and common difference 2, equate their sum to 360, and solve the resulting quadratic.
Allow \(ax^2+bx=c\). The quadratic-solving mark allows one sign error and some simplification.
body:
A polygon has \(n\) sides, where \(n>5\). When arranged in order of size, starting with the largest number, the sizes of the interior angles of the polygon, in degrees, are the terms of an arithmetic sequence. Here are the first five terms of this sequence.
\(177\qquad175\qquad173\qquad171\qquad169\)
Find the value of \(n\). Show clear algebraic working.

title: Parameterized completed square
markscheme: Correct factorisation, for example \(-q(x^2-\dfrac{12}{q}x)+q\), or state \(b=q\).
Start the correct process to complete the square, for example \(-q[(x-\dfrac6q)^2\ldots]\) oe.
Complete the square, for example \(-q(x-\dfrac6q)^2+\dfrac{36}{q}+q\) oe. It does not need to be simplified.

\(a=\dfrac{36}{q}+q,\ b=q,\ c=\dfrac6q\) oe. \(a\) and \(c\) must come from a correct completing-the-square process. Alternatively expand \(a-b(x-c)^2\), equate \(b=q\), \(2bc=12\), and \(a-bc^2=q\), then solve for \(a,b,c\).
The expressions do not need to be simplified. \(a\) and \(c\) must come from a correct process of completing the square.
body:
Express each of \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) in terms of \(q\) so that\[q+12x-qx^2\]

can be written as \(a-b(x-c)^2\).

title: Spinner probabilities and expectation
body:
Here is a biased spinner. When the spinner is spun once, the probabilities that it lands on red or on yellow or on green are given in the table.
Colourredyellowpurplegreen
Probability\(0.25\)\(0.2\)\(0.2\)
parts: Work out the probability that the spinner lands on red or on yellow.

Yang is going to spin the spinner \(300\) times.

Work out an estimate for the number of times the spinner will land on purple.
markscheme: For example \(300\times"0.35"\) or \(300-"195"\), for a complete method.
Allow use of their \("0.45"\) from part (a); check the table. The answer \(\dfrac{105}{300}\) scores M2 only.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A circular spinner divided into four unequal sectors labelled red at the top, yellow at the right, purple at the bottom and green at the left.

title: Shelving pattern width
body:
In a warehouse there are two types of shelves, type \(R\) and type \(S\).

These two types of shelves are arranged into shelving units that form a sequence of patterns.

Here are the first three terms in the sequence.

The width of each type \(R\) shelf is \(2.4\) m and the width of each type \(S\) shelf is \(3.5\) m.
parts: Work out the total width of a shelving unit that has \(6\) type \(R\) shelves.

A shelving unit has \(n\) type \(R\) shelves.
The total width of this shelving unit is \(W\) metres. Find an expression for \(W\) in terms of \(n\).
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: \(5.9n-3.5\) oe, but must be in simplest form, for example \(-3.5+5.9n\).
The final expression must be in simplest form.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Three shelving-unit patterns, not accurately drawn. Term 1 is R–S–R; term 2 is R–S–R–S–R; term 3 is R–S–R–S–R–S–R. Terms 1 and 2 sit side by side on the first row with term 3 below them. The R shelves are shaded and taller than the S shelves. Beneath term 2, a double-headed dimension arrow spanning its FIRST R shelf reads 2.4 m and one spanning its SECOND S shelf reads 3.5 m. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Missing value from a mean
body:
Here are five cards. Each card has a number written on it.
\(15\qquad7\qquad-2\qquad23\qquad x\)
The mean of the five numbers is \(12\). Work out the value of \(x\).
markscheme: \(5\times12=60\), or \((15+7-2+23+x)/5=12\) oe, for a method to find the total or set up an equation in \(x\).

title: Percentage comparison of language groups
body:
The language department of a college has \(180\) students.
Each student studies exactly one of French, German, Italian or Spanish. \(15\) students study French.
\(45\%\) of the students study German. Express the percentage of students studying Italian or Spanish as a percentage of those studying French or German.
markscheme: For example \(180-15-"81"=84\), or \("81"+15=96\), or equivalent fraction, decimal or percentage methods.
For example \("84"/(180-"84")\times100\), or \("84"/"96"\times100\), for a complete method.
\(81\), \(84\), or \(96\) may be seen as part of an equation.

title: Expansion, factorisation and roots
markscheme: \(3c^4+12c^3\). B2 for both terms; B1 for \(3c^4\) or \(12c^3\).
Award B1 for either correct term.
(ii) \(-9,1\), ft dependent on factorising in the form \((x+p)(x+q)\).
The final mark is ft and dependent on a factorised form.

title: Mixed-number fraction proof
body: Show that\[2\dfrac23+3\dfrac34=6\dfrac5{12}\]You must write down all the stages in your working.
markscheme: Correct improper fractions, or fractional parts written correctly over a common denominator, for example \(\dfrac83+\dfrac{15}4\) or \(2\,\dfrac8{12}+3\,\dfrac9{12}\).
Correct fractions with common denominator 12 or a multiple, for example \(\dfrac{32}{12}+\dfrac{45}{12}\), or \(2\,\dfrac8{12}+3\,\dfrac9{12}=5\,\dfrac{17}{12}\) oe.
Shown, dependent on M2, from fully correct working; or show both sides equal \(\dfrac{77}{12}\).
A correct answer without the required intermediate working does not earn the final A1.

title: Density of an iron cylinder
body:
The diagram shows a solid cylinder made from iron. The cylinder has diameter \(18\) cm and height \(3.5\) cm.
The mass of the cylinder is \(7.04\) kg. Work out the density of the iron.
Give your answer in \(\text{g/cm}^3\) correct to \(2\) significant figures.
markscheme: Correct method for volume, for example \(V=\pi\left(\dfrac{18}2\right)^2(3.5)=890.64\ldots\) or \(567\pi/2\).
Correct density method, for example \((7.04\times1000)/"890.64"\). If volume is incorrect, their clearly labelled value may be used.
Accept use of 7.04 or an incorrect conversion from kg to g for the mass method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. A solid upright cylinder, not accurately drawn. The vertical height is labelled 3.5 cm and the horizontal diameter across the base is labelled 18 cm. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Car depreciation
body:
Jane bought a new car for \(\$18\,000\).
The car depreciates in value by \(15\%\) each year. Work out the value of the car at the end of \(4\) years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar.
markscheme: \(18000\times0.85^4\) oe, or repeated multiplication by \(0.85\), dependent on M1.

title: Solving a linear inequality
body: Solve the inequality\[3-4x\leq11\]
markscheme: \(-4x\leq11-3\), or \(-4x\leq8\), or equivalent. Allow equals sign or condone an incorrect inequality sign for M1 only.
SC B1 for \(x\) and \(-2\) with an incorrect sign between them, or \(-2\) as an answer.

title: Equation of a plotted line
body:
Line \(L\) is drawn on the grid. Find an equation for \(L\).
Give your answer in the form \(y=mx+c\).
markscheme: Correct method to find gradient, for example \(3\div2=1.5=\dfrac32\), or correct value \(c=-1\).
Use \(y=mx+c\) with either \(m\) or \(c\) correct, with \(m\ne0\), or \(y-5=m(x-4)\).
For the gradient, a correct calculation or \(\dfrac32\) oe may be seen; for the intercept allow \(c=-1\), \(y=-1\), or \(L=mx-1\) oe.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Coordinate grid with x-axis from −4 to 6 and y-axis from −3 to 6, both at unit intervals, origin labelled O. Straight line L passes through (0,−1) and (4,5).

title: Length from a quadrilateral area
body:
The diagram shows a quadrilateral \(ABCD\). In the diagram, \(ABC\) and \(DAC\) are right-angled triangles.
\(BC=6\) cm and \(AC=7.5\) cm.
The area of quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is \(31.5\text{ cm}^2\). Work out the length of \(AD\).
markscheme: Correct first step to find \(AB\), or complete method for angle \(BAC\) or \(BCA\), for example \(AB^2=7.5^2-6^2\) or \(\sin BAC=\dfrac6{7.5}\).
Area \(ABC=\dfrac12\times6\times"4.5"=13.5\), ft their labelled \(AB\) or angle \(BCA\).
Area \(DAC=31.5-"13.5"=18\), ft dependent on previous M1.
\(AD=("18"\div7.5)\div0.5\) oe, complete method dependent on correct working.
Follow-through requires the candidate’s value to be clearly labelled.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Quadrilateral ABCD, not accurately drawn, split by diagonal AC. A is left-centre, B lower-left, C lower-right and D upper-centre. Triangles ABC and DAC are right-angled at B and A respectively. Label BC = 6 cm and AC = 7.5 cm. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: HCF and prime-power product
body:
\(P=3^3\times5^2\times7\)
\(Q=3^2\times5\times7^2\)
parts: Write down the highest common factor (HCF) of \(P\) and \(Q\).

Work out the value of \(P^3\times Q\).
Give your answer in the form \(3^x\times5^y\times7^z\), where \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\) are positive integers.
markscheme: Award B1 for an answer \(3^p\times5^q\times7^r\) where one or two indices are correct.

title: Interquartile range
body:
Here is the number of runs scored by a baseball team in each of its \(15\) games this season.
The numbers of runs have been arranged in order of size.
\(0\quad1\quad1\quad3\quad5\quad6\quad7\quad7\quad8\quad9\quad9\quad12\quad12\quad15\quad16\)
Work out the interquartile range of the number of runs.
markscheme: Identify both quartiles unambiguously as \(12\) and \(3\).
Both quartile values must be unambiguously identified for M1.

title: Simultaneous linear equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[3x-5y=25\]\[4x+3y=14\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Correct elimination or substitution method: coefficients of one variable equal and correct operation, or correctly write one variable in terms of the other and substitute. Condone one arithmetical error.
Substitute the found variable, dependent on M1, or repeat the elimination/substitution steps for the second variable.
\(x=5,\ y=-2\), cao and dependent on M1.
A correct answer without working scores no marks.

title: Angle in a cyclic configuration
body:
\(P,Q,R\) and \(S\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\).

\(PS\) is a diameter of the circle.

Angle \(PQR=136^\circ\).

Work out the size of angle \(RPS\).
markscheme: \(RPS=180^\circ-90^\circ-"44^\circ"\) oe, or \(RQS=136^\circ-90^\circ=46^\circ\), for a complete method.
The angle used for M1 may be seen on the diagram but must be labelled or identified with three-letter notation.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Circle, not accurately drawn, with P at lower-left, Q upper-left, R at top and S at right. PS is a diameter through centre O. Chords PQ, QR and RS are drawn; angle PQR is labelled 136°. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Triple expansion and negative index
markscheme: Correct intention to multiply all three factors by first multiplying two factors; allow one error.
Expand by the third factor, dependent and ft; allow one error.
Alternative: M2 for a complete eight-term expansion with at least four correct terms.
One of reciprocating, simplifying, or squaring performed correctly.
Two of reciprocating, simplifying, or squaring performed correctly.
Alternative: M2 for two correct terms; M1 for one correct term.

title: Diagonal of a parallelogram from area
body:
Here is a parallelogram \(PQRS\), in which angle \(SPQ\) is acute.
\(PQ=6.1\) cm and \(PS=3.8\) cm.
The area of the parallelogram is \(18\text{ cm}^2\). Work out the length of \(QS\).
Give your answer correct to \(3\) significant figures.
markscheme: Correct area equation, for example \(\dfrac12(6.1)(3.8)\sin P=9\), or calculate perpendicular height from \(6.1\times SX=18\).
Correct expression for \(\sin P\), or start Pythagoras to find \(PX\).
Complete method to find angle \(P\), or method to find \(QX\).
Correct expression for \(QS^2\) or \(QS\), for example cosine rule using their angle or Pythagoras using their height and base.
The point X is vertically below S on PQ in the alternative construction.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Parallelogram PQRS, not accurately drawn, with P lower-left, Q lower-right, R upper-right and S upper-left; angle SPQ is acute. Label PS = 3.8 cm and PQ = 6.1 cm. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Midpoint distance through a cube
body:
The diagram shows a cube \(ABCDEFGH\) with sides of length \(6\) cm. \(T\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(V\) is the midpoint of \(CH\). Work out the distance from \(T\) to \(V\) in a straight line through the cube.
Give your answer in the form \(\sqrt a\) cm, where \(a\) is an integer.
markscheme: Correct expression for a length squared in the cube, for example \(BV^2=3^2+6^2=45\), \(DH^2=6^2+6^2=72\), or \(MV^2=3^2+3^2=18\).
Complete Pythagoras method for that length, for example \(BV=\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt5\).
Correct expression for \(VT\), for example \(VT=\sqrt{45+3^2}\), or \(\sqrt{18+6^2}\).
\(\sqrt{54}\). If \(54\) is seen and answer then given as \(3\sqrt6\), isw and award full marks.
M3 may be awarded directly for \(VT=\sqrt{6^2+3^2+3^2}=3\sqrt6\); M2 for \(VT^2=54\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Oblique wireframe cube ABCDEFGH, not accurately drawn, with top face ABGF and bottom face DCHE. Every side has length 6 cm. T is marked at the midpoint of AB and V at the midpoint of CH. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Frequency from an unscaled histogram
body:
The histogram gives information about the height, \(h\) cm, of each tree in part of a forest.

There are no trees for which \(h\leq200\) and for which \(h>800\).

The number of trees for which \(300<h\leq400\) is \(8\) fewer than the number of trees for which \(400<h\leq500\).

Work out an estimate for the number of trees in this part of the forest that have a height greater than \(500\) cm.
markscheme: Use the histogram grid to establish scale, for example four large squares represent 8 trees, or one large square represents 2 trees, or a correct frequency for any bar.
Correct method for total number of trees greater than \(500\) cm, for example \(5\times2+2\times2\) oe.
Accept a frequency-density scale where one large vertical square is \(0.04\), with no contradictions.
figureNote: A histogram on 2 mm graph paper. Height (h cm) runs 100 to 850, labelled every 100 as far as 800; the Frequency density axis carries no number but 0, and nothing in the question pins it - the answer comes from the ratio of areas. The class boundaries are 200, 250, 300, 400, 450, 600 and 800, and the bars are 25, 20, 15, 37.5, 12.5 and 2.5 small squares tall.

title: Surface-area reduction of similar statues
body:
The diagram shows two similar metal statues. The volume of statue \(B\) is \(20\%\) less than the volume of statue \(A\). The surface area of statue \(B\) is \(k\%\) less than the surface area of statue \(A\). Work out the value of \(k\).
Give your answer correct to \(3\) significant figures.
markscheme: Correct linear scale factor, for example \(\sqrt[3]{0.8}=0.928\ldots\), \(\sqrt[3]{1.25}\), or \(\sqrt[3]4:\sqrt[3]5\) oe.
Correct area scale factor, for example \((\sqrt[3]{0.8})^2=0.861\ldots\), or equivalent.
Method for percentage reduction, for example \((1-"0.861\ldots")\times100\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two similar stylised metal statues, not accurately drawn, labelled A beneath the larger left statue and B beneath the smaller right statue. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Simplifying a surd fraction
body:
Express\[\dfrac{3+\sqrt8}{(\sqrt2-1)^2}\]in the form \(p+\sqrt q\), where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers.

Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: Expand denominator \((\sqrt2-1)^2=3-2\sqrt2\), or rationalise using \((\sqrt2+1)^2\). Must see expansion.
Method to rationalise, or correct expansion of \((\sqrt2-1)^2\), \((\sqrt2+1)^2\), or \((\sqrt2-1)(\sqrt2+1)\), oe ft.
Correct expansion of brackets, dependent on the second M1.
\(17+\sqrt{288}\), or \(p=17,q=288\), from fully correct working with intermediate steps shown.
The final answer must follow from fully correct working; intermediate steps are required.

title: Turning points of reciprocal curves
body:
The diagram shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation \(y=x^2-\dfrac px\), where \(p\) is a positive constant.

For all values of \(p\), the curve has exactly one turning point and this turning point is a minimum shown as the point \(T\) in the sketch.
parts: For the curve where the \(x\)-coordinate of \(T\) is \(-3\), find the value of \(p\).

The line with equation \(y=k\) is a tangent to the curve with equation \(y=x^2-\dfrac{16}{x}\).
Find the value of \(k\).
markscheme: \(dy/dx=2x+px^{-2}\) oe. M2 for both terms correct; M1 for one term correct.
Substitute \(-3\) into a derivative of the form \(ax+bx^{-2}\), dependent on M1, and set equal to zero.
Set \(dy/dx=2x+16x^{-2}=0\), with at least one derivative term correct.
Rearrange the correct equation to remove the negative power: \(2x^3+16=0\), so \(x=-2\).
The derivative must be set equal to zero for the first method mark.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE for part (a). Sketch, not accurately drawn, of the negative-x branch of y = x² − p/x on coordinate axes labelled x and y with origin O. The curve falls to one minimum turning point T above the x-axis and to the left of O, then rises steeply towards the y-axis. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Completing the square and minimum point
parts: Express \(2x^2-12x+3\) in the form \(a(x+b)^2+c\), where \(a,b\) and \(c\) are integers.

The curve \(C\) has equation \(y=2(x+4)^2-12(x+4)+3\).

The point \(M\) is the minimum point on \(C\).

Find the coordinates of \(M\).
markscheme: \(2(x^2-6x)+3\), or start an equivalent completing-the-square process. M1 also for one of \(a,b,c\) correct.
\(2[(x-3)^2-9]+3\) oe. M1 also for two of \(a,b,c\) correct.
\((-1,-15)\). B2ft; accept their \(-b-4\) for the x-coordinate or their \(c\) for the y-coordinate.
Award B1 ft for one correct coordinate.

title: Turning two-sided counters
body:
Elliot has \(x\) counters. Each counter has one red face and one green face. Elliot spreads all the counters out on a table and sees that the number of counters showing a red face is \(5\). Elliot then picks at random one of the counters and turns the counter over.
He then picks at random a second counter and turns the counter over. The probability that there are still \(5\) counters showing a red face is \(\dfrac{19}{32}\).
Work out the value of \(x\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Correct expression for \(P(R,G)\) or \(P(G,R)\), for example \(5/x\times(x-4)/x\) oe.
Correct quadratic equation, \(19x^2-352x+1600=0\) oe, or \(19x^2-352x=-1600\) oe.
Solve their three-term quadratic by a correct method. If factorising, allow brackets giving two of three correct terms; formula/completing square allows one sign error and some simplification.
\(8\), cao and dependent on M2. Do not award if a non-integer solution is also given; 8 must come from correct working.
For the quadratic formula or completing the square, allow one sign error and simplification as far as the stated discriminant form.

title: Arithmetic-series constraints
body:
The sum of the first \(10\) terms of an arithmetic series is \(4\) times the sum of the first \(5\) terms of the same series. The \(8\)th term of this series is \(45\). Find the first term of this series.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Correct expression for \(S_{10}\), \(S_5\), or the eighth term, for example \(S_{10}=10(2a+9d)/2\) or \(a+7d=45\).
Dependent on M1, obtain \(d\) in terms of \(a\), or vice versa, or correctly reduce and substitute to an equation in one variable.
Dependent on M2, form a correct one-variable equation, obtain \(d=6\), or correctly eliminate one variable; condone one arithmetical error.
Take 9 as their 10−1, 4 as their 5−1, and 7 as their 8−1.
The final A1 is dependent on M3.

title: Integers from summary statistics
body:
Here are some integers where \(aThe median of the integers is \(8\).
The range of the integers is \(4\). Work out the value of \(a\), the value of \(b\), the value of \(c\) and the value of \(d\).
markscheme: Obtain \(d=9\), or use \((c+d)\div2=8\), or \(d-a=4\), algebraically or with clearly labelled integers.
Obtain at least two of \(a=5\), \(c=7\), \(d=9\), or use either stated condition.
The conditions may be shown algebraically or by clearly labelled integers.

title: Graphing linear inequalities
parts:
On the grid, draw and label with its equation the straight line with equation

(i) \(y=1\)  (ii) \(x=2\)  (iii) \(x+y=7\).

Show, by shading on the grid, the region that satisfies all three of the inequalities\[y\geq1\qquad x\geq2\qquad x+y\leq7\]

Label the region \(R\).
markscheme: Allow dashed or solid lines. Condone missing labels if unambiguous.
Correct region indicated, shaded in or out, and labelled \(R\), or clear intention. Ft only for one vertical, one horizontal and one negative-gradient line.
Each boundary line must be at least 2 cm long and the shaded area must be enclosed.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Blank square coordinate grid for parts (a) and (b), with both axes from 0 to 8 at unit intervals, axes labelled x and y, and origin labelled O.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. On the same 0-to-8 grid draw and label y = 1, x = 2 and x + y = 7. Shade the triangular common region with vertices (2,1), (2,5) and (6,1), and label it R.

title: Average aeroplane speed
body:
An aeroplane travelled from New York City to Los Angeles. The aeroplane travelled a distance of \(3980\) kilometres in \(5\) hours \(24\) minutes. Work out the average speed of the aeroplane.
Give your answer in kilometres per hour correct to the nearest whole number.
markscheme: Sight of \(5\) h \(24\) min \(=5.4\) h oe, or \(324\) minutes, or \(19440\) seconds.
\(3980\div5.4\), or \(\dfrac{3980}{324}\times60\) oe, distance divided by time to give km/h.
SC: allow \(3980\div5.24\) for M1 unless 324 minutes or 5.4 hours oe has been awarded. If no working, 738 scores SC B2.

title: Subtracting mixed numbers
body: Show that\[5\dfrac13-2\dfrac67=2\dfrac{10}{21}\]You must write down all the stages in your working.
markscheme: Correct improper fractions, or fractional parts over a common denominator, for example \(\dfrac{16}3-\dfrac{20}7\) or \(5\,\dfrac7{21}-2\,\dfrac{18}{21}\).
Correct fractions with a common denominator and minus sign, for example \(\dfrac{112}{21}-\dfrac{60}{21}\), or mixed-number working to the stated stage.
Shown, dependent on M2, from fully correct working.
If all three fractions are converted on the first line, candidates must clearly show that the left-hand side equals \(\dfrac{52}{21}\).

title: Missing length in a compound shape
body:
The diagram shows an \(8\)-sided shape \(ABCDEFGH\).
\(HG=28\) cm, \(FG=12\) cm and \(AB=EF=5\) cm.
The height of the shape is \(20\) cm.
\(CD\) is parallel to \(HG\). The area of shape \(ABCDEFGH\) is \(434\text{ cm}^2\). Find the length of \(CD\).
markscheme: Correct rectangle area, for example \(28\times12=336\), \(5\times12=60\), or correct trapezium-area expression with numbers substituted.
Correct use of their values from correct working in an equation involving \(CD\), for example \("336"+0.5("18"+CD)"8"=434\) oe.
Correct process to solve a correct equation, or correct process to find \(CD\) using correct values.
Numbers in quotation marks must come from correct working. Check the diagram for labelled areas.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Irregular symmetric-looking 8-sided shape ABCDEFGH, not accurately drawn. A and B form a 5 cm horizontal inset on the upper-left, C–D is the top horizontal side, E and F form a 5 cm horizontal inset on the upper-right, FG is the 12 cm right vertical side, and HG is the 28 cm bottom horizontal side. The overall vertical height is 20 cm. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Right-triangle side
body:
The diagram shows triangle \(PQR\). Work out the value of \(x\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Correct trig statement for \(x\), for example \(\cos42^\circ=x/9.5\), or correct Pythagoras expression for \(x^2\).
Equivalent sine, tangent, or Pythagoras methods are accepted.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Right-angled triangle PQR, not accurately drawn, with right angle at Q, vertical side PQ labelled x cm, hypotenuse PR labelled 9.5 cm, and angle QPR labelled 42°. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Speed unit conversion
body: Change a speed of \(81\) kilometres per hour to a speed in metres per second.
markscheme: One of multiply by 1000, divide by 60 twice, divide by 3600 oe, or sight of \(81000\), \(1350\), or \(0.0225\).
Fully correct method with correct brackets, for example \(81\times1000/(60\times60)\), \(\dfrac{81}{3.6}\), or \(81\times5/18\).
An unbracketed calculation such as 81000 ÷ 60 × 60 is M1 only unless recovered.

title: Celebration cards with numbers
body:
Behnaz makes \(300\) celebration cards so that number of birthday cards : number of anniversary cards : number of congratulations cards = 7 : 5 : 3 \(\dfrac25\) of the birthday cards have numbers on them.
\(36\%\) of the anniversary cards have numbers on them.
None of the congratulations cards have numbers on them. Work out what fraction of the \(300\) cards have numbers on them.
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: \(300\div(7+5+3)=20\), or clear correct use of the total ratio 15.
\(\dfrac25(7\times"20")=56\) oe, finding two-fifths of the birthday cards.
Any unsimplified fraction from correct working, for example \(("56"+"36")/300\), or \(0.3066\ldots\).
No mark for 15 unless it is used correctly; use of 140 or 100 in further work assumes the first M1.

title: Compound interest
body:
Pasha invests \(50\,000\) dollars in a savings account for \(4\) years.
He gets \(1.3\%\) per year compound interest. Work out how much money Pasha will have in his savings account at the end of \(4\) years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar.
markscheme: Complete compound-interest method, for example repeated multiplication by \(1.013\), dependent on M1.
M2 for \(50000\times1.013^4\) or \(50000\times1.013^5\). If no marks, SC B1 for the listed one-step or wrong-year compound expressions.

title: Simultaneous linear equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[7x+3y=3\]\[3x-y=7\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Correct elimination or substitution method; allow one total multiplication error with correct eliminating operation.
Dependent on M1, correct method to calculate the other variable; an incorrect value obtained from a correct method may be substituted.
A correct answer alone is not sufficient because clear algebraic working is required.

title: Factorising and solving a quadratic
markscheme: (ii) \(3,-8\), ft from their factors in the form \((x+a)(x+b)\).
The root mark must follow through from a factorised expression.

title: Parcel mean weights
body:
Larry is a delivery man. He has \(7\) parcels to deliver.
The mean weight of the \(7\) parcels is \(2.7\) kg. Larry delivers \(3\) of the parcels.
Each of these \(3\) parcels has a weight of \(W\) kg. The mean weight of the other \(4\) parcels is \(3.3\) kg. Work out the value of \(W\).
markscheme: \(7\times2.7=18.9\), or \(4\times3.3=13.2\), or a correct equation in \(W\).
If 1.9 is obtained from correct working and then altered, award M2.

title: Cumulative frequency and commuters
body:
The table gives information about the ages, in years, of \(80\) people in a train carriage.
Age (\(a\) years)Frequency
\(0\(7\)
\(20\(25\)
\(30\(20\)
\(40\(14\)
\(50\(8\)
\(60\(6\)
parts:
Complete the cumulative frequency table.
Age (\(a\) years)Cumulative frequency
\(0
\(0
\(0
\(0
\(0
\(0
On the grid, draw a cumulative frequency graph for your table.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the median age of the \(80\) people.

Of the people in the train carriage, \(60\%\) of those who are aged between \(18\) and \(65\) are going to work.
None of the other people in the train carriage are going to work. Use your graph to find an estimate for the number of people in the train carriage who are going to work.
markscheme: Fully correct cumulative-frequency graph: points at upper interval ends, joined by a curve or line segments.

If not B2, award B1 ft from a table with only one arithmetic error for five or six correctly plotted points, or consistent within-interval plotting joined correctly. Ignore the segment from 0 to the first point.
\(32\)–\(34\), ft their ascending graph reading across at 40 or 40.5.
Correct method to take readings at 18 and 65, for example 6 and 77, even if values are not written; ft an ascending graph.
\((77-6)\times0.6\) oe, ft dependent on previous M1 and their difference.
\(42,43\), or \(44\), ft their graph; answer must be a whole number.
For the final accuracy mark all readings must be correct; a whole-number answer may be rounded or truncated.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE for parts (b), (c) and (d). Blank cumulative-frequency grid with Age (years) on the horizontal axis from 0 to 70 at intervals of 10 and Cumulative frequency on the vertical axis from 0 to 80 at intervals of 10.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Plot cumulative-frequency points (0,0), (20,7), (30,32), (40,52), (50,66), (60,74), (70,80), joined by a smooth increasing curve.

title: Triple expansion and changing the subject
parts:
Expand and simplify \((5-x)(2x+3)(x+4)\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Multiply two factors only, allowing one error, for example \((5-x)(2x+3)=-2x^2+7x+15\).
Expand by the third factor, dependent and ft, allowing one further error.
Alternative: M2 for a complete eight-term expansion with at least four correct terms; M1 for four correct terms from any number of terms.
Add 7 to both sides first, or remove the fraction correctly.
Remove the fraction and expand all brackets in an equation with no more than one error.
Collect terms in \(c\) on one side and other terms on the other, ft dependent on previous M1.
If “c =” is missing, allow full marks if seen in working; otherwise maximum 3. SC B2 and B1 alternatives apply as stated in the source.

title: Fractional equation and quadratic inequality
parts:
Solve the inequality \(2y^2-7y-30\leq0\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Write over a common denominator or remove denominators, for example \([2(4x+5)-3(3-2x)]/6=13\) oe. Allow one error in removing brackets.
Remove brackets and fractions correctly in an equation, ft dependent on previous M1.
Put terms in \(x\) on one side and constants on the other, ft dependent on previous M1.
\(x=5.5\) oe, for example \(\dfrac{11}2\), dependent on M2.
Correct quadratic-solving method, for example \((2y+5)(y-6)\), formula, or completing square; stated allowances apply.
Critical values \(6\) and \(-2.5\), dependent on M1.
Do not penalise a change of variable, for example y to x.

title: Three-set Venn diagram
body:
\(100\) farmers are asked if they have goats \((G)\), sheep \((S)\) or chickens \((C)\) on their farms. Of these farmers:
\(31\) have sheep;
\(53\) have chickens;
\(6\) have goats, sheep and chickens;
\(11\) have sheep and goats;
\(17\) have sheep and chickens;
\(18\) have goats and chickens;
\(20\) do not have any goats, sheep or chickens.
parts: Using this information, complete the Venn diagram to show the number of farmers in each appropriate subset.

One of the farmers who has chickens is chosen at random.

Find the probability that this farmer also has goats.
markscheme: All seven other regions correct. B2; award B1 for four, five or six others correct.
The diagram need not be complete for the partial B1.
(i) \(36\), ft from a diagram with values in the required regions.
If these are given as probabilities, mark the first incorrect but award subsequent marks where the numerator is correct.
Award B1 for \(18/m\) where \(m>18\), \(n/53\) where \(n<53\), \(18:53\), or corresponding ft forms.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE for part (a). Blank three-set Venn diagram inside universal set E, with G the left circle, S the right circle and C the lower circle.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE. Complete the Venn diagram with 6 in the triple intersection, 5 in G∩S only, 12 in G∩C only, 11 in S∩C only, 9 in S only, 24 in C only, 13 in G only and 20 outside all circles.

title: Direct proportionality to a cube
body:
\(M\) varies directly as the cube of \(h\).
\(M=4\) when \(h=0.5\). Find the value of \(h\) when \(M=500\).
markscheme: \(k=\dfrac4{0.5^3}=32\). Allow this for M2 if \(M=kh^3\) is not written.
\(h=\sqrt[3]{500/"32"}\), or equivalent correct expression using correct values.

title: Upper bound of a formula
body:
\[X=\dfrac{2a-b}{f}\]\(a=7.5\) correct to \(1\) decimal place.
\(b=3.42\) correct to \(2\) decimal places.
\(f=2\) correct to the nearest whole number. Work out the upper bound of the value of \(X\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: One correct upper or lower bound from \(7.45,7.55,3.415,3.425,1.5,2.5\).
\((2\times7.55-3.415)/1.5\) oe, using \(2\times UB_a-LB_b\) over \(LB_f\) within stated ranges.
Allow recurring-nine equivalents for the upper bounds.

title: Substitution into a rational expression
body:
\[a=\dfrac{14}{3x-7}\qquad x=\dfrac7{4y-3}\]Express \(a\) in the form \(\dfrac{py+q}{ry+s}\), where \(p,q,r\) and \(s\) are integers.
Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: \(14(4y-3)/(21-7(4y-3))\) oe, or a correct unsimplified single fraction.
Alternative: rearrange x in terms of a and equate the two expressions, then simplify.

title: Four circles in a square
body:
The diagram shows four identical circles drawn inside a square. Each circle touches two other circles and two sides of the square. The region inside the square that is outside the circles, shown shaded in the diagram, has a total area of \(40\text{ cm}^2\). Work out the perimeter of the square.
Give your answer correct to \(3\) significant figures.
markscheme: Correct one-variable expression or equation for shaded area, for example \(4r\times4r-4\pi r^2=40\) oe.
Correct expression for \(r\), diameter, or square side, for example \(4r=\sqrt{640/(16-4\pi)}\) oe.
Substitute their correct dimension into a perimeter calculation, ft dependent on first M1.
The equation must contain only one unknown; accepted unknowns are radius, diameter, whole-square side, or quarter-square side.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Square, not accurately drawn, containing four equal circles in a 2-by-2 arrangement. Each circle touches two neighbouring circles and two sides of the square. Shade only the region inside the square and outside all four circles. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Vector intersection ratio
body:
\(OAB\) is a triangle.
\(Q\) is the point on \(AB\) such that \(OQP\) is a straight line.
\(\overrightarrow{OA}=4\mathbf a\), \(\overrightarrow{OB}=6\mathbf b\), and \(\overrightarrow{AP}=2\mathbf a+8\mathbf b\).
Using a vector method, find the ratio \(AQ:QB\).
markscheme: One correct vector, for example \(OP=6a+8b\), \(AB=6b-4a\), or \(BP=6a+2b\) oe.
One correct expression for a vector involving \(Q\), for example \(OQ=4a+\lambda(6b-4a)\) oe.
A second correct expression for the same vector, or two correct parallel-vector expressions used to form an equation in one variable.
A correct vector may be seen as part of another vector calculation.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Triangle OAB, not accurately drawn, with O lower-left, A upper-centre and B lower-right. Q lies on AB, and the straight line OQP continues beyond Q to P above-right. Label vector OA as 4a and vector OB as 6b. Print Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Coordinates of kite vertices
body:
\(ABCD\) is a kite, with diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\), drawn on a centimetre square grid, with a scale of \(1\) cm for \(1\) unit on each axis.

\(A\) is the point with coordinates \((-3,4)\).

The diagonals of the kite intersect at the point \(M\) with coordinates \((0,2)\).

Given that \(AB=AD=6.5\) cm and the \(x\)-coordinate of \(B\) is positive, find the coordinates of the points \(B\) and \(D\).
markscheme: Correct method for gradient of \(AM\): \((4-2)/(-3-0)=-\dfrac23\) oe.
Correct equation of line \(BD\), for example \(y=\dfrac32x+2\), or correct coordinate expression for \(B\) or \(D\).
Correct equation in \(x,y\), for example \((x+3)^2+(y-4)^2=6.5^2\) or \(x^2+(y-2)^2=29.25\).
Correct substitution into a correct equation to obtain an equation in one variable.
Fully correct simplified one-variable equation with brackets expanded and like terms grouped.

SC B3 for one correct coordinate pair, both x-values correct, or both y-values correct. Alternative: use Pythagoras to obtain AM = √13 and BM = \(\dfrac{3\sqrt{13}}2\), scale the components of AM by \(\dfrac32\) to obtain translations (3, 4.5) and (−3, −4.5), then translate M.

title: Cosine graph coordinates
body: The diagram shows a sketch of the graph of \(y=\cos\left(\dfrac x2\right)^\circ\).
parts:
(i) Find the coordinates of the point \(A\).

(ii) Find the coordinates of the point \(B\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Sketch of y = \cos(x/2)° on coordinate axes labelled x and y with origin O. A is the first positive x-intercept and B is the first minimum below the x-axis. The curve is labelled with its equation.

title: Solving an exponential equation
body:
\[\dfrac{18\times\left(\sqrt{27}\right)^{4n+6}}{6\times9^{2n+8}}=3^x\]Express \(x\) in terms of \(n\).
Show your working clearly and simplify your expression.
markscheme: Two of: write \(18=2\times3^2\) and \(6=2\times3\), or cancel fully; write \(\sqrt{27}=3^{3/2}\); write \(9=3^2\) and apply the power law.
Correct expression or equation using only powers of 3, not necessarily a single power.
\(x=2n-6\) oe, for example \(2(n-3)\), dependent on M1.
\(\sqrt{27}\) must be changed to a power of 3; \(3^3\) is not accepted unless recovered.

title: Coordinate transformations
parts: Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle \(A\) onto triangle \(B\).

On the grid above, translate triangle \(A\) by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}-4\\3\end{pmatrix}\).
Label your triangle \(C\).
markscheme: Enlargement, enlarge, or enlarged, with no mention of translate, reflect, rotate, move, or flip.
Scale factor \(3\), SF 3, \(\times3\), factor of 3, or “three times”, with no mention of a vector, symmetry line, or angle.
For the description marks, do not accept an answer contaminated by a different transformation attribute.
Triangle drawn at \((1,4),(1,6),(2,4)\). Condone missing label.
The translated triangle may be drawn with solid or dashed sides.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Coordinate grid with x-axis from 0 to 14 and y-axis from 0 to 10, ruled every 1 and numbered every 2, origin labelled O. Triangle A has vertices (5,1), (5,3), (6,1). Triangle B has vertices (9,3), (9,9), (12,3). Both are shaded.
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE for part (b). Add triangle C with vertices (1,4), (1,6), (2,4), labelled C.

title: Prime factorisation of 1200
body:
Write \(1200\) as a product of powers of its prime factors.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: At least two correct stages in prime factorisation giving two prime factors; allow no more than one mistake ft. May be a factor tree, table, or list.
Correct prime factors \(2,2,2,2,3,5,5\). Condone inclusion of 1.
\(2^4\times3\times5^2\), dependent on M2, in any order and index form.
Working was requested, so the final A1 is dependent on both method marks.

title: Missing heights from median and range
body:
Alberto, Bill, Candela and Diana are four friends. Here is some information about the height of each of these friends. Alberto’s height is \(158\) cm.
Bill’s height is \(175\) cm.
Candela’s height is greater than Diana’s height. The median height of these four friends is \(160\) cm.
The range of the heights of these four friends is \(21\) cm. Work out Candela’s height and Diana’s height.
markscheme: Method for Candela’s height, for example \((158+C)/2=160\), or \(C=160+(160-158)=162\) oe.
Independently, method for Diana’s height, for example \(175-21=154\) oe.
A correct height on the wrong answer line earns its method mark. If no marks, SC B1 for Candela 179.

title: Set notation and membership
parts:
(i) List the members of the set \(A\cap B\).

(ii) List the members of the set \(A\cup B\).

Is it true that \(24\in A\)?

Tick one of the boxes, Yes or No.

Give a reason for your answer.
