The smooth increasing curve passes approximately through (0,0), (10,3), (20,8), (30,15), (40,25), (50,40), (60,55) and (70,60).

title: Equation with algebraic fractions
body: Solve\[\dfrac{x+3}{4}-\dfrac{7-x}{5}=4.3\]Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: M1 for Clear intention to multiply all terms by 20 (or \(4\times5\)) or a multiple of 20 oe, or express the left side over a common denominator.
If the numerator is expanded, allow one error.
Note: M1 for Expanding brackets and multiplying by denominator with no more than one error in total; \(4.3\times20\) or 86 must be accurate.
A1 dep on M1. Working required.

title: Angles in a circle with tangent
body:
\(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) are points on a circle, centre \(O\).

(EBF) is the tangent to the circle at \(B\).
parts:
(i) Work out the size of angle (DCB).

(ii) Give a reason for your answer to (a)(i).
Work out the size of angle (ADO).
markscheme: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to \(180^\circ\) oe.
The reason mark is dep on B1 in (a)(i), or seeing (180-40), with no contradiction.
For (b), one of \(\text{angle }ADB=66^\circ\), \(\text{angle }ABO=24^\circ\), \(\text{angle }BAO=24^\circ\), \(\text{angle }ODB=50^\circ\), or reflex \(\text{angle }DOB=280^\circ\), clearly labelled.
A second one of those values.
figureNote: A circle with centre O, diagram not accurately drawn. Points A, D, C and B lie on the circumference in that order. Chords AB, BC, CD and DA form a cyclic quadrilateral. The angle DAB is labelled 40°. A straight tangent EBF touches the circle at B, with E to the left and F to the right; the angle between BA and BF is labelled 66°. Radii OB and OD are drawn.

title: Comparing cricket-score spread
body:
Here is a list giving the numbers of runs scored last week by the eleven members of cricket team A.\[2\quad3\quad4\quad6\quad21\quad26\quad27\quad32\quad34\quad61\quad72\] The interquartile range of the numbers of runs scored last week by the eleven members of cricket team B was 42. Using a suitable calculation, write down one comparison between the numbers of runs scored by the members of cricket team A and the members of cricket team B.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: B's scores are more spread out, or A's are more consistent, because \(42>30\).
4 and 34 clearly indicated, either in the list or working; condone 26 also indicated.
B1ft must follow through from the stated IQR for team A.
The comparison must concern IQR or spread and must not be contradicted by further statements.
Do not accept comparisons of total runs, averages, or ranges.

title: Recurring decimal proof
body: Use algebra to show that\[0.4\dot3\dot8=\dfrac{217}{495}\]
markscheme: Let \(x=0.43838\ldots\) and form aligned multiples such as \(1000x\) and \(10x\).
Select two correct recurring decimals which subtract to a whole number or terminating decimal, with intention to subtract.
If recurring dots are not shown, at least one number must be shown to at least 5 significant figures.
Completion to \(\dfrac{217}{495}\), dep on M1 and use of some algebra.

title: Simplifying and rationalising surds
parts:
Show that \(\dfrac{5-\sqrt{18}}{1-\sqrt2}\) can be written in the form \(a+b\sqrt2\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
Show each stage of your working clearly.
markscheme: Showing correct expansions, not necessarily as a fraction. Allow \(\sqrt{18}\) or \(3\sqrt2\), and \(\sqrt{36}\) or 6.
A1 dep on M2; all stages of working must be shown convincingly, or state \(a=1\) and \(b=-2\).
body: Given that\[8\sqrt m+\sqrt{49m}-\sqrt{9m}=k\sqrt m\]where \(k\) is an integer and \(m\) is a prime number,

title: Parcel-weight histogram
body:
The table gives information about the weights, in kg, of the parcels that Pedro delivers on Monday.
Weight (\(w\) kg)Frequency
\(0<w\leq2\)12
\(2<w\leq3\)7
\(3<w\leq6\)15
\(6<w\leq9\)12
\(9<w\leq14\)9
parts: On the grid, draw a histogram for this information.

One of the parcels that Pedro delivered on Monday is chosen at random.

Using the information in the table, find an estimate for the probability that this parcel weighs more than 7 kg.
markscheme: Draw all five bars with correct widths and heights.
For at least two frequency densities correct or at least two correct bars.
For at least four frequency densities correct or four correct bars.
A fully correct histogram gains full marks.
SCB2 for all five bars of correct width with heights in the correct ratio; SCB1 for three such bars.
For (b), \(9+\dfrac23\times12=17\) oe; may be seen as numerator of fraction, ft their graph dep on M1 in (a).
Accept \(\dfrac{17}{55}\), 0.30909… or 30.909…% to at least 2 sf. SCB1 for \(\dfrac{38}{55}\).
figureNote: A blank histogram grid with Weight (kg) on the horizontal axis from 0 to 14 labelled every 2, and Frequency density on the vertical axis from 0 to 8 labelled every 2.
answerFigureNote: The completed histogram has bars: 0–2 height 6; 2–3 height 7; 3–6 height 5; 6–9 height 4; 9–14 height 1.8.

title: Volumes of similar vases
body:
\(A\) and \(B\) are two similar vases.

The vases are such that

surface area of vase B = \(\dfrac{25}{64}\times\) surface area of vase A

and that

volume of vase A − volume of vase B = \(541.8\text{ cm}^3\)

Calculate the volume of vase \(B\).
markscheme: A correct scale factor for length or volume, or a correct equation for the volume of vase B.
A correct equation for the volume of B or the volume of A.
A completely correct method to find the volume of vase B or vase A.
figureNote: Larger vase outline A. No dimensions are printed. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.
figureNote2: Similarly shaped smaller vase outline B. No dimensions are printed. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Line-circle simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[y=7-2x\]\[x^2+y^2=34\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Substitution of the linear equation into the quadratic.
dep on previous M1 for multiplying out and collecting terms to form a three-term quadratic with at least two non-zero coefficients correct.
Solving their three-term quadratic by any correct method; ft dep on M1.
Substitute their two found values into a suitable equation, or correct values for the other variable; ft dep on previous M1.
Working must be shown; pairs must be matched correctly.

title: Sphere volume from surface area
body:
Given that the surface area of a sphere is \(49\pi\text{ cm}^2\), find the volume of the sphere.

Give your answer correct to the nearest integer.

title: Quadratic inequality
body: Solve the inequality\[6x^2+37x\leq35\]Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: A correct method to solve \(6x^2+37x-35=0\), allowing factorisation which expands to 2 out of 3 correct terms, one sign error in formula substitution, or completing the square as shown.
Correct critical values \(\dfrac56\) and (-7), dep on M1; allow 0.83….
Working must be seen for both accuracy marks. Accept equivalent interval notation.

title: Angle of a prism diagonal to its base
body:
The diagram shows a solid prism \(ABCDEFGHIJ\).

The prism is such that each cross section is a pentagon where

\(AE=BC=x\text{ cm}\qquad AB=2x\text{ cm}\qquad ED=CD=8\text{ cm}\)

angle \(EAB=\) angle \(CBA=90^\circ\qquad\) angle \(AED=\) angle \(BCD=120^\circ\)

Given that \(AG=BH=EF=DJ=CI=12\text{ cm}\), calculate the angle that \(AJ\) makes with the base \(ABHG\) of the prism.

Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Resolve an 8 cm sloping side: vertical component 4 and horizontal component \(4\sqrt3\).
\(DN=8\sin30^\circ\) or \(8\cos60^\circ=4\) oe, where N is the midpoint of EC.
\(x=8\cos30^\circ=4\sqrt3\) oe, with the perpendicular component, or equivalent cosine-rule method.
\(AM=\sqrt{12^2+(4\sqrt3)^2}=8\sqrt3\) oe, where M is the midpoint of GH.
Clear intention that this is AM, not EC.
Accept 38.1–38.4. If no marks scored, SCB2 for \(\tan\angle MAJ=\dfrac{4+x}{\sqrt{x^2+12^2}}\), or SCB1 for \(AM=\sqrt{x^2+12^2}\).
figureNote: A solid pentagonal prism ABCDEFGHIJ, diagram not accurately drawn. The front pentagonal cross section is ABCDE: AB is the horizontal lower edge labelled 2x cm; AE and BC are vertical sides each labelled x cm; ED and CD are the two upper sloping sides each labelled 8 cm, meeting at D; angles EAB and CBA are right angles, and angles AED and BCD are each 120°. The congruent back cross section is FGHIJ, joined by AG, BH, EF, DJ and CI, each 12 cm. The diagonal AJ is not drawn.

title: Parameters of a sine graph
body:
The graph of \(y=a\sin x^\circ+b\) is drawn on the grid.

Find the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).
figureNote: A sine curve on a coordinate grid. The horizontal x-axis is labelled 60, 120, 180, 240, 300 and 360; the vertical y-axis is labelled from −3 to 4. The curve has a maximum of 2 at x = 90, crosses its midline y = 0.5 at x = 0, 180 and 360, and has a minimum of −1 at x = 270. The origin is labelled O.

title: Inverse of a restricted quadratic
body:
The function \(f\) is such that\[f(x)=3x^2-12x+7\quad\text{where }x\leq2\]

Express the inverse function \(f^{-1}\) in the form \(f^{-1}(x)=\ldots\).
markscheme: A correct equation for a first step to complete the square.
Only the negative square root; answer must be in terms of \(x\). Allow candidates to swap \(x\) and \(y\) while finding the inverse.

title: Solving an exponential equation
body:
Find the values of \(n\) such that\[\dfrac{10^{4n}\times2^{3(n^2-5n)}\times5^{2(1-2n)}}{20^2}=1\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Express 10 and 20 in powers of 2 and 5.
Cancel all powers of 5 and combine powers of 2.
Obtain an equation in powers of 2 only.
Write \(10^{4n}\) correctly as a product of powers of 5 and 2, or write \(20^2\) correctly as a product of powers of 5 and 2, or cancel the numerator \(5^2\) with \(20^2\).
For two of those correct transformations, or obtaining the numerator as \(2^{4n}\times2^{3n^2-15n}\times5^2\) oe.
Write the equation in powers of 2 only.
Correct quadratic equation dep on M1.
Both answers required, dep on M1. Working required.

title: Dividing mixed numbers
body: Show that\[4\dfrac23\div1\dfrac56=2\dfrac6{11}\]
markscheme: Note: M1 for Both mixed numbers expressed as improper fractions.
Note: A1 for Conclusion to \(2\dfrac6{11}\) from correct working.
A1 dep on M2. Working required.

title: Rotating and translating a triangle
parts:
On the grid, rotate triangle \(A\) 180° about \((1,-1)\).
Label the new triangle \(B\).

On the grid, translate triangle \(A\) by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}-7\\3\end{pmatrix}\).

Label the new triangle \(C\).
markscheme: For (a), B2 for a correct triangle with correct orientation and position.
If not B2 then award B1 for a correct triangle with correct orientation in the wrong position, or 2 out of 3 correct vertices.
figureNote: A coordinate grid with both axes labelled from −6 to 6. Triangle A has vertices (3,1), (3,2) and (5,1). The origin is labelled O.
answerFigureNote: On the same coordinate grid, triangle B is the 180° rotation of A about (1,−1), with vertices (−1,−3), (−1,−4), (−3,−3). Triangle C is the translation of A by vector (−7,3), with vertices (−4,4), (−4,5), (−2,4).

title: Integer and number-line inequalities
parts: Find all the possible values of \(y\).
Write down the inequality shown on the number line.
markscheme: For (a), B2 for all five correct values.
If not B2 then award B1 for 4 correct and no incorrect values, or 6 values with no more than one incorrect value.
figureNote: A number line labelled from −5 to 5. There is an open circle at −1 and a bold ray extending to the right with an arrowhead.
body:
\[-8<2y\leq2\]

\(y\) is an integer.

title: Constructing an angle bisector
body:
Using ruler and compasses only, construct the bisector of angle BAC.
You must show all your construction lines.
markscheme: Draw the correct intersecting construction arcs.
Draw the angle bisector through A and the arc intersection.
B2 for a fully correct angle bisector with all relevant arcs shown.
If not B2 then B1 for all arcs and no angle bisector, or a correct bisector within the guidelines but no or insufficient correct arcs.
figureNote: An acute angle BAC with vertex A at the left, ray AB sloping upward to the right and ray AC sloping slightly downward to the right. No angle size is given.
answerFigureNote: The same angle BAC with equal-radius arcs from A cutting both rays, intersecting construction arcs from those two points, and the straight angle bisector drawn from A through the arc intersection.

title: Drawing a straight-line graph
body: On the grid, draw the graph of \(5x+2y=10\) for values of \(x\) from −2 to 4.
markscheme: Plot at least two correct points, such as \((-2,10),(0,5),(2,0),(4,-5)\).
Use enough correct points or the correct gradient and intercept.
Draw the correct line segment over the full interval.
B3 for a correct line between \(x=-2\) and \(x=4\).
If not B3 then award B2 for a line segment through at least 3 listed points, or all points plotted correctly.
If not B2 then award B1 for at least 2 correct points plotted or stated, a negative-gradient line through \((0,5)\), or a line with gradient −2.5.
figureNote: A blank coordinate grid with x-axis from −2 to 4 and y-axis from −6 to 11, labelled at each integer. The origin is labelled O.
answerFigureNote: The straight line segment y = 5 − 2.5x for −2 ≤ x ≤ 4, passing through (−2,10), (0,5), (2,0) and (4,−5).

title: Missing counter probability
body:
In a bag, there are only red counters, blue counters, green counters and yellow counters. The total number of counters in the bag is 80.
In the bag the number of red counters is \(x+7\)
the number of blue counters is \(x-11\)
the number of green counters is \(3x\). Jude takes at random a counter from the bag. The probability that he takes a red counter is \(\dfrac14\).
Work out the probability that Jude takes a yellow counter.
markscheme: For setting up a correct equation in terms of \(x\) only.
A complete method to find \(x\), or \(x=13\); award implies M2.
A method to find the number of yellow counters or \(P(R\text{ or }B\text{ or }G)\).

title: HCF and LCM from prime factors
parts: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 200 and 420.

\(A=2^3\times3\times5\times7^2\)
\(B=2\times3^2\times7\)
\(C=3\times5^2\times11\)
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\).
Write your answer as a product of powers of prime factors.
markscheme: Use prime factors of at least one number.
For (a), one number written as a product of prime factors, or at least two factors for each excluding 1 and the number itself.
For (b), \(2^m3^n5^p7^q11^r\) with at least three exponents correct and all five terms seen, or one term omitted and the others fully correct.

title: Combined mean exam mark
body:
60 students sat a Mathematics exam. The mean mark for the 32 students in Class A was 55.
The mean mark for the 28 students in Class B was 52. Find the mean mark for all 60 students.
markscheme: For one correct product or method to find the total mark for both classes.
Correct answer scores full marks unless from obvious incorrect working.

title: Investment growth and depreciation
parts:
Teresa invests $2000 for 3 years in a savings account.
She gets 4% each year compound interest. How much money will Teresa have in her savings account at the end of 3 years?
Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar.

Sam invested $\(T\).
The value of his investment decreased by 9% each year. At the end of the first year, the value of Sam’s investment was $1365. Work out the value of \(T\).
markscheme: For (a), finding 4% or 104% of 2000; M2 for \(2000\times1.04^3\) oe.
For completing the method to find the total after 3 years.
Accept 2249–2250. SC: if no other marks, award M1 for a simple 12% method.
For (b), M2 for \(1365\div0.91\); if not M2 then M1 for a correct percentage equation or division by 91.
Correct answer scores full marks unless from obvious incorrect working.

title: Density after melting two solids
body:
The diagram shows two solids, \(A\) and \(B\), made from two different metals. Solid \(A\) is in the shape of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm.
Solid \(A\) has a mass of 2000 g. Solid \(B\) has a mass of 3375 g.
Solid \(B\) has a volume of 450 cm³. All of the metal from Solid \(A\) and Solid \(B\) is melted down to make a uniform Solid \(C\). Given that there is no change to mass or volume during this process, work out the density of Solid \(C\). Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Method to find the volume of Solid A.
indep; method to find the density of Solid A, B or C, allowing their volume for A and C.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Two solids, diagram not accurately drawn. Solid A is a cylinder, taller than it is wide, with its base radius labelled 3 cm on an arrow across the top face and its height labelled 7 cm on a dimension arrow beside it; it is captioned Solid A. Solid B is an icosahedron drawn as a hexagonal silhouette with its visible triangular faces, captioned Solid B.

title: Number of sides of a regular polygon
body:
(AB), (BC), (CD), (DE) and (EF) are five sides of a regular polygon. (RST), (SCU) and (BCV) are straight lines.
(RST) is parallel to (CD).
Angle \(RSC=128^\circ\).
Angle \(UCV=32^\circ\). Work out how many sides the polygon has.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Identify \(\angle SCD=128^\circ\) or an equivalent useful angle.
Interior angle \(=128+32=160^\circ\), so exterior angle is 20°.
Use \(\dfrac{360}{20}\), or the interior-angle sum formula.
Angles must be identified or marked on the diagram. M2 for an identified interior angle 160° or exterior angle 20°.
dep on previous M1; method to find one interior or exterior angle.
Set up the interior-angle equation or \(360\div20\).
A1 dep on M2. Working required.
figureNote: Part of a regular polygon with consecutive vertices A, B, C, D, E and F, diagram not accurately drawn. A straight line RST passes through S and is parallel to side CD. The straight line SCU crosses it at S, and BC is extended through C to V. Angle RSC is labelled 128° and angle UCV is labelled 32°.

title: Indices and triple expansion
markscheme: For (b), if not B2 then B1 for \(8a^k\), \(k\ne3\), or \(ka^3\), \(k\ne8\).
For (c), correct intention to multiply all 3 factors by first multiplying 2; allow one error.
dep ft; expand by the third factor, allow one error.
isw a correct later factorisation only after the correct expanded result has been seen; do not isw incorrect simplification.

title: Percentage area reduction
body:
A rectangle has length \(L\) and width \(W\). \(L\) is increased by 20%.
\(W\) is decreased by 35%. Calculate the percentage reduction in the area of the rectangle.
markscheme: Allow other variables for \(L,W\) if clearly labelled, and \(1+0.2\), \(1-0.35\) for the multipliers.
Method to find the percentage reduction; allow the subtraction written the other way around.
Alternative: any positive numerical values for length and width with the same percentage method.

title: Perimeter of a major sector
body:
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are points on a circle, centre \(O\). The radius of the circle is 8.5 cm.
Angle \(ABC=132^\circ\). Work out the perimeter of the shaded sector (AOC).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Method to find the angle at the centre; do not award if contradicted on the diagram.
Method to find arc (AC) or perimeter of the sector, allowing their clearly labelled (angle AOC).
figureNote: A circle with centre O, diagram not accurately drawn. Points A, B and C lie on the circumference. Chords AB and BC are drawn and angle ABC is labelled 132°. Radii OA and OC bound the major sector AOC, which is shaded. One radius is labelled 8.5 cm.

title: Comparing tennis aces
body: Here are the numbers of aces that Rutger served in each of 11 tennis matches.\[1\quad1\quad2\quad4\quad6\quad8\quad8\quad9\quad11\quad12\quad15\]
parts:
Find the interquartile range of the numbers of aces.
Show your working clearly.

Kim also plays in 11 tennis matches.
For Kim, the median number of aces is 11 and the interquartile range of the numbers of aces is 5.
(i) State, giving a reason, whether Rutger or Kim served more aces on average.
(ii) State, giving a reason, whether Rutger or Kim was more consistent with the number of aces served.
markscheme: For (a), 2 and 11 clearly identified either in the list or stated.
A1 dep on M1. Working required.
For (b)(i), Kim as she has a higher median oe, ft their median if a value is given.
Do not accept merely stating both medians without a comparison, or combining median and IQR in one reason.
For (b)(ii), Kim as she has a smaller IQR oe, ft their part (a).
Do not accept merely stating both IQRs without a comparison.

title: Column vector AC
body:
Here are two vectors.\[\overrightarrow{BA}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-4\end{pmatrix}\qquad \overrightarrow{BC}=\begin{pmatrix}9\\1\end{pmatrix}\]

Find \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) as a column vector.

title: Homework-time histogram
body:
The table gives information about the time taken by each student in Year 11 to complete a homework task.
Time taken (\(t\) minutes)Frequency
\(10<t\leq25\)15
\(25<t\leq30\)18
\(30<t\leq50\)32
\(50<t\leq60\)4
parts: On the grid, draw a histogram for this information.

One of these students who took 50 minutes or less and more than 25 minutes to complete this homework task is chosen at random.

Find an estimate for the probability that this student took 45 minutes or less to complete this homework task.
markscheme: B3 for a fully correct histogram.
If not B3 then B2 for 3 correct densities or bars; if not B2 then B1 for 2.
SCB2 for all 4 bars of correct width with heights in the correct ratio; SCB1 for 3 such bars.
For (b), method to estimate the count from 30–45, 45–50, or 25–45 minutes; ft incorrect histogram.
figureNote: A blank histogram grid with Time taken (t minutes) on the horizontal axis from 10 to 60 in steps of 10, and Frequency density on the vertical axis from 0 to 4 in steps of 1.
answerFigureNote: The completed histogram has bars: 10–25 height 1; 25–30 height 3.6; 30–50 height 1.6; 50–60 height 0.4.

title: Volume of a similar statue
body:
A statue and a model of the statue are mathematically similar. The statue has a total surface area of 3600 cm².
The model has a total surface area of 625 cm². The volume of the model is 750 cm³. Work out the volume of the statue.
markscheme: A correct length scale factor or ratio, or a correct equation involving the statue volume.
dep on M1; a correct method to work out the statue volume.

title: Proof with consecutive even numbers
body: Prove algebraically that, for any three consecutive even numbers, the sum of the squares of the smallest even number and the largest even number is 8 more than twice the square of the middle even number.
markscheme: Form the two required square expressions.
Three consecutive even numbers in algebraic form; any letter may be used.
Sum of the squares of largest and smallest and twice the square of the middle; no need to expand for this mark.
A1 dep on M2. Working required. SCB1/SCB2 available for the stated \(p,p+2,p+4\) special cases.

title: Completing a three-set Venn diagram
body:
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are three sets. \(n(A\cap B\cap C)=5\) \(n(A\cap B\cap C\prime)=2\) \(n(A\cap C)=5\) \(n(A)=17\) \(n([A\cup B\cup C]')=3\)
\(n(A'\cap B\cap C')=6\) \(n(B\cap C)=7\) \(n(C)=14\) Complete the Venn diagram to show the number of elements in each region.
markscheme: A only 10; B only 6; C only 7.
Outside all sets 3, with every region correct.
If not B4, award B3 for 6 or 7 sections, B2 for 4 or 5, B1 for 2 or 3.
Allow the zero region to be blank if every other region contains a number.
figureNote: A rectangular universal set labelled E containing three overlapping circles: A on the left, B on the right and C below them. Each of the eight regions contains a dotted blank.
answerFigureNote: The completed Venn diagram has A only 10, B only 6, C only 7, A ∩ B only 2, A ∩ C only 0, B ∩ C only 2, A ∩ B ∩ C equal to 5, and outside all three sets 3.

title: Estimating a curve gradient
body:
The diagram shows the graph of \(y=f(x)\).

The point \(P\) has \(x\)-coordinate −2.

Use the graph to find an estimate for the gradient of the curve at \(P\).
markscheme: Use rise over run from two points on the tangent.
Approximately 0.5, with answers 0.2–0.8 accepted from a valid tangent.
dep on B1; method to find gradient using difference in \(y\)-values over difference in \(x\)-values, or an answer from −0.8 to −0.2.
Answer depends on tangent at P; accept 0.2–0.8 from correct figures for their tangent.
figureNote: A smooth cubic curve y = f(x) on a coordinate grid with x-axis from −8 to 8 in steps of 2 and y-axis from −4 to 6 in steps of 2. The curve has a local maximum near (−1.6, 2.6), passes through the marked point P at (−2, approximately 2.5), has a local minimum near (4.2, −3.6), and then rises steeply. The origin is labelled O.
answerFigureNote: The same curve with a tangent drawn at P. A suitable rise-over-run triangle on the tangent gives a gradient in the accepted range 0.2 to 0.8, approximately 0.5.

title: Nonlinear simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[2y^2+x^2=-6x+42\]\[2x+y=-3\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Substitute \(y=-3-2x\), or the corresponding expression for \(x\), to obtain an equation in one variable.
dep ft; multiply out and collect a three-term quadratic with at least 2 non-zero coefficients correct.
dep on M1; solve their quadratic by a correct method, allowing one sign error, or correct values for one variable.
dep on previous M1; substitute both found values into a suitable equation, using 2 dp or better, or fully correct values for the other variable.

title: Intersecting chords and sine rule
body:
\(AEC\) and \(BED\) are chords of a circle. \(AE=(x+5)\text{ cm}\qquad BE=x\text{ cm}\qquad CE=(5x-12)\text{ cm}\qquad DE=(x+12)\text{ cm}\) Angle \(DAE=48^\circ\). Work out the size of angle \(ADE\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Use sine rule in triangle ADE.
Set up a correct intersecting-chords equation.
Correct quadratic expression in the form \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), or equivalent.
dep on M1; complete method to solve their three-term quadratic, allowing one sign error.
Complete method for (angle ADE); allow use of \(x=-4\) for this mark.
figureNote: A circle with intersecting chords AEC and BED, diagram not accurately drawn. Chord AC slopes down from A through E to C; chord BD slopes up from B through E to D. AE is labelled (x + 5) cm, BE is labelled x cm, CE is labelled (5x − 12) cm and DE is labelled (x + 12) cm. Chord AD is drawn and angle DAE is labelled 48°.

title: Cone surface-area proof
body:
The diagram shows a solid cone and a solid sphere. The cone has base radius \(r\), slant height \(l\) and perpendicular height \(h\).
The sphere has radius \(r\). The base radius of the cone is equal to the radius of the sphere. Given that \(k\times\) volume of the cone = volume of the sphere show that the total surface area of the cone can be written in the form\[\pi r^2\left(\dfrac{k+\sqrt{k^2+a}}{k}\right)\] where \(a\) is a constant to be found.
markscheme: Substitute into \(\pi r^2+\pi rl\) and factor as required.
Set up an equation with the two volumes and some simplification, with at least 2 terms simplified.
Find \(h\) in terms of \(r,k\) in simplest form; may be seen later.
Rearrange and remove \(r\) from the square root; may be seen later.
Correct surface-area expression in \(r,k\), with \(\pi r^2\) removed as a factor.
figureNote: Two solids, diagram not accurately drawn. On the left is a solid cone with base radius r, slant height l and perpendicular height h, each shown by an arrowed dimension line. On the right is a solid sphere with a radius r drawn from its centre; the hidden rear half of its equator is dashed.

title: Symmetric trapezium coordinate
body:
(ABCD) is a trapezium with (AB) parallel to (DC). \(A\) is the point with coordinates \((-4,6)\).
\(B\) is the point with coordinates \((2,3)\).
\(D\) is the point with coordinates \((-1,8)\). The trapezium has one line of symmetry.
The line of symmetry intersects (CD) at the point \(E\). Work out the coordinates of the point \(E\).
markscheme: Form equations for CD and the symmetry line.
Use \(m_1m_2=-1\) to find gradient of symmetry line.
Method to find equation of (CD) or symmetry line.
Correct linear equation for one coordinate of \(E\).
Alternative using the length of (CD) is also allowed as specified in the source scheme.

title: Complex algebraic fraction
body:
Write\[\dfrac{4x^2-17x-15}{2x-1}\times\dfrac{2x^2-7x+3}{x^2-25}+(29-4x)\]

as a single fraction in its simplest form.
markscheme: Factor at least one quadratic correctly.
Factor at least two and cancel common factors.
Combine the remaining expression over denominator \(x+5\).
M2 for factorising at least 2 of the quadratics correctly; may be implied by 2 factors cancelled correctly.
If not M2 then M1 for factorising at least 1 of the 3 quadratics correctly.
Write the correct expressions over a common denominator \(x+5\), with or without brackets removed; need not be simplest and may be two fractions.

title: Football goals ratio
body:
Last season, the number of goals scored by Arjun, by Simon and by Kath for their football team were in the ratios (2:5:8).

Simon scored 12 more goals than Arjun.

Work out the number of goals scored by Kath.
markscheme: Three ratio parts represent 12, so one part is 4.
Method to find one share, work with Arjun or Simon’s ratio, set up an equation, or find total goals 60.
Complete method to find Kath’s goals.

title: Estimated total walking time
body:
The table gives information about the number of minutes that Abby spent walking each day in September.
Number of minutes (\(M\))Frequency
\(0<M\leq30\)5
\(30<M\leq60\)6
\(60<M\leq90\)8
\(90<M\leq120\)9
\(120<M\leq150\)2
Work out an estimate for the total number of minutes that Abby spent walking in September.
markscheme: Form and add the five products.
M2 for midpoint products, allowing one error or omission, with attempt to add.
If not M2 then M1 for products using a consistent value within each range and attempt to add, or at least 4 correct midpoint products without addition.
An answer of 72 gains M2 but loses A1.
Lower-bound products are 0, 180, 480, 810, 240; upper-bound products are 150, 360, 720, 1080, 300.

title: Percentage profit on notebooks
body:
Nanette buys 60 notebooks for a total cost of 780 dirhams. Nanette sells 70% of the notebooks for 22 dirhams each.
She sells the remaining notebooks for 19 dirhams each. Work out Nanette’s percentage profit.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Income or profit for one selling-price group.
Income or profit for both selling-price groups; 1266 or 486 implies M2.
Complete method to find percentage profit.
Correct answer scores full marks unless from obvious incorrect working.

title: Coordinate transformations
parts:
The diagram shows a sketch of triangle \(A\) and triangle \(B\) on a coordinate grid.

Given that triangle \(A\) has been translated to give triangle \(B\), work out the value of \(d\), the value of \(e\) and the value of \(f\).

The diagram shows shape \(P\) and shape \(Q\) drawn on a grid.

Describe fully the single transformation that maps shape \(P\) onto shape \(Q\).

On the grid above, rotate shape \(P\) 90° clockwise about \((3,5)\).
Label your shape \(R\).
markscheme: The translation vector is 13 right and 10 up.
Use it for at least two missing coordinates.
For (a), a correct translation vector or one correct missing-coordinate calculation.
For (b), “enlargement” with no other transformation language; scale factor 3 with no vector/angle/line language; centre \((0,2)\).
For (c), B2 for correct shape; if not B2 then B1 for correct orientation in wrong position, 3 of 4 vertices, or a 90° anticlockwise rotation about \((3,5)\).
figureNote: A coordinate sketch, diagram not accurately drawn, showing congruent triangles A and B. Triangle A has vertices (−11,−5), (−7,2) and (f,−3). The corresponding vertices of triangle B are (2,d), (6,12) and (9,e). The axes are labelled x and y and the origin O.
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE, parts (b) and (c). Grid with both axes from 0 to 12, ruled and numbered every 1, origin labelled O. Shape P is the quadrilateral drawn in the order (2,5), (3,3), (3,2), (2,3) - two verticals joined by two slants, no horizontal edge. Shape Q is its enlargement, drawn in the order (6,11), (9,5), (9,2), (6,5).
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE for part (c). Add shape R, the 90 degree clockwise rotation of P about (3,5), drawn in the order (3,6), (1,5), (0,5), (1,6), labelled R.

\(AE=7.2\text{ cm}\qquad BE=5.4\text{ cm}\qquad BC=6\text{ cm}\qquad\) angle \(AEB=90^\circ\).

Work out the perimeter of the shaded shape.
markscheme: Complete Pythagoras method to find \(AB=DC\); a 9 marked on (DC) implies M2.
Complete method to find the perimeter.
figureNote: A rectangle ABCD, diagram not accurately drawn, with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. Point E is inside the rectangle, about two thirds of the way across from A towards B and about two thirds of the way down from AB towards DC, so the removed triangle leaves a deep V-shaped notch in the top edge. body:

Find the inequalities that define \(R\).

parts:

body:
Solve the simultaneous equations\[2x+9y=14.5\]\[7x+3y=8\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Use the first solution to find the second.
Correct elimination or substitution, allowing one arithmetic error.

body:

markscheme: 15 and 25 clearly identified in the list or stated; condone 19 also indicated.

body: The curve \(C\) has equation \(y=4x^3+x^2-20x\).
parts:
Find the \(x\)-coordinates of the points on \(C\) where the gradient is 4.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: dep on M1, rearrange their derivative to a quadratic.
Solve their three-term quadratic by a correct method; allow factorisation giving 2 of 3 terms or one sign error in formula/completing square.
Both values required, dep on M2; isw an attempt to find \(y\)-coordinates. Working required.

For (c), reading 38 from vertical axis or (50-) their reading at height 35.

Find an equation of the straight line that passes through the points \(A\) and \(B\).
markscheme: Use either point to find the intercept.
Use either point to find intercept, ft their gradient.

markscheme: If not B3 then B2 for \(2(5g\pm3)(5g\pm3)\) oe.
If not B2 then B1 for \(2(25g^2-9)\), a partly doubled factorisation, or the unfactored-out difference of squares.

body:

Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Form the equal shaded/unshaded area equation.
Complete method for larger-circle radius or pentagon-triangle height.
Complete method for larger-circle or sector area.

Correct equal-area equation for smaller radius.
Correct rearrangement with smaller-circle area as subject or better.

title: Surface area of a square frustum
body:
A frustum is made by removing a small square-based pyramid from a similar large square-based pyramid as shown in the diagram. The height of the small pyramid is 15 cm.
The height of the large pyramid is 45 cm.
The square base of the large pyramid has side length 39 cm. Work out the total surface area of the frustum.
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

Add four trapezoidal faces and both square ends.
\(5090\text{ cm}^2\) to the nearest whole number.
Sum areas of the two square ends; may be embedded.
Find perpendicular slant height of either pyramid.
M2 for direct correct frustum slant-height method.
Find frustum slant height, or one/all triangular face areas for either pyramid.
figureNote: A square-based frustum, diagram not accurately drawn, shown as the lower part of a large square-based pyramid with the removed small pyramid indicated by dotted edges above it. The small pyramid height is marked 15 cm, the full large pyramid height 45 cm, and two adjacent sides of the large square base are each labelled 39 cm. Hidden frustum edges are dashed.

title: Number of sides from connected polygons
body:
\(BCDEFG\) is a hexagon.
\(AB\), \(BC\) and \(CD\) are three sides of a regular \(n\)-sided polygon. Calculate the value of \(n\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: M1 for a method to find the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon, then M1 for a method to find its missing angle.

title: Recurring decimal as a fraction
body: Use algebra to show that \(0.1\dot7\dot6=\dfrac{35}{198}\).
markscheme: Let x be the decimal and form two shifted recurring decimals, such as \(100x=17.6767\ldots\) and \(x=0.1767\ldots\).

Note: M1 for two recurring decimals which, when subtracted, give a whole number or terminating decimal, with intention to subtract. If recurring dots are not shown in both numbers, show at least one number to at least 5 significant figures.
Note: A1 for a correct algebraic conclusion of \(\dfrac{35}{198}\). Working required.

title: Inverse-square proportion
parts: Find a formula for \(F\) in terms of \(r\).
Work out the value of \(F\) when \(r=48\).
markscheme: Note: For (a), M1 for \(F=\dfrac{k}{r^2}\) oe and M1 for substituting \(F=36,r=4\) to find \(k\).

title: Greatest possible fence-cost difference
body:
Diego builds a fence using fence panels. The total length of the fence is 50 metres, correct to the nearest 5 metres.
The length of each fence panel is 1.3 metres, correct to the nearest 10 cm. The cost of each fence panel is £8.65. Diego may only buy complete fence panels.
Diego only pays for the number of panels he needs to build the fence. Work out the greatest difference in the possible amounts that Diego could pay to build the fence.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: Use bounds: total fence length is at least 47.5 m and less than 52.5 m; panel length is at least 1.25 m and less than 1.35 m.
Note: M1 for each correct extreme whole-panel count, using complete panels only. Final A1 cao for the greatest cost difference. Working required.

title: Comparing routes using vectors
body:
The diagram shows a triangle \(ABC\) where \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) represent the positions of three towns. Pru travels directly from \(A\) to \(B\) and then directly from \(B\) to \(C\). Yang travels directly from \(A\) to \(C\).
Given that the values for \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BC}\) are in kilometres, work out how much further Pru travels than Yang travels. Give your answer in km, correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: M1 for correctly adding the vectors to obtain \(\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}\).
Note: M1 dep on the previous M1 for a method to find the magnitude of \(AC\); M1 indep for the magnitude of either \(AB\) or \(BC\); final route method is dep on that M1.
figureNote: A triangle of town positions \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\), diagram not accurately drawn. The directed sides are labelled \(\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}7\\-2\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BC}=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\5\end{pmatrix}\).

title: Function and curve transformations
parts:
(i) Write down the coordinates of the maximum point on the curve with equation \(y=2f(x)\). (ii) Write down the coordinates of the maximum point on the curve with equation \(y=f(x)-7\).
(iii) Write down the coordinates of the maximum point on the curve with equation \(y=f(-x)\).

Curve \(L\) has equation \(y=x^2+7x+20\). Curve \(L\) is transformed to curve \(S\) under the translation \(\begin{pmatrix}2\\0\end{pmatrix}\). Find an equation for \(S\).
Give your answer in the form \(y=ax^2+bx+c\).
markscheme: Note: For (a), each ordered pair is B1 cao.

Curve \(C\) has equation \(y=f(x)\).

title: Percentage above an age from a histogram
body:
Some people attend a concert.
The histogram shows information about the ages of these people. Work out an estimate for the percentage of these people who are aged more than 55 years.
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Find the total area across all bars.
Form the required area as a fraction of total area and multiply by 100.
Note: M1 for a method to find the area of the 55-75 bar and M1 for a method to find the total area, using all bars and allowing one error or omission.
Note: M1 for a fraction or percentage aged 55+ using all correct values only. A1 awrt 16.7.

Age (years) runs 20 to 80, labelled every 10; the Frequency density axis carries no number but 0 and nothing pins it - the answer is a percentage of the total area. The class boundaries are 20, 25, 30, 40, 50 and 75, and the bars are 16, 50, 33, 19 and 9 small squares tall, which give the mark scheme's 16.7 per cent above 55 years.

title: Simplifying a compound rational expression
body:
Simplify \(\left(x^2-4\right)\div\left(\dfrac{4x^2-7x-2}{x}\right)-2x\).

Give your answer in the form \(\dfrac{ax^2}{bx+c}\) where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are integers.
markscheme: Factor both, invert the divisor and cancel.
Note: M1 for complete factorisation of \(x^2-4\) or \(4x^2-7x-2\); each factor must be of the form \(ax\pm b\), where \(a,b\) are integers.

Note: M1 for complete factorisation of both expressions, inversion and intention to multiply; next M1 for a correct single fraction following correct cancellation, or two correct fractions with a common denominator.
Note: A1 oe but the answer must have the requested form with integer \(a,b,c\).

title: Solving an exponential index equation
body:
Given that \(2^n=2^{x^2}\times16^x\times8\) and \(x>0\), find an expression for \(x\) in terms of \(n\).

State any restrictions on \(n\).
markscheme: Complete the square or solve the quadratic.
Note: M1 for writing \(16^x\) and 8 as powers of 2, or all terms as powers of 4, 8 or 16.
Note: M1 for a correct first step in completing the square or using the quadratic formula, ft their three-term quadratic.
Note: The square root must be positive. Accept \(x=\sqrt{n+1}-2\) oe and \(n>3\).

title: Largest angle from algebraic triangle data
body:
Here is a triangle \(ABC\). The area of the triangle is \((x^2+x-3.75)\text{ cm}^2\). Find the size of the largest angle in triangle \(ABC\).
Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.
markscheme: Use the cosine rule to find \(BC^2=6^2+8^2-2(6)(8)\cos30^\circ\).
Use a sine or cosine rule for angle B.
Rearrange and evaluate the obtuse solution.
Note: M1 for equating the area of the triangle to the given area; A1 for \(x=3.5\).

Note: M1 ft dep on the previous M1 for a correct method to find angle \(ABC\) or angle \(BCA\). Final A1 cao for 103 degrees.
figureNote: Triangle \(ABC\), diagram not accurately drawn, with \(AB=(2x-1)\text{ cm}\), \(AC=(2x+1)\text{ cm}\), and included angle \(BAC=30^\circ\).

title: Showing a mixed-number division
body:
Show that \(4\dfrac{2}{3}\div1\dfrac{1}{5}=3\dfrac{8}{9}\).

You must write down all the stages in your working.
markscheme: Write the mixed numbers as \(\dfrac{14}3\) and \(\dfrac65\).
Invert the second fraction and multiply: \(\dfrac{14}3\times5/6\).
Note: M1 for both mixed numbers expressed as correct improper fractions. No need for a division or multiplication sign; equivalent fractions are allowed.
Note: M1 for inverting the second fraction and showing intention to multiply, or both fractions expressed with the same denominator and intention to divide.
Note: A1 dep on M2 for concluding \(3\dfrac89\) from correct working. Working required.

title: Spinner expected frequency
body:
A biased spinner can land on green or on yellow or on brown or on pink. The table gives the probabilities that, when the spinner is spun, it will land on green or on yellow or on brown.
Colourgreenyellowbrownpink

Note: M1 for a complete method, or an answer of \(\dfrac{540}{10}\). A1 cao for 54.

body:

Find the size of the largest angle inside the trapezium.

title: Numbers of two coin types
body:
Nancy has some coins with a total value of 85 pence.
She has only 2 pence coins and 5 pence coins.
The ratio number of 2 pence coins : number of 5 pence coins = 1 : 3 Nancy has more 5 pence coins than 2 pence coins. How many more? You must show all your working.
markscheme: One ratio group is worth \(1(2)+3(5)=17\) pence.
So there are 5 two-pence coins and 15 five-pence coins.
Note: M1 for 2 and 15 oe, 17, or a correct equation in one unknown for either coin count or the total count.
Note: M1 assumes the previous M1 and is for finding a coin count, the total count, or the values of the two coin groups.
Note: M1 for correct numbers 5 and 15 or a subtraction to find the difference. SCB1 if no other marks are awarded for 21.25 in working or on the answer line.

title: Reflex angle between radii
body:

title: Compound growth of a painting
body:
Charlotte buys a painting for $680.
The value of the painting increases by 4% each year. Work out the value of the painting at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest $.
markscheme: Note: M1 for finding 4% or 104% of 680; M2 for \(680\times1.04^3\) or \(680\times1.04^4\).
Note: M1 for completing the repeated-percentage method. A1 accepts 764-765; a correct value followed by incorrect rounding gains full marks.

Note: SC: if no other marks are gained, award M1 for \(1.12\times680\) oe or 761.60 (or 762), \(0.12\times680\) oe or 81.6 (or 82), or \(0.96^3\times680\) oe or 601.62... (or 602). Accept \(1+0.04\) as 1.04 throughout, but not \(1+4\%\).

body:
Change a speed of 27 kilometres per hour to a speed in metres per second.

title: Comparing scores from changed means
body:
Team A and Team B take part in a quiz league. After 11 rounds, Team A has a mean score per round of 17.
After 9 rounds, Team B has a mean score per round of 18. Both teams take part in a further round.
After this round, both teams have a mean score per round of 18.5. In the further round, Team A scored more points than Team B. How many more? You must show all your working.
markscheme: Find an old or new total for each team.
Note: M1 for an expression for either existing total or either new total. M2 for both teams’ further-round scores.
Note: M1 for subtracting the two new scores. A1 cao.

Note: Use the regular nonagon central angle and the geometry of the two straight lines.

parts: Work out the probability that both dice land on yellow.

title: At least one red counter remains
body:
There are 12 counters in a bag. 3 of the counters are red.
9 of the counters are green. Ameya, Jack and Ella each take at random one counter from the bag. Work out the probability that at least one red counter is still in the bag. You must show all your working.

body:

body:

title: Missing coordinate of a kite
body:

\(B\) is the point with coordinates \(\left(-\dfrac{27}{5},4\right)\).

title: Upper bound for sphere density
body:
A solid sphere has a radius of 2.8 centimetres, correct to 1 decimal place.
The sphere has a mass of \(M\pi\) grams, where \(M=260\) correct to 2 significant figures. Work out the upper bound for the density of the sphere.
Give your answer in \(\text{g/cm}^3\) correct to 2 decimal places.

markscheme: Note: B1 for sight of a correct upper or lower bound: 255, 265, 2.85 or 2.75.
Note: M1 for calculating the lower-bound volume using \(V=\dfrac43\pi r^3\) with \(r=2.75\).
Note: M1 for the upper-bound density using the upper bound of mass and lower bound of volume; condone a missing \(\pi\) where it cancels.
Note: A1 dep on M2 and all correct bounds; allow 9.55-9.56.

title: Substitution and expansion
parts: Work out the value of \(P\) when \(m=-5\) and \(c=3\).
markscheme: Note: For (a), M1 for either 25 or -12 in the correct substitution; A1 cao.
Note: For (b), M1 for a correct expansion with at least three correct terms; A1 for the simplified quadratic.
body:
\(P=m^2-4c\).

Show clear working for each stage of the calculation.

title: Minimum cost for equal quantities
body:
Sandeep wants to buy some packets of pens and some boxes of pencils for his stationery shop. Each packet of pens contains 9 pens.
Each box of pencils contains 12 pencils. Each packet of pens costs £7.60.
Each box of pencils costs £4.80. Sandeep can only buy full packets of pens and full boxes of pencils.
He wants to buy exactly the same number of pens as pencils. Work out the minimum amount Sandeep needs to pay.
markscheme: The least common multiple of 9 and 12 is 36.
So buy 4 pen packets and 3 pencil boxes.
Note: M1 for at least two multiples of 9 and 12, or a correct common-multiple method.
Note: M1 for finding the least common number of pens and pencils, then M1 for a complete cost method. A1 cao.
Note: Accept equivalent exact money calculations; final answer cao.

title: Average train speed
body:
Anjali travels on the Eurostar train from Paris to Amsterdam. The distance the train travels between Paris and Amsterdam is 515 km.
The time taken by the train to travel between Paris and Amsterdam is 3 hours 18 minutes. Work out the average speed of the train.
Give your answer in km/h correct to the nearest whole number.
markscheme: Convert the time to 3.3 hours or 198 minutes.
Use distance divided by time with consistent units.
Note: M1 for converting 3 hours 18 minutes to hours oe, and M1 for distance divided by time.
Note: A1 for the nearest whole-number speed.

title: Arithmetic-sequence nth term
body:
Here are the first four terms of an arithmetic sequence.\[38\qquad31\qquad24\qquad17\]

Find an expression, in terms of \(n\), for the \(n\)th term of the sequence.
markscheme: Note: M1 for \(-7n+k\), where \(k\ne45\), or identifying the common difference -7. A1 for the correct nth term.

title: Average field price per hectare
body:
A field is in the shape of a trapezium.

The field is sold for a price of $49 650.

Given that 1 hectare = 10 000 \(\text{m}^2\), work out the average price of the field per hectare.
markscheme: Note: M1 for the trapezium area, M1 for converting square metres to hectares, and M1 for dividing the price by their area in hectares. A1 cao.
Note: Accept equivalent unit conversions oe; final answer cao.
figureNote: A trapezium field, diagram not accurately drawn. Its parallel sides are labelled 170 m and 330 m, and the perpendicular height is labelled 240 m.

title: Percentage pay changes
parts: Work out the percentage increase in the amount that Pierre is paid for a 5-day week.

Marie changes her job. Her salary decreases by 6%.
Her new salary is 23 030 euros. Work out Marie’s salary before she changes her job.
markscheme: The new salary is 94% of the old.
Note: For (a), M1 for working out new weekly pay, M1 for the increase, and M1 for expressing it as a percentage of 400.
Note: For (b), M1 for using 94%, M1 for division by 0.94, and A1 cao.
body:
In his previous job, Pierre was paid 400 euros in total for working a 5-day week. In his new job, Pierre is paid 14 euros per hour.
In his new job, Pierre works for 7 hours each day for a 5-day week.

title: Solving and reading inequalities
parts: Write down the three inequalities that represent the shaded region \(R\).
markscheme: Note: For (a), M1 for a correct first rearrangement and A1 for the correct inequality, including reversal when dividing by a negative.
Note: For (b), award B1 for each correct inequality. Accept equivalent rearranged forms; the inequality sign must agree with region \(R\).
figureNote: A coordinate grid with x-axis from 0 to 10 in steps of 1 and y-axis from 0 to 8 in steps of 1. Region R is the triangle bounded by the solid lines y=2, x=6 and y=x, with vertices (2,2), (6,2) and (6,6).

title: Cylinder formed from a rectangular sheet
body:
The diagram shows a rectangular sheet of metal \(ABCD\). \(BD=50\text{ cm}\) and angle \(BDC=32^\circ\). Nasser joins side \(AD\) to side \(BC\) to form a cylinder. \(BC\) is the height of the cylinder.
\(DC\) is the circumference of the cross section of the cylinder. Work out the volume, in \(\text{cm}^3\), of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: M1 for a correct trigonometric method to find one side, M1 for the other side, M1 for converting circumference to radius, and M1 for a cylinder-volume method.
Note: Final A1 is for the correctly rounded 3 significant figure answer.
Note: ft their side lengths through the radius and volume calculations.
figureNote: Rectangle ABCD, diagram not accurately drawn, with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. Diagonal BD is labelled 50 cm and angle BDC is labelled 32 degrees.

title: Sunday distance from weekly means
body:
Gemara works as a taxi driver.
Last week, he recorded the following information about the distances he drove. For the 5 days from Monday to Friday, the mean number of kilometres he drove was 104.
For the 7 days from Monday to Sunday, the mean number of kilometres he drove was 127. On Saturday, Gemara drove 132 kilometres. Work out the number of kilometres he drove on Sunday.
markscheme: Note: M1 for \(104\times5\) or \(127\times7\), M1 for a complete subtraction including Saturday, and A1 cao.

title: Power of an algebraic quotient
body: Express \(\left(\dfrac{m^6k^{10}}{25}\right)^{\frac32}\) in the form \(\dfrac{m^ak^b}{c}\), where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are integers to be found.
markscheme: Note: Apply the exponent \(\dfrac32\) to every factor. If B2 not awarded, award B1 for at least two of \(a,b,c\) correct.

title: Matching equations to sketches
parts: Write down the letter of the graph of \(y=\dfrac{10}{x^2}\).
Write down the letter of the graph of \(y=x-3+3x^2-x^3\).
Write down the letter of the graph of \(y=-\dfrac3x\).
markscheme: Note: Each correct graph letter is B1 cao.
figureNote: Six coordinate sketches labelled Graph A to Graph F in two rows of three. Preserve the exact source curves, including the positive inverse-square graph, the negative reciprocal graph, the stated cubic, and three distractors.
body: Here are six graphs.

title: Unknown compound-interest rate
body:
Feruzi invests 80 000 Kenyan shillings (KES).
He invests the money for 3 years at \(x\)% compound interest each year. At the end of 3 years, the total interest he receives is 6151.25 KES. Work out the value of \(x\).
markscheme: Cube-root the balance ratio to get multiplier 1.025.
Note: M1 for \(80000(1+x/100)^3=86151.25\) oe, M1 for taking the cube root and rearranging, and A1 cao.

title: IQR and consistency
parts: Find the interquartile range of her scores.

Machi played the same computer game eleven times. The interquartile range for Machi’s scores was 9. Who had the more consistent scores, Akari or Machi?
Give a reason for your answer.
markscheme: Identify lower quartile 22 and upper quartile 28.
Note: For (a), M1 for ordering the numbers, M1 for identifying the correct quartiles, and A1 for their difference.
Akari, because her IQR is smaller.
Note: For (b), B1 for Akari with a correct comparison of interquartile ranges and consistency.
body:
Akari played a computer game eleven times.
Here are her scores.\[25\quad20\quad28\quad27\quad26\quad22\quad23\quad29\quad20\quad29\quad26\]

title: Three tails from three heads probability
body:
Osvaldo has a biased coin.
He spins the coin three times. The probability that the coin lands on a head three times is \(\dfrac{27}{64}\).
Work out the probability that the coin will land on a tail three times.
markscheme: Note: M1 for taking the cube root to find the head probability, M1 for the complementary tail probability and cubing, and A1 oe.

title: Rationalising a surd fraction
body:
Show that \(\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{\sqrt3-1}\) can be written in the form \(a+\sqrt a\) where \(a\) is an integer.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Expand and simplify the numerator and denominator.
Note: M1 for multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate, M1 for correct expansion and simplification, and A1 for the required form. Working required.

title: Making x the subject of a cube-root formula
body: Make \(x\) the subject of \(y=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{6+5x}{x+4}}\).
markscheme: Note: M1 for cubing both sides, M1 for clearing the denominator, M1 for collecting the \(x\)-terms, and A1 for \(x\) as subject.

title: Intersecting secants from an external point
body:
\(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) are points on a circle.

\(ABP\) and \(DCP\) are straight lines.

\(AB=16\text{ cm}\quad BP=14\text{ cm}\quad CP=12\text{ cm}\).

Work out the length of \(DC\).
markscheme: Note: M1 for using the intersecting-secants theorem \(DP\times12=30\times14\) oe.
Note: M1 for a correct solution for \(DP\), then A1 for subtracting \(CP\) to obtain \(DC\).
figureNote: A circle with two secants from external point P, diagram not accurately drawn. Along the upper secant the order is P-B-A with BP=14 cm and AB=16 cm. Along the lower secant the order is P-C-D with PC=12 cm; DC is unknown.

title: Two adults from a set intersection
body:
30 adults booked to stay in a hotel. 19 adults booked breakfast.
15 adults booked dinner.
4 adults did not book breakfast or dinner. Some adults booked breakfast and dinner. Meihui chooses at random two of the 30 adults. Work out the probability that these two adults each booked breakfast and dinner.
markscheme: Note: M1 for finding the intersection count using \((19+15+4)-30\) oe.
Note: M1A1 for a fully correct without-replacement product using that count; final A1 for the simplified probability.

title: Circle tangent and isosceles triangle
body:
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are points on a circle.

\(MN\) is the tangent to the circle at \(C\).

\(AB=CB\).

Angle \(BCN=78^\circ\).

Find the size of angle \(ABC\).
markscheme: By the alternate segment theorem, the two base angles are 78°, so use \(180-78-78\).
Note: M1 for a complete correct method, for example \(180-78-78\) oe, using the alternate segment and isosceles triangle facts. A1 cao.
figureNote: A circle through A, B and C, diagram not accurately drawn. MN is tangent at C. Chords AB, BC and AC form a triangle with AB=CB. The angle between CB and tangent CN is labelled 78 degrees.

title: Intersections of a line and quadratic curve
body:
Work out the coordinates of the points of intersection of\[y-2x=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad y^2+xy=7\]

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Substitute both x-values to find y.
Note: M1 for a correct substitution of the line into the curve, M1 for a correct resulting quadratic, and M1 for solving it.
Note: Accuracy marks require both corresponding coordinate pairs. Working required.

title: Lengths and angles in cuboids
parts:
Here is a cuboid \(ABCDEFGH\). \(AB=15\text{ cm}\quad BC=4\text{ cm}\quad CF=9\text{ cm}\). Work out the length of \(BE\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Here is a cuboid \(PQRSTUVW\). \(PR=42\text{ cm}\). The size of the angle between \(PU\) and the plane \(PQRS\) is 30 degrees. \(M\) is the midpoint of \(PR\). Work out the size of angle \(UMR\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: For (a), M1 for \(4^2+9^2+15^2\) oe and A1 for the 3 significant figure space diagonal.
Note: For (b), M1 for using the 30 degree angle to find the vertical height or space diagonal, M1 for the midpoint geometry and trigonometry, and A1 for the requested angle.
figureNote: Cuboid ABCDEFGH, diagram not accurately drawn, with AB=15 cm, BC=4 cm and vertical edge CF=9 cm.
figureNote2: Cuboid PQRSTUVW, diagram not accurately drawn. Base diagonal PR=42 cm. M is the midpoint of PR. Space diagonal PU makes a 30 degree angle with plane PQRS.

title: Term count in an arithmetic series
body:
Here are the first three terms of an arithmetic sequence.\[8p\qquad7p-3\qquad4p+2\] The sum of the first \(n\) terms of the sequence is -1914. Work out the value of \(n\).
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Equate consecutive differences to obtain p=4.
Note: M1 for equating consecutive differences to find \(p\), M1 for the common difference and first term, and M1 for a correct arithmetic-series equation.
Note: M1 for solving the resulting equation in \(n\); A1 for the valid positive integer. Working required.

title: Radii from sphere area and volume
body:
The surface area of sphere \(A\) is nine times the surface area of sphere \(B\).
The difference between the volume of sphere \(A\) and the volume of sphere \(B\) is \(117\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Find the radius of the smaller sphere.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Note: M1 for using the surface-area ratio to obtain a radius ratio of 3:1.
Note: M1 for a correct volume-difference equation, M1 for simplifying the cubic equation, and M1 for solving for the smaller radius. A1 cao.
Note: Radius must be positive; isw any subsequent negative-root discussion.

title: Midpoint on a perpendicular bisector
body:
The straight line with equation \(y-2x=7\) is the perpendicular bisector of the line \(AB\), where \(A\) is the point with coordinates \((j,7)\) and \(B\) is the point with coordinates \((6,k)\). Find the coordinates of the midpoint of the line \(AB\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Write the gradient or midpoint in terms of j and k.
Form one correct equation, such as \(2k-j=8\) or \(k-2j=19\).
Note: M1 for a correct midpoint expression and M1 for using that midpoint on the perpendicular-bisector line.
Note: M1 for a perpendicular-gradient relation, M1 for a second equation, and M1 for solving; A1 for the midpoint coordinates. Working required.

title: Parameters of a cosine graph
body:
Here is a sketch of the curve with equation \(y=a\cos(bx^\circ)+c\), where \(-90\leq x\leq450\).

Find the value of \(a\), the value of \(b\) and the value of \(c\).
markscheme: Note: Award B1 cao for each correct value of \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), obtained from amplitude, period and vertical translation.
figureNote: A coordinate graph for -90≤x≤450 with x ticks at -90, 0, 90, 180, 270, 360 and 450 and y ticks from -2 to 4. Preserve the exact printed cosine curve and its extrema.

parts: List the members of the set \(A\).
List the members of the set \(A\cap B\).
List the members of the set \((A\cup B)'\).

title: Factorisation and metal-bar counts
parts:
There are 56 metal bars in a box.
Each metal bar is gold or silver or zinc. \(y\) metal bars are gold.
\((3y+7)\) metal bars are silver.
\((2y-5)\) metal bars are zinc. Work out the number of metal bars that are zinc.
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: For (a), if B2 not awarded, award B1 for a correct common factor or correct partial factorisation.
Note: For (b), M marks are for forming and simplifying the total-count expression; accept equivalent forms oe.

title: Percentage profit on a car
body:
Joshua buys a car for $12 500. He sells the car to Nina.
Nina pays a deposit of $1500 followed by 36 monthly payments of $450. Work out Joshua’s percentage profit.
markscheme: Note: M1 for total selling price, M1 for profit, and M1 for profit as a percentage of 12 500. A1 awrt the correct percentage.
Note: ft their total income provided a complete percentage-profit method is shown; isw subsequent currency notation.

title: Spinner probability and frequency
parts:
The spinner is spun 250 times.

Work out an estimate for the number of times the spinner will land on blue.
markscheme: Note: For (a), use probabilities summing to 1; A1 cao.
Note: For (b), M1 for \(0.58\times250\) oe and A1 cao.
body:
A biased spinner has three sections each of a different colour. The table shows the probability that, when the spinner is spun once, it will land on blue or on orange or on white.
Colourblueorangewhite
Probability0.58\(2x\)\(x\)

title: Perimeter of overlapping semicircles
body:
The diagram shows a shaded shape made from three identical semicircles, \(X\), \(Y\) and \(Z\). \(ABCDE\) is a straight line. \(AC\) is the diameter of semicircle \(X\) and \(B\) is its centre.
\(BD\) is the diameter of semicircle \(Y\) and \(C\) is its centre.
\(CE\) is the diameter of semicircle \(Z\) and \(D\) is its centre. \(AC=BD=CE=20\text{ cm}\). Work out the perimeter of the shaded shape.
Give your answer correct to the nearest centimetre.
markscheme: One full circumference for diameter 20 is \(20\pi\), or one semicircle arc is \(10\pi\).
Add three semicircle arcs and two radius segments: \(30\pi+20\).
Note: M marks for identifying the required semicircular arcs and using \(\pi d/2\).
Note: ft consistent use of their radius or diameter; final A1 for nearest-centimetre rounding.
figureNote: Three identical overlapping semicircles X, Y and Z on collinear diameter endpoints A, B, C, D and E, diagram not accurately drawn. AC, BD and CE are each 20 cm. Preserve the source shaded outline.

title: Difference between original ticket prices
body:
Juan wants to buy a ticket to fly from Madrid to Berlin.

He finds two different types of ticket he can buy in a sale, ticket A and ticket B.

Ticket A is \(\dfrac16\) off its normal price and costs 140 euros in the sale.

Ticket B is 20% off its normal price and costs 136 euros in the sale.

Work out the difference between the normal prices of ticket A and ticket B.
markscheme: Ticket A retains \(\dfrac56\) of its price; ticket B retains 0.8.
Note: M1 for dividing each sale price by its remaining-price multiplier.
Note: M1 for both normal prices and M1 for their difference; A1 cao.
Note: Accept exact fractions or decimals oe; final difference cao.

title: HCF from prime powers
body:
\(A=5^3\times7^3\times11^6\) and \(B=5^6\times7^2\times11^4\). Find the highest common factor (HCF) of \(A\) and \(B\).
Give your answer as a product of powers of prime factors.
markscheme: Note: B marks require the minimum power common to both numbers for each prime. Final answer may have factors in any order.

title: Algebraic and graphical inequalities
parts:
The region \(R\), shown shaded in the diagram, is bounded by three straight lines.

Write down the three inequalities that define the region \(R\).
markscheme: Note: For (a), M1 for clearing denominators and M1 for correct collection; reverse the inequality when required.
Note: For (b), B2 for the exact endpoint and direction; if B2 not awarded, award B1 for one correct feature.
figureNote: A coordinate grid with both axes from 0 to 9 in steps of 1. Region R is the shaded triangle bounded by the solid lines y=2, x=7 and y=x, with vertices (2,2), (7,2) and (7,7).

title: Standard form and neuron ratio
parts:
The number of neurons in a human brain is \(8.5\times10^{10}\)
The number of neurons in a monkey brain is \(1.47\times10^{9}\) The number of neurons in a human brain is \(K\times\) the number of neurons in a monkey brain. Work out the value of \(K\).
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Note: A1 oe eg \(5.78\times10\) awrt 57.8 allow 58 or \(5.8\times10\) with correct working seen
Working: Working not required, so correct answer scores full marks (unless from obvious incorrect working)
extract: Transcriber's note: parts (a) and (b) were stored swapped and with numbers that are not on the paper, and part (c) had lost the monkey-brain figure and carried the wrong power. The question and mark scheme here are as printed on the November 2023 Paper 1H and its mark scheme; the stored mark scheme's own answers (0.000 587, \(8.4\times10^{7}\), \(K=57.8\)) already matched the printed question rather than the stored one.

title: Angle in a non-right triangle
body:
Here is triangle \(ABC\). \(AB=22\text{ m}\), the perpendicular distance from \(C\) to \(AB\) is \(8\text{ m}\), and angle \(BAC=40^\circ\). Work out the size of angle \(ABC\). Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Drop a perpendicular from C and use \(AD=8/\tan40^\circ\) or equivalent.
Note: M1 for a correct cosine-rule method to find \(BC\), M1 for a sine-rule or cosine-rule angle method, and A1 for correct rounding. Working required.
Note: Angle accuracy is dep on a valid non-right-angled trigonometric method.
figureNote: Triangle ABC, diagram not accurately drawn, with AB=22 m, AC=8 m and included angle BAC=40 degrees.

title: Adding algebraic fractions
body: Express \(\dfrac34+\dfrac{5-x}{6x}\) as a single fraction in its simplest terms.
markscheme: Use a common denominator such as 12x.
Note: M1 for a common denominator, M1 for a correct combined numerator, and A1 for the single simplified fraction.

title: Cubic graph and graph recognition
parts:
Complete the table of values for \(y=x^3-3x+1\).
\(x\)-2-1012
\(y\)-1
On the grid, draw the graph of \(y=x^3-3x+1\) for values of \(x\) from \(-2\) to \(2\)

Here are four graphs.

Write down the letter of the graph that could have the equation \(y=-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\)
markscheme: Plot at least four points correctly.
Note: For (b), M1 ft their table for sufficient correctly plotted points; A1 for a correct smooth cubic. For (c), B1 ft their graph.
Note: For (a), if B2 not awarded, award B1 for at least two correct missing values.

title: Bank login cumulative frequency
parts: Use the graph to find an estimate for the median time.

Work out the percentage of these adults that took longer than 50 seconds to log in.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Read cumulative frequency about 74–76 at 50 seconds and subtract from 80.
Divide the remaining 4–6 by 80 and multiply by 100.
Note: Median and quartile readings are ft the supplied cumulative-frequency curve; use cumulative frequencies 40, 20 and 60.
Note: Accept readings within the mark-scheme intervals and a correct subtraction for IQR.
figureNote: A cumulative-frequency graph with Time in seconds on the horizontal axis from 0 to 60 in steps of 10 and Cumulative frequency on the vertical axis from 0 to 80 in steps of 10. The smooth curve passes approximately through (3,0), (10,9), (20,29), (30,50), (40,66), (50,75) and (60,80).

title: Circle angle from radii
body:
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are points on a circle with centre \(O\).

Angle \(OAC=52^\circ\).

Find the size of angle \(ABC\).

Give a reason for each stage of your working.
markscheme: The angle at the circumference is half the central angle, so \(\angle ABC=38^\circ\).
Give the two valid circle/isosceles reasons.
Note: M1 for the isosceles radius-triangle angle, M1 for the angle at the centre, and M1 for the angle at the circumference.
Note: Reasons must identify equal radii and the angle-at-centre theorem oe.
figureNote: A circle with centre O and points A, B and C on the circumference. Radii OA and OC and chords AC, AB and BC are drawn. Angle OAC is labelled 52 degrees.

title: Changing the subject of a rational formula
body: Make \(n\) the subject of the formula \(x=\dfrac{3p-n}{3n+4}\).
markscheme: Note: M1 for clearing the denominator, M1 for collecting all \(n\)-terms on one side, and A1 for \(n\) as subject.

title: Points with a given gradient
body:
A curve has equation \(y=4x^3-8x+5\).

Find the two \(x\)-coordinates of the points on the curve where the gradient is \(\dfrac13\).

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: M1 for correct differentiation, M1 for setting the derivative equal to \(\dfrac13\), and M1 for a correct quadratic.
Note: Accuracy marks require both x-coordinates; working required.

title: Medium oranges from a histogram
body:
The histogram gives information about the weights, in grams, of some oranges in a box.

24 of these oranges weigh less than 20 grams.

Medium oranges weigh between 35 grams and 55 grams.

Work out an estimate for the number of medium oranges.
markscheme: Use the 24 below 20 g to calibrate histogram area to frequency.
Find the areas representing 35–50 g and 50–55 g.
Note: M1 for using the 24 oranges to determine the frequency-density scale.
Note: M1 for the total histogram area over 35-55 and A1 for the estimated frequency.
figureNote: A histogram on 2 mm graph paper. Weight (grams) runs 0 to 80, labelled every 10; the Frequency density axis carries no number but 0. The class boundaries are 0, 20, 30, 50, 65 and 75 with frequency densities 1.2, 3.4, 2.2, 1.8 and 0.6 - the scale set by the 24 oranges under 20 grams.

title: Village route from bearings
body:
The diagram shows the positions of three villages, \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\). The bearing of \(B\) from \(A\) is 054 degrees.
The bearing of \(C\) from \(B\) is 132 degrees. \(AB=3.6\text{ km}\) and \(BC=8.4\text{ km}\). A walker follows route \(A-B-C-A\) at 6 km/h. Work out the total time for the route, in hours and minutes.
markscheme: Note: M1 for the included angle found from the two bearings, M1 for a cosine-rule method to find \(AC\), and M1 for total distance.
Note: M1 for distance divided by 6 and A1 for correct hours-and-minutes conversion.
Note: Accept equivalent bearing-angle reasoning oe; ft their \(AC\) in the route time.
figureNote: A bearing diagram for villages A, B and C, diagram not accurately drawn, with north lines at A and B. Bearing AB is 054 degrees, bearing BC is 132 degrees, AB=3.6 km and BC=8.4 km.

title: Last term of an arithmetic series
body:
Here are the first 4 terms in an arithmetic sequence.\[3\quad7\quad11\quad15\] The last term of the sequence is \(x\).
The sum of the terms of the sequence is 7260. Find the value of \(x\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: M1 for a correct nth-term relation between \(x\) and the number of terms.
Note: M1 for the arithmetic-series sum equation, M1 for solving the resulting quadratic and A marks for the valid sequence value. Working required.

title: Mean value from two coin selections
body:
A bag contains only 10 cent coins and 20 cent coins.

Josip takes at random a coin from the bag, records its value and replaces it in the bag.

He then takes at random a second coin, records its value and replaces it.

The probability that the mean value is 10 cents is \(\dfrac{49}{121}\).

Work out the probability that the mean value is 15 cents.
markscheme: Note: M1 for taking the square root of \(\dfrac{49}{121}\) to find the 10-cent probability.
Note: M1 for the two mixed outcomes, with replacement, and A1 for their total probability.

title: Volume of a triangular prism
body:
Here is a triangular prism \(ABCDEF\). \(AD=53\text{ cm}\).
\(DF=28\text{ cm}\).
Angle \(FDE=30^\circ\). Work out the volume of the triangular prism.
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
markscheme: Note: M1 for trigonometry in the right-angled end triangle, M1 for its area, and M1 for multiplying by prism length.
Note: Final A1 is for correct nearest-whole-number rounding.
figureNote: Triangular prism ABCDEF, diagram not accurately drawn. AD=53 cm is the diagonal of the rectangular face containing the prism-length edge AF and the triangle edge FD, so the prism length AF is not given. End triangle DEF is right-angled at E, with hypotenuse DF=28 cm and angle FDE=30 degrees.

title: Distance between tangent intercepts
body:
[In this question 1 cm = 1 unit on the \(x\)-axis and 1 cm = 1 unit on the \(y\)-axis.]
\(P\) is a point on a circle with centre \((0,0)\).
The coordinates of \(P\) are \((8,-10)\). The line \(L\) is the tangent to the circle at \(P\). \(L\) crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\) and the \(y\)-axis at \(R\). Work out the length of \(RQ\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Use the distance formula for RQ.
Note: M1 for the radius gradient or perpendicular tangent gradient, M1 for the tangent equation, and M1 for each intercept.
Note: M1 for a distance-formula calculation of \(RQ\); A1 for 3 significant figures.
Note: ft their tangent intercepts in the distance calculation; final value awrt the scheme value.

title: Similar solids with exponential dimensions
body:
Solid \(A\) is similar to solid \(B\). Here is some information about solid \(A\) and solid \(B\).
solid Asolid B
Height (cm)\(3^x\)
Area (cm²)7776486
Volume (cm³)\(8^x\)\(2^{x+4}\)
Work out the height of solid \(B\).
Give your answer as a decimal.
markscheme: Area ratio is 16, so linear scale factor A:B is 4:1.
Use the volume scale factor 64 in an equation linking \(8^x\) and \(2^{x+4}\).
Rewrite in powers of 2 and solve to obtain \(x=5\).
Note: M1 for the area scale factor and M1 for the corresponding linear scale factor.
Note: M1 for the volume scale factor equation, M1 for solving the indices and A1 for the decimal height.

title: Translation and cosine parameters
parts: Write down the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\) in the translation vector \(\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}\).

The graph of \(y=p\cos(x+q)^\circ\) for \(0\leq x\leq360\) is drawn on the grid.

Given that \(p>0\) and \(0<q<360\), find the value of \(p\) and the value of \(q\).
markscheme: Note: For (a), each translation component is B1 cao.
Note: For (b), amplitude gives \(p\) and horizontal displacement gives \(q\); each is B1 cao.
figureNote: A coordinate graph for 0≤x≤360 with x ticks at 90, 180, 270 and 360 and y ticks from -4 to 4. The cosine curve starts at (0,2), crosses the x-axis at 45, has minimum (135,-3), crosses again at 225, has maximum (315,3), and ends at (360,2).
body: The curve with equation \(f(x)=5x^2+9x+2\) is transformed to the curve with equation \(g(x)=5(x+4)^2+9(x+4)+8\) by a translation.

title: Grouped telephone-call lengths
parts: Work out an estimate for the total length, in minutes, of these telephone calls.
markscheme: Note: For (a), B1 cao for the modal class.
Multiply each midpoint by its frequency and add.

Note: For (b), M2 for at least five correct midpoint-frequency products added. If not M2 then award M1 for consistent representative values in at least five intervals with intention to add. A1 for the estimated total.
body:
The table shows information about the lengths, in minutes, of 50 telephone calls.
Length of telephone call (\(m\) minutes)Frequency
\(0<m\leq5\)8
\(5<m\leq10\)2
\(10<m\leq15\)6
\(15<m\leq20\)4
