Note: M1 for method to find AC2 or AC or FB2 or FB or GC2 or GC or for a correct equation using BC2 and 18 and 7 and 9 other longer ways to find AC, FB, GC may be used but must be a complete method eg \(\angle FCA = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7}{18}\right)\) \((= 22.88...)\) and \(AC = \dfrac{7}{\tan\text{"}22.88...\text{"}}\)
Note: M1 for complete method to find BC2 other longer ways to find BC may be used but must be a complete method, leading to a trig equation in BC
figureNote: Cuboid ABCDEFGH with AB=9 cm, AF=7 cm and space diagonal FC=18 cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Function transformations
parts:
The curve with equation \(y=f(x)\) has one turning point. The coordinates of this turning point are \((-6,9)\).
Write down the coordinates of the turning point on the curve with equation \(y=f(3x)\).

The curve \(C\) with equation \(y=g(x)\) is transformed to give the curve \(S\) with equation \(y=g(x+a)+b\).

The point \((4,-5)\) on \(C\) is mapped to \((1,-16)\) on \(S\).

Write down the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).

title: Circle-line simultaneous equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations
\(x^2+y^2=41\)
\(2x+y=3\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Note: M1 substitution of \(y = \pm 2x \pm 3\) (or \(x = \dfrac{\pm y \pm 3}{2}\)) into \(x^2 + y^2 = 41\) to obtain an equation in x only (or y only)
Note: M1 dep on previous M1 for multiplying out and ft collecting terms, forming a three term quadratic in any form of ax2 + bx + c \(= 0\) where at least 2 coefficients (a or b or c) are correct

Note: M1 dep on M1 method to solve their 3 term ft quadratic using any correct method (allow one sign error and some simplification – allow as far as eg \(\dfrac{12 \pm \sqrt{144+640}}{10}\) or \(\dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36+3100}}{10}\) or if factorising allow brackets which expanded give 2 out of 3 terms correct) or correct values for x or correct values for y

Note: M1 dep on previous M1 for substituting their 2 ft found values of x or y into one of the two given equations or their rearranged equation used in the substitution or for one correct pair of values
Note: A1 oe dep on M2 for all 4 values (allow coordinates)

title: Intersecting chords algebra
body:
\(PTR\) and \(QTS\) are chords of a circle.

\(PT=(3y-5)\) cm, \(QT=(y+3)\) cm, \(RT=4x\) cm, \(ST=(x+2)\) cm.

Find an expression for \(y\) in terms of \(x\).
markscheme: Note: M1 for correct use of intersecting chords theorem to form an equation

Note: M1 for expanding the brackets or for removing the fractions and expanding the brackets, allow one error in one term we can ft 4 x ( y + 3 ) = ( x + 2 ) ( 3 y − 5 ) oe for the 2nd , 3rd and 4th method marks
Note: M1ft dep on previous M1 for correctly collecting all the y terms on one side and non-y terms on the other side
Note: M1ft dep on 2nd M mark for factorising, for y, an equation in the form a x + b = c x y + d y (may not be simplified) the factorisation must be correct
figureNote: Two chords PTR and QTS intersect at T inside a circle; PT=3y - 5, QT=y+3, RT=4x, ST=x+2. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Arithmetic series with two variables
body:
The first 3 terms of an arithmetic series are \((2x+5)\), \((3y-4)\), \((4x-2)\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are constants. The sum of the first 9 terms of the series is 216. Find the value of \(x\) and the value of \(y\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Form a correct nine-term sum equation.
Note: M1 for a correct expression or equation using the common difference, may be in terms of d for this mark we will allow an expression for −d or −2d

title: Arc length from a segment
body:
\(BAC\) is a sector of a circle, centre \(A\). \(BCD\) is a sector of a circle, centre \(C\). Angle \(BAC=40^\circ\).
Angle \(BCD=130^\circ\).
Area of shaded segment = 28 cm². Find the length of the arc \(BD\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Use cosine or half-angle geometry for chord BC.
Use 130° arc length with radius BC.
Note: M1 for a correct expression for the area of the shaded region Allow 3.14… or \(\dfrac{22}{7}\) for \(\pi\) sin 40 = 0.64…
Note: A1 Allow answers in the range 31.5 – 32.0
Note: M1 for a correct first step to find BC using their clearly identified radius eg r = …. or seen on diagram NB \(\dfrac{180-40}{2} = 70\) sin 20 = 0.34… sin 70 = 0.93… or 0.94
Note: M1 dep on previous M1 for a complete method to find BC cos 40 = 0.76… or 0.77
figureNote: Linked sectors BAC (centre A, 40 degrees) and BCD (centre C, 130 degrees), sharing chord BC. The minor segment between chord BC and arc BC of the first sector is shaded and has area 28 cm². Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Three similar vases
body:
\(R\), \(S\) and \(T\) are three similar vases. The volume of vase \(S\) is 72.8% more than the volume of vase \(R\). The height of vase \(R\) is \(h\) cm.
The height of vase \(T\) is \(6h\) cm. The surface area of vase \(S\) is \(A\) cm².
The surface area of vase \(T\) is \(kA\) cm². Work out the value of \(k\).
markscheme: Volume scale R:S is \(1:1.728\), giving length scale 1:1.2.
Square the length scale for area.

Note: M1 for method to find the scale factor between the heights of R and S or for a correct ratio for the lengths R : S or for a correct ratio for the lengths R : S : T or for a correct ratio or scale factor for the volumes S : T

Note: M1 for method to find the scale factor between the heights of S and T or for a correct ratio of the heights of S and T in the form 1 : n or for a correct method to find the ratio for the areas S : T ft their ratio of lengths or for a correct method to find the ratio for the areas R : S : T ft their ratio of lengths (maybe seen as the two separate ratios of R : S and R : T)

Note: M1 for squaring the scale factor of the heights of S and T or for a correct ratio in the form 1 : n for the areas S : T ft their ratio of areas, may be implied by their final answer or for a correct calculation using the area ratio of S : T to find the value of k
figureNote: Three similar vase outlines labelled R, S and T, increasing in size. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Complete six ordered values
body:
Rio has six cards.
He writes a number on each card so that the range of the numbers is 10, the median of the numbers is 7.5 and the mode of the numbers is 6. Rio arranges the cards so that the numbers are in order of size.
The printed cards show 6, 10 and 14, with three numbers hidden.
Complete the cards to show the three numbers that are hidden.
figureNote: A horizontal row of six cards arranged in increasing order. The third, fifth and sixth cards show 6, 10 and 14 respectively; the first, second and fourth cards are blank for the student to complete.

title: Two transformations
parts: On the grid, enlarge shape \(A\) with scale factor 3 and centre \((0,1)\).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle \(P\) onto triangle \(Q\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE, part (a). Grid 0 to 14 by 0 to 12, numbered every 2. Shape A is the shaded L-hexagon with vertices (1,1), (3,1), (3,4), (2,4), (2,2), (1,2).
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE for part (a). Add the enlargement of A, scale factor 3, centre (0,1): (3,1), (9,1), (9,10), (6,10), (6,4), (3,4).
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE, part (b). Grid 0 to 10 by 0 to 9, numbered every 1. Triangle P has vertices (2,2), (2,6), (4,2); triangle Q has vertices (6,8), (8,8), (8,4). Both shaded.

title: Subtracting mixed numbers
body: Show that \(7\dfrac13-3\dfrac47=3\dfrac{16}{21}\).
markscheme: Use common denominator 21 and subtract correctly.

title: Construct a perpendicular bisector
body:
Using ruler and compasses only, construct the perpendicular bisector of the line AB.
Show all your construction lines.
markscheme: Draw the correct perpendicular bisector with two pairs of intersecting arcs.
figureNote: Horizontal line segment AB with blank construction workspace.
answerFigureNote: Perpendicular bisector of AB with all relevant compass arcs.

title: Similar quadrilaterals
body:
The diagram shows two similar quadrilaterals, \(ABCD\) and \(EFGH\).

\(AB=5\) cm, \(BC=4\) cm, \(CD=y\) cm.

\(EF=x\) cm, \(FG=10\) cm, \(GH=24\) cm.
figureNote: Two similar quadrilaterals ABCD and EFGH with AB=5, BC=4, CD=y, EF=x, FG=10, GH=24 cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Ratio after money transfers
body:
Pau, Sam and Tia share £240 in the ratios 3 : 4 : 5. Sam and Tia each give £10 of their share to Pau.
Work out the ratios of the amounts of money that Pau, Sam and Tia now have.
Give your answer in its simplest form.

title: Bracelet appreciation
body:
Tim buys a bracelet for 4000 Swiss francs.
The value of the bracelet increases by 7% each year.
Work out the value of the bracelet at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest Swiss franc.

title: Simultaneous linear equations
body:
Solve the simultaneous equations
\(3x+5y=8\)
\(4x+y=-3.5\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Use a correct elimination or substitution method.
Find the other variable by substitution or repeated elimination.

title: Linear inequalities
parts:
The region \(R\), shown shaded in the diagram, is bounded by three straight lines.

Write down three inequalities that define the region \(R\).
figureNote: Coordinate grid with both axes from 0 to 10 in steps of 1. Region R is the shaded triangle bounded by the solid lines x = 2, y = 3 and x + y = 9, with vertices (2, 7), (2, 3) and (6, 3). All three boundary lines are drawn right across the grid.

title: Nested right triangles
body:
\(ABD\) and \(ABC\) are right-angled triangles. \(AB=16\) cm, \(BC=12\) cm, \(AD=1.5\times AC\). Find the length of \(CD\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: M1 for a correct method using triangle ABC
Note: M1 for a correct method to find AC
Note: M1 for a correct method using triangle to find \(BD^2\) or angle BAD or angle BDA or for a correct equation for side CD
Note: M1 for a correct method to find BD or CD

Working: \(BD=\sqrt{(1.5\times\text{"}20\text{"})^2-16^2}=25.3(771)\ldots\) or \(BD=\sqrt{30^2-16^2}=\sqrt{900-256}=\sqrt{644}=2\sqrt{161}=25.3(771\ldots)\) or \(BD=16\times\tan\text{"}57.7\text{"}=25.3(771\ldots)\) or \(BD=\text{"}30\text{"}\times\sin\text{"}57.7\text{"}=25.3(771\ldots)\) or \(BD=\sqrt{16^2+\text{"}30\text{"}^2-2\times16\times\text{"}30\text{"}\times\cos\text{"}57.7\text{"}}=25.3(771\ldots)\) or \(BD=30\times\cos\text{"}32.2\text{"}=25.3(771)\ldots\) or \(BD=\dfrac{16}{\tan\text{"}32.2\text{"}}=25.3(771\ldots)\) or \(BD=\dfrac{16}{\sin\text{"}32.2\text{"}}\times\sin\text{"}57.7\text{"}=25.3(771\ldots)\) or \(CD=\dfrac{\text{"}30\text{"}}{\sin\text{"}126.9\text{"}}\times\sin\text{"}20.9\text{"}\) oe
Working: Working not required, so correct answer scores full marks (unless from obvious incorrect working)
figureNote: Right triangles ABC and ABD share AB=16 cm, with BC=12 cm and AD=1.5×AC. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Unknown number of counters
body:
Khalid has a box of counters. 17 of the counters are red.
28 of the counters are blue.
The rest of the counters are orange.
Khalid takes a counter at random. The probability of orange is \(\dfrac49\).
Work out the number of orange counters in the box.
markscheme: Find total 81 or form the equivalent equation.

title: Expanding three factors
body: Expand and simplify \(3x(2x+5)(7x-4)\).
markscheme: Expand one multiplication with at most one error.
Note: M2 for 3 (out of a maximum of 4) of \(42x^3+105x^2-24x^2-60x\) (M1 for 2 correct out of a maximum of 4)
Note: M1 An expansion with only one error. Do not award this mark for 6x² + 15x + 21x² – 12x or (6x² + 15x)( 21x² – 12x)
Note: M1 ft dep on M1 allow one further error
Working: Working not required, so correct answer scores full marks (unless from obvious incorrect working)
Note: A1 cao (terms may be in any order but must be simplified) dep on M1 ISW correct factorisation eg \(3(14x^3+27x^2-20x)\) Do not ISW incorrect simplification eg \(14x^3+27x^2-20x\)
extract: Transcriber's note: the two signs inside the brackets extracted transposed; (2x+5)(7x-4) is what gives the mark scheme's 42x^3 + 81x^2 - 60x. The question paper's text was recovered from the mark scheme, which is unambiguous on this point.

title: Puzzle cumulative frequency
parts: On the grid opposite, draw a cumulative frequency graph for your table.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the median time.
Use your graph to find an estimate for the number of these people who took more than 45 minutes to complete the puzzle.
markscheme: Plot at least five correct upper-boundary points.
Read cumulative frequency at 45 and subtract from 60.
figureNote: Blank cumulative-frequency grid with Time 0 to 60 and Cumulative frequency 0 to 60, both in steps of 10.

The frequency table gives information about the times, in minutes, that 60 people took to complete a puzzle.

\(0<t\leq10\)

title: Recognising polynomial graphs
parts: Write down the letter of the graph that could have the equation \(y=5-x^2\).
Write down the letter of the graph that could have the equation \(y=2x^3\).
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE. Five labelled sketch graphs, A to E, with a bare letter over each and no table rule, laid out three then two. A is a reciprocal curve with branches in quadrants II and IV; B is a downward parabola with its maximum above the x-axis; C is an increasing cubic through the origin; D is an upward parabola with its minimum below the x-axis; E is a STRAIGHT LINE with negative gradient crossing the y-axis above the origin.
body: Here are five graphs.

title: Negative power simplification
body: Simplify fully \(\left(\dfrac{2a^3}{10a^7c^2}\right)^{-3}\).
markscheme: Apply the negative power or simplify the internal coefficient.

title: Making t the subject
body: Make \(t\) the subject of the formula \(c=\dfrac{t^2+3}{7-8t^2}\).

title: Turning points of a cubic
parts:
Find the coordinates of the turning points on the graph with equation \(y=4x^3+5x^2+2x\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Differentiate at least two terms correctly.

title: Recurring decimal proof
body: Use algebra to show that \(0.\dot7 0\dot2=\dfrac{26}{37}\).
markscheme: Form compatible shifted equations and subtract.

Note: M1 for 2 recurring decimals that when subtracted give a whole number or terminating decimal with intention to subtract. (ie give 702 or 7020 or 70200 etc) eg \(1000x =\) 702.702... and \(x =\) 0.702.... or \(10000x =\) 7027.02.… and \(10x =\) 7.02.… or \(100000x =\) 70270.20.… and \(100x =\) 70.20.… with intention to subtract x is not required to award this mark (if recurring dots not shown in both numbers then showing at least one of the numbers to at least 6sf) NB Accept bar notation for dot notation to indicate recurring decimals
Note: A1 for completion to \(\dfrac{26}{37}\) dep on M1 and must use algebra for this final mark to be awarded. No algebra used gets a maximum of 1 mark

title: Quadratic inequality
body:
Solve the inequality \(4x^2+4x-15<0\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Factorise or otherwise solve the quadratic.

title: Gardeners three-set survey
parts: Complete the Venn diagram to show this information.

One of the gardeners who grows carrots is chosen at random.

Calculate the probability that this gardener also grows potatoes.
markscheme: Place exclusive regions 10,6,14,15,12,20,14 and outside 29 correctly.
Note: B3 for all numbers in correct regions (B2 for 5, 6 or 7 correct numbers B1 for 3 or 4 correct numbers)
Note: B1 ft for their a + their b Do not ft if there are no values for a and b

Note: M1 for \(\dfrac{n}{43}\) where n < 43 or \(\dfrac{18}{m}\) where m > 18 or \(\dfrac{b+c}{p}\) ft their where p > b + c or \(\dfrac{q}{a+b+c+d}\) ft their where q < a + b + c + d Do not ft if there are no values for a, b, c and d
figureNote: Blank three-set Venn diagram in universal set E, circles C, P and T.
body:
120 gardeners were asked if they grow carrots \((C)\), potatoes \((P)\) or tomatoes \((T)\).
43 grow carrots; 12 grow all three; 18 grow carrots and potatoes; 27 grow carrots and tomatoes; 32 grow potatoes and tomatoes; 29 grow none. The number who grow only potatoes equals the number who grow only tomatoes.
answerFigureNote: Completed Venn regions from the printed gardener data.

title: Cuboid surface-area identity
body:
The diagram shows a cuboid measuring \(3x\) cm by \(2x\) cm by \(y\) cm.
The volume is 1014 cm³ and the total surface area is \(A\) cm².
Show that \(A=12x^2+\dfrac{1690}{x}\). You must show all the stages of your working.
figureNote: Cuboid dimensions 3x cm, 2x cm and y cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Bounds for a shaded area
body:
The diagram shows a square inside rectangle \(ABCD\).
The shaded area is \(X\) cm².
\(AB=11.5\) cm correct to the nearest 0.5 cm; \(BC=9.2\) cm correct to 2 significant figures; side of square = 4.1 cm correct to 2 significant figures.
By considering bounds, work out \(X\) to a suitable degree of accuracy.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Identify at least one correct bound.
figureNote: Rectangle ABCD containing a square; the region of the rectangle outside the square is shaded. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Compound algebraic fraction constant
body:
\(\dfrac{4x^2-4x-120}{5x^2-180}\div\dfrac{x^2+5x}{10x^2+60x}=p\), where \(p\) is an integer.
Find the value of \(p\). Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Factorise two or three quadratics fully.
Invert the second fraction and cancel.

Note: M1 for factorising 2 or 3 of the quadratics fully – could be implied by 2 factors cancelled correctly NB factors must be in the form (ax + b) NB Substitution of values of x into the given equation is not an acceptable algebraic method

title: Square-pyramid edge ratio
body:
The diagram shows a square-based pyramid \(ABCDE\). \(EA=EB=EC=ED\). \(M\) is the centre of the horizontal square base \(ABCD\).
\(Q\) is the midpoint of \(AB\).
Angle \(EQM=80^\circ\). \(EA:AB=n:1\). Find \(n\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Use a consistent base side to find EQ or EM.
Use a second right-triangle relationship for EA².
figureNote: Square-based pyramid ABCDE with apex E, centre M of base ABCD and Q midpoint of AB. EA=EB=EC=ED and angle EQM=80 degrees. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Complete square and sketch
parts: Write \(28+24x-6x^2\) in the form \(a-b(x-c)^2\), where \(a,b,c\) are integers.

On the axes, sketch \(y=28+24x-6x^2\).
Show clearly the coordinates of the turning point and the point of intersection with the \(y\)-axis.
figureNote: Blank x-y axes for a quadratic sketch.
answerFigureNote: Downward parabola y=28+24x−6x² with turning point (2,52) and y-intercept (0,28) labelled.

title: Volumes of similar solids
body:
A and B are two similar solids. The height of solid A is 31 cm.
The height of solid B is 18.6 cm.
Given that volume of A − volume of B = 735 cm³, find the volume of solid A.
markscheme: Set volume ratio \(125:27\) and a difference equation.

title: Factorisation and inequality
markscheme: Remove the fraction correctly, eg \(5-2x=18x-24\), or separate the fractions on the left-hand side.
Rearrange their four-term equation, eg \(29=20x\) oe.

title: Prime factor decomposition
body:
Write 1400 as a product of powers of its prime factors.
Show your working clearly.
markscheme: Find at least two prime factors through valid stages.

Note: M1 for finding 2 prime factors after at least 2 stages of prime factorisation with 0 incorrect stages or for finding 2 prime factors after at least 3 stages of prime factorisation with no more than 1 incorrect stage Each stage gives 2 factors – may be in a factor tree or a table or listed (see LHS for examples of the amount of work needed for the award of this mark) but we want to see 2 prime factors. Example of finding 2 prime factors after at least 3 stages with 1 incorrect stage: 1400 = 10 × 14 = 2 × 5 × 2 × 7
Note: M1 dep on M1 for factors 2, 2, 2, 5, 5, 7 identified with no others in any form, eg listed, multiplied, added Ignore 1s May be seen in a fully correct factor tree or ladder
Note: A1 dep on M2 May be in any order and allow \(2^3\times5^2\times7\)

title: Simultaneous equations
body:
Solve \(3x+2y=10\) and \(3x-4y=16\).
Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Use a correct elimination or substitution method.
Substitute to find the second variable.

Note: M1 a correct method to eliminate x or y: coefficients of x or y are the same and the correct operation to eliminate is selected; if operator not written, the correct operation can be implied by 2 out of 3 terms correct Allow one arithmetic error if multiplying to equate coefficients or for a correct substitution of one variable into the other equation NB: the mark is for the method and not for the result of the method. However, if the correct result of this method is seen, the mark can be awarded
Note: M1 dep on M1 a correct substitution to find the value of the second variable using their value or for starting again with elimination or substitution (as above)

title: Tiling percentage profit
body:
Joshua is going to cover a floor with tiles for a customer.
The area of the floor is 45 m².
Joshua buys one box of tiles for each 1.5 m² of floor area. Each box costs £64. He also buys 5 bags of tile adhesive at £12 each. Joshua charges the customer £3000. Work out his percentage profit.
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
markscheme: Find 30 boxes or an equivalent tile-cost rate.
Total cost is £1980 or profit is £1020.
Divide profit by cost and multiply by 100.
Note: M1 for a method to find the number of boxes needed or the cost of adhesive or cost of tiles per m2
Note: M1 for a method to find the cost of the boxes of tiles
Note: M1 for a method to find the total cost or the profit
Note: M1 for a method to find the percentage profit or be one step away
Note: A1 awrt 51.5 SCB3 for answer 56.3 or 56.25 (from use of 1920 instead of 1980 as total cost)

title: Two shape transformations
parts: On the grid, reflect shape \(A\) in the line \(y=x\).
On the grid, enlarge shape \(B\) by scale factor 2 with centre \((1,1)\).
markscheme: Note: B2 for the correct shape in the correct position. B1 for the correct orientation of the shape but the wrong position, for 3 out of 4 vertices correct, or for \(y=x\) drawn.
Note: B2 for the correct shape in the correct position. B1 for the correct size and orientation of the shape but the wrong position, or for 3 out of 4 vertices correct.
figureNote: QUESTION-SIDE, part (a). Grid with x and y both from −3 to 10, ruled and numbered every 1, origin labelled O. Shape A is the shaded trapezium (5,2), (6,3), (7,3), (8,2).
answerFigureNote: ANSWER-SIDE for part (a). Add the reflection of A in y = x as an outline: (2,5), (3,6), (3,7), (2,8).
figureNote2: QUESTION-SIDE, part (b). The same grid. Shape B is the shaded quadrilateral (3,2), (3,4), (4,4), (5,2).
answerFigureNote2: ANSWER-SIDE for part (b). Add the enlargement of B, scale factor 2, centre (1,1), as an outline: (5,3), (5,7), (7,7), (9,3).

title: Index laws
markscheme: Note: M1 for one correct application of an index rule (must be seen in powers of 5) this could be after an initial mistake – working will need to be clearly seen or for forming a correct equation in the indices alone or for a complete method for the value of k
Note: B2 for a correct answer (B1 for answer of the form \(kd^me^n\) where at least two of \(k=8\), \(m=12\) and \(n=15\) are correct)
extract: Transcriber's note: part (c) is \((2d^4e^5)^3\) on the paper — the minus sign in an earlier transcription was spurious, and the mark scheme's \(8d^{12}e^{15}\) is correct. Checked against the printed question paper and mark scheme.

title: Volume of a silver coin
body:
The mass of a silver coin is 48.3 g.
The density of silver is 10.5 g/cm³.
Work out the volume of the silver coin.
markscheme: Note: M1 oe for substituting 10.5 and 48.3 correctly into a correct formula for density; may use any letter for the volume

title: Mean of remaining numbers
body:
The mean of 7 numbers is 60.

The mean of 3 of the numbers is 46.

Work out the mean of the other 4 numbers.
markscheme: Note: M1 may be embedded within an equation
Note: M1 for a method to find the sum of the 4 numbers Allow this mark if they do further incorrect work using 282

title: Reverse sale percentage
body:
In a sale, normal prices are reduced by 15%. The sale price of a dishwasher is 612 Swiss francs.
Work out the normal price of the dishwasher.
markscheme: Note: M1 may be seen embedded Do not allow (1 – 15%) unless processed correctly

title: Equation of a parallel line
body:
A straight line \(L\) is parallel to \(y=2-5x\).
\(L\) passes through \((0,6)\). Find an equation of \(L\).
markscheme: Note: M1 for the equation of any line with gradient −5 other than y = 2 – 5x or for the equation of any line passing through the point (0, 6) or the correct line missing ‘y =’ or with the wrong subject
Note: A1 oe equation eg y = 6 – 5x or y – 6 = −5(x – 0) or y + 5x = 6

title: Area from linked right triangles
body:
The diagram shows triangles \(ADE\) and \(CDB\).
\(ABD\) is a straight line. \(AE=28\) cm, \(ED=45\) cm, \(AB=21\) cm, \(CD=35\) cm.
Angles \(AED\) and \(CBD\) are 90°.
Work out the area of triangle \(CDB\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Use Pythagoras or trigonometry in triangle ADE.
Note: M1 for a correct method to find AD² or angle EDA or angle EAD
Note: M1 for a correct method to find AD
Note: M1 for correct method to find BC or angle BDC or angle BCD
Note: M1 for a correct method to find the area of triangle CDB
figureNote: Two right triangles ADE and CDB with A-B-D collinear; AE=28, ED=45, AB=21, CD=35 cm and right angles AED and CBD. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Changing car depreciation
body:
Osman buys a car for $16 000.
The car depreciates at 12% each year for the first 2 years.
In the third year it depreciates by \(x\)%.
At the end of 3 years its value is $11 461.12. Work out \(x\).
markscheme: Find the third-year multiplier 0.925 or depreciation 0.075.

Note: M1 for a method to find the value of the car after two years or a method to find the overall percentage multiplier after two years and the overall percentage multiplier for the three years May be seen embedded, eg in an equation Do not allow (1 – 12%) unless processed correctly

Note: M1 for a complete method to find the value of the decimal equivalent of x% or for a complete method to find the percentage multiplier for the third year May be seen embedded, eg within a correct equation rearranged to one of these equivalent forms

title: Factorising and expanding
parts: Show that \(4x(x+3)(2x-5)\) can be written as \(ax^3+bx^2+cx\), where \(a,b,c\) are integers.
markscheme: Expand one pair of factors correctly.
Obtain the four correct product terms.
Note: M2 for 3 terms (out of a maximum of 4 terms) from: \(8x^3-20x^2+24x^2-60x\) If not M2, then M1 for 2 correct out of a maximum of 4

title: Beads from bags and box
parts: Use this information to complete the probability tree diagram.
Work out the probability that Sara takes two red beads.

Sara replaces the beads. A box contains only red and green beads, with \(P(\text{green})=\dfrac2{11}\). Sara takes one bead from each bag and one from the box.
Work out the probability that she takes more red beads than green beads.
markscheme: Correct branch pairs: \(\dfrac59,\dfrac49\) and \(\dfrac7{10},\dfrac3{10}\) from either first branch.
Find one relevant outcome probability correctly.
Add RRR, RRG, RGR and GRR probabilities.

Note: Allow ft their tree diagram provided the relevant probabilities are less than 1 in each case For A1, allow decimals or percentages that round or truncate correctly to at least 2sf. ISW any attempt to convert to other form once correct probability seen
figureNote: Incomplete probability tree for Bag A then Bag B, each with red/green branches.
body:
Sara has two bags, A and B.
Bag A contains 5 red and 4 green beads.
Bag B contains 7 red and 3 green beads.
Sara takes one bead at random from each bag.
answerFigureNote: Completed tree: Bag A red/green 5/9,4/9; Bag B red/green 7/10,3/10 from either branch.

title: Circle angle with centre
body:
\(A,B,C\) lie on a circle centre \(O\). Angle \(BAO=36^\circ\), angle \(BCO=21^\circ\).
Work out angle \(ACO\).
markscheme: Use radii to establish a correct related angle or central angle.

Note: M1 for a method to find one of the angles on the scheme; for this mark, values and calculations must be linked to the correct angle by notation or by being marked on the diagram. May also be awarded for a correct method to set up and solve an equation to find one of these angles; the variable must be clearly defined where X is a point on the tangent at A where Y is a point on the tangent at C where AD is a diameter OR for any correct pair of simultaneous equations with clearly defined variables one of which must be angle ACO or any correct equation in terms of ACO only

Note: M1 for a complete method to find angle ACO OR forms a correct equation in terms of ACO only and solves to get a value (condone arithmetic errors) implies the 1st M mark (provided no incorrect working seen)
figureNote: Circle centre O with points A,B,C; chords AB,BC and radii OA,OB,OC; angles BAO=36 and BCO=21 degrees. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Rationalising a surd denominator
body:
Show that \(\dfrac4{3\sqrt5+7}\) can be written in the form \(a-\sqrt b\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers.
Show each stage of your working.
markscheme: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.
Note: M1 for multiplying the numerator and denominator by \(3\sqrt5-7\) or \(-3\sqrt5+7\) (may be implied)

Note: M1 for expanding the denominator in a correct fraction denominator may be 4 terms which all need to be correct \(\dfrac{4}{3\sqrt5+7}\times\dfrac{3\sqrt5-7}{3\sqrt5-7}=7-3\sqrt5\) scores M1M0 Implies the 1st mark
Note: A1 dep on M2 SCB1 for answer \(7-\sqrt{45}\) with no method marks awarded SCB2 for \(7-\sqrt{45}\) if you would award the 1st M1 but not the 2nd M1 (total 2 marks)

title: Rearranging a rational formula
body: Make \(k\) the subject of \(p=\dfrac{8k^2+5}{7-3k^2}\).
markscheme: Note: M1 for correctly multiplying both sides by the denominator and expanding the brackets

Note: M1ft dep on 2 terms in \(k^2\) and 2 other terms for correctly collecting their \(k^2\) terms on one side and their other terms on the other side Note: eg \(8k^2+3k^2\) does not count as 2 terms in \(k^2\)
Note: M1ft dep on previous M1 for correctly factorising for \(k^2\) or \(-k^2\) in their equation

Note: A1 oe eg \(k=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{5-7p}{-3p-8}}\) or \(k=\pm\left(\dfrac{7p-5}{8+3p}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\) or \(k=\pm\left(\dfrac{7p-5}{8+3p}\right)^{0.5}\) (condone omission of \(\pm\)) NB: to award A1 we must see \(k=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{7p-5}{8+3p}}\) in working if \(\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{7p-5}{8+3p}}\) alone is given as an answer

title: Vector section of a triangle
parts: Write down \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) in terms of \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\).
Express \(\overrightarrow{OP}\) in terms of \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\). Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: Note: M1ft for a correct expression ft their (a) where [AB] is their answer to (a) of the form \(m\mathbf a+n\mathbf b\), \(m,n\neq0\)
figureNote: Triangle OAB with P on AB, OA=4a, OB=4b and AP:PB=1:3. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.
body: \(OAB\) is a triangle. \(\overrightarrow{OA}=4\mathbf a\), \(\overrightarrow{OB}=4\mathbf b\). \(P\) lies on \(AB\) such that \(AP:PB=1:3\).

title: Domain and composite function
parts: State the value of \(x\) that cannot be included in any domain of \(g\).
Find \(gf(x)\). Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: Note: B1 oe Accept \(x=-\dfrac{1}{2}\), accept \(x\neq-\dfrac{1}{2}\) Do not allow inequalities, eg \(x>-\dfrac{1}{2}\) or \(x\le-\dfrac{1}{2}\)
Note: M1 for a correct unsimplified expression for \(gf(x)\)
Note: A1 oe eg \(\dfrac{4-3x}{7-6x}\) Correct answer seen followed by incorrect subsequent working scores M1A0
extract: Transcriber's note: the denominator of \(g(x)\) extracted as \(2x-1\); it is 2x+1, which is what makes part (a)'s excluded value -1/2 and part (b)'s answer (3x-4)/(6x-7). The question paper's text was recovered from the mark scheme, which is unambiguous on this point.

title: Book-weight histogram probability
body:
The histogram gives information about the weights, in grams, of some books.

75 books weigh less than 100 grams.

A book is chosen at random.

Find an estimate for the probability that this book weighs between 400 grams and 600 grams.
markscheme: Calibrate the scale, for example density \(\dfrac{75}{100}=0.75\).
Find frequency 200 between 400 g and 600 g.

Note: M3 for any complete method that relies only on counting squares, eg counting large squares: \(\dfrac{4+10+2}{6+18+20+10+4}\) Allow one error in number of squares in each of numerator and denominator but do not allow any omissions Must use a consistent method for the award of more than one mark
figureNote: A histogram on 2 mm graph paper. Weight (grams) runs 0 to 700, labelled every 100; the Frequency density axis carries no number but 0. The class boundaries are 0, 100, 200, 450, 500 and 700 with frequency densities 0.75, 2.25, 1, 2.5 and 0.25 - the scale set by the 75 books under 100 grams, and the totals the mark scheme's 725 and 200.

title: Quadratic inequality
body:
Solve \(2x^2-7x-15>0\).

Show clear algebraic working.
markscheme: Factorise as \((2x+3)(x-5)\) or use the quadratic formula.

Note: Allow M1A1 for the correct critical values AND evidence of another algebraic method that has led to these: eg x(2x + 3) – 5(2x + 3) and the correct critical values or 2x(x – 5) + 3(x – 5) and the correct critical values or (2x + 3)(2x – 10) and the correct critical values

title: Maximum cuboid volume
body:
The diagram shows a cuboid with dimensions \(x\) cm, \(x\) cm and \((15-4x)\) cm.
Its volume is \(V\) cm³.
Find the maximum value of \(V\).
markscheme: Set the derivative to zero and find \(x=2.5\).
Note: M1 for a correct expression for the volume \(condone missing V = …\)
Note: M1ft dep on a V of the form \(ax^3+bx^2\) where \(a,b\neq0\) for a two-term derivative with at least one term correct for their V eg \(15(2)x\) or \(30x\) or \(-3(4)x^2\) or \(-12x^2\)

Note: M1ft dep on previous M mark for equating their 2-term first derivative to 0 and solving to get a value of x (the value of x obtained must be greater than 0 and must not be where their second derivative is equal to 0) or the correct value of x
Note: M1 dep on M3 for a full and correct substitution of their value of x
Note: A1 oe eg \(\dfrac{125}{4}\) ignore any units on the answer line
figureNote: Cuboid dimensions x cm, x cm and (15 - 4x) cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Angle in a triangular prism
body:
The diagram shows triangular prism \(ABCDEF\), with horizontal rectangular base \(ABCD\).
\(M\) is the midpoint of \(AC\). \(AC=40\) cm, angle \(CAE=35^\circ\), angle \(ABF=90^\circ\).
Work out angle \(CME\).
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
markscheme: Note: M1 for a correct method to find CE
Note: M1 for a complete method to find angle CME
figureNote: Triangular prism ABCDEF with horizontal rectangular base ABCD, M midpoint of AC, AC=40 cm, angle CAE=35 degrees and angle ABF=90 degrees. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.

title: Perpendicular bisector from coordinates
body:
\(PQ\) is a straight line on a square grid, scale 1 cm per unit.
\(P=(-5,a)\), \(Q=(7,3a)\), where \(a>0\), and \(PQ=4\sqrt{10}\) cm.
Find the perpendicular bisector of \(PQ\).
Give your answer as \(y=mx+c\), where \(m,c\) are integers.
markscheme: Note: M1 for forming a correct equation in terms of a; brackets must be used correctly, but allow recovery from missing or incorrect brackets to be recovered; condone \(4\sqrt{10}^2\) in place of \((4\sqrt{10})^2\)
Note: M1 dep on M1 for a complete method to solve a correct equation for a; condone inclusion of ±
Note: M1ft for a method to find the gradient of PQ where [2] is what they believe the value of a to be; must be positive and clearly identified

Note: M1ft for a method to find the gradient of the perpendicular bisector where \(\left[\dfrac{a}{6}\right]\) or \(\left[\dfrac13\right]\) is what they believe to be the gradient of PQ; must be clearly identified

Note: M1ft for a method to find the x coordinate and y coordinate of the midpoint of PQ; condone if the coordinates are the wrong way around where [2] is what they believe the value of a to be; must be positive and clearly identified
Note: A1 oe correct equation in required form eg y = 7 – 3x

title: Parameters of a sine graph
body:
The graph of \(y=a\sin(x+b)^\circ+c\), for \(0\leq x\leq360\), is drawn on the grid.
Find suitable values for \(a,b,c\).
markscheme: Note: B1 for a = 3 or a = –3 B1 for a > 0 and b = 45 or for a < 0 and b = 225 if no answer for a is seen allow this mark for b = 45 B1 for c = 1 Allow correct alternative angles for the value of b, eg 45 or –315, 225 or –135
figureNote: Coordinate grid with x-axis from 0 to 360 in steps of 90 and y-axis from -4 to 5 in steps of 1, showing the printed sinusoidal curve.

title: Surface area of a hemispherical bowl
body:
The diagram shows a solid hemisphere \(H\), radius \(x\) cm and volume \(6174\pi\) cm³.
A bowl is made by removing a hemisphere so the uniform thickness is 2 cm.
Work out the total surface area of the bowl.
Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
markscheme: Find the annular top area or both curved surfaces.
Combine outer curved, inner curved and annular areas.

Note: M2 for use of formula for total surface area of hemispherical shell in a complete method, eg \(3\pi([21])^2+\pi([21]-2)^2\) oe If not M2, allow M1 for this formula used with omission of \(\pi\) eg \(3([21])^2+([21]-2)^2\)
figureNote: Solid hemisphere H radius x cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.
figureNote2: Cross-section of a hemispherical bowl of uniform thickness 2 cm. Diagram NOT accurately drawn.
